Communities across the UK are being offered a share of £30m in new government funding to build their own solar panels and other clean energy projects.

Great British Energy launched the funding on Thursday 17 September as the first wave of the government’s Local Power Plan, which has up to £1bn earmarked for locally owned renewable energy projects.

Community groups and councils will be able to use the money to develop projects ranging from solar panels on local buildings to community-owned wind turbines and hydro schemes. The wider programme aims to support more than 1,000 local and community-led clean energy projects by 2030.

However, despite solar panels being among the technologies covered, it’s important to note that this isn’t a new solar panel grant that individual homeowners can apply for.

Households looking for financial help towards installing panels on their own property will instead need to explore the existing solar panel grants and funding, such as ECO4 and local authority schemes.



Get a quote for solar panels on your home

Use our comparison tool to find free quotes from leading UK solar panel installers.



What is the new £30m community energy fund?

The biggest part of the package is a new £20m Community Fund, which will provide grants to community organisations in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

The money can be used to test, develop and build community-owned clean energy assets, including solar, wind and hydro projects.

To qualify, projects must give the community a defined legal and financial interest and ensure that a defined proportion of the benefits stays within the local area.

A further £5m Partnerships Grant will help councils in England work with community energy organisations on joint projects.

Scotland will receive £1.8m through its existing Community and Renewable Energy Scheme (CARES), while Great British Energy is providing up to £2.9m for organisations offering advice to community groups in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

Applications for the new grants opened on 17 September.

Can homeowners apply for the funding?

Individual homeowners cannot apply for money from the £30m package to put solar panels on their own roof. Instead, the funding is designed to create renewable energy assets owned by community groups or local authorities.

That means the financial benefit to households is less direct than with schemes such as ECO4, which can help eligible households fund energy-efficiency improvements and, in some cases, solar panels.

The government says community projects could instead reduce energy costs for facilities such as libraries, schools and leisure centres, while income generated from electricity can be reinvested locally.

Depending on how an individual project is structured, revenue could also be used for measures such as helping households in fuel poverty or funding other community services.

Could community solar cut energy bills?

There is already some evidence of the savings public buildings could make from locally generated solar electricity.

Great British Energy has previously provided up to £16m to Mayoral Combined Authorities in England, helping install 157 rooftop solar projects on buildings including fire stations and leisure centres.

The government says those and further renewable projects could collectively generate up to £50m in energy bill savings, with the money available to be reinvested in local services.

That figure shouldn’t be confused with savings on individual household energy bills, though. How residents benefit will depend on the ownership and financial model used by each community project.

The £30m announced this week is only the first part of the government’s wider Local Power Plan. Great British Energy has committed up to £1bn over the programme, with the ambition that every UK community should have the opportunity to own a local energy project by 2030.

“Our vision is that every community should have the chance to build and own its own renewable energy,” said CEO of Great British Energy Dan McGrail. “These grants will give community organisations and local authorities the practical support they need to get clean energy projects off the ground – lowering bills, supporting jobs and putting the benefits from energy into local hands.

The government also says it will publish more details this autumn on proposals that would allow community energy groups to take ownership stakes in larger commercial renewable energy projects, enabling a share of their proceeds to remain in the areas where the energy is generated.

A Georgia school district is looking to install stop-arm cameras on school buses to dissuade drivers from illegally passing — a move that warrants a $1,000 fine in the state.

DeKalb County Schools is looking to find a vendor to add cameras to over 1,000 school buses in the district. The buses already have cameras inside, but the stop-arm cameras would show what’s happening outside, CBS Atlanta reported.

“The goal of DeKalb County School District is to ensure we’re protecting 100 percent of our students 100 percent of the time by providing safe and reliable consistent transportation to and from school each and every day,” Director of Student Transportation Bernando Brown said.

The district, which transports about 45,000 students, says it plans to get cameras with multi-angle video, license plate recognition, GPS tagging and automatic activation. Data collected with the cameras would automatically be sent to law enforcement.

“The camera will actually be mounted right on the side of our bus,” Brown said. “Directly up under our stop arm. As long as no one passes the bus, there’s nothing to worry about.”

The DeKalb County School District in Georgia hopes to install cameras on all of its school buses to try to deter drivers from passing the buses ( AFP via Getty Images )

However, cars that pass buses will be tracked by the camera the entire time, Brown said.

A survey from the Governor’s Highway Safety Association found that 46 percent of children riding the school bus have had a close call with a dangerous driver.

The data also found that 53 percent of parents believe dangerous driving continues because motorists think they won’t get caught.

Georgia officials estimate that drivers in the state illegally pass school buses over 9,000 times a day.

“It’s pretty frequent,” Brown told the outlet. “We have certain areas in DeKalb County where it’s almost every time a bus stops, you’re going to see it.”

In Georgia, the fine for passing a school bus starts at $1,000.

The district says it hopes to install the cameras no later than January.

News.content:

A 75-year-old man who portrayed Santa Claus at a Christmas-themed amusement park faces multiple felony charges following allegations that he attempted to arrange sexual encounters with children over the internet.

Clarence Russell of Paul Smiths, New York, was arrested on September 5, according to the Ticonderoga Police Department. Investigators say that the arrest stems from digital communications in which Russell believed he was coordinating meetings with minors.

Russell is charged with attempted second-degree rape involving a victim under the age of 15, as well as attempted endangering the welfare of a child, as reported by CBS 6 Albany. According to a relative, Russell was released on his own recognizance, with an arraignment in Ticonderoga Town Court set for September 23.

Public records and local media reports indicate that Russell worked as a seasonal Santa Claus at Santa’s Workshop in Wilmington, New York, for approximately ten years. The historic park has welcomed visitors since 1949. Representatives for the theme park were contacted by The Independent for comment regarding his current employment status.

A man named Eric Arthurs, who goes by the screen name “The Underagent,” documented a confrontation with Russell and the police intervention that followed on social media.

open image in gallery Clarence Russell, a 75-year-old resident of Paul Smiths, New York, who previously worked as a seasonal Santa Claus at a regional holiday attraction, faces multiple felony charges following allegations that he attempted to arrange sexual encounters with minors online ( Ticonderoga Police Department )

In videos posted to Facebook by Arthurs, Russell is shown being confronted about his alleged online activity before being taken into custody. According to Arthurs, he posed online as a mother setting up sexual encounters and described graphic messages sent by Russell.

Arthurs shared these details with police and noted that Russell drove roughly two hours from his home in Franklin County to meet the fictitious family in Ticonderoga.

Russell’s daughter, identified only as Kourtney, told The Adirondack Daily Enterprise that a “history of pedophilia and sexual crimes” had long been known to relatives, and she pointed to a 1993 conviction for sexual misconduct and abuse.

“None of this surprises me,” she said. “This has been public knowledge. This is what my family grew up knowing. This has been our truth. We’ve known him to be a creep.”

An online profile tied to Russell referenced his seasonal occupation, including a self-description depicting himself as a “jolly old elf living at the north pole with Mrs Claus surrounded by elf's and rainedeer,” CBS 6 reported.

The Wilmington park is currently closed for the summer and fall operating seasons as crews perform property upgrades.

Ticonderoga Police are continuing to investigate the matter and ask anyone with information regarding Russell to contact them at 518-585-3456.

Could a Glee reboot really be in the works?

Both the Fox show’s co-creator Ryan Murphy and star Lea Michele have spoken about the potential for a reboot in recent months, sparkling a flurry of speculation as to whether it could actually happen.

At a recent New York Fashion Week event, Michele told E! News she “loves Glee” and that it “holds such a special place in my heart,” adding, “I will follow Ryan wherever he goes.”

Now, Murphy’s longtime collaborator and Glee co-creator Ian Brennan has weighed in, speaking to The Independent at the premiere of the collaborators’ new Netflix show Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story about the potential for a reunion.

“I'll say this: I would follow both of them to a Glee reboot. And that’s all I can say,” Brennan said before adding, “Watch this space.”

open image in gallery Ian Brennan spoke to 'The Independent' at the premiere of 'Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story' ( AP )

Brennan, Murphy, and Brad Falchuk co-created the hit musical series about the trials and tribulations of high school glee club New Directions. The show aired from 2009 to 2015 on Fox, winning six Emmy Awards and four Golden Globes.

In addition to Michele, Glee starred Matthew Morrison, Jane Lynch, Chris Colfer, Dianna Agron, Kevin McHale and Amber Riley, along with late actors Cory Monteith, Mark Salling, and Naya Rivera.

The show wasn’t without its flaws, as several controversies emerged during and after filming, including accusations that Michele bullied other cast members. She issued a public apology for her actions.

Speaking about the show and its legacy, as well as the potential for a reboot, Murphy told People in July, “That show is interesting because it’s come back around. So many young people now watch it. And I’m like, ‘Maybe we should revisit that show.’

open image in gallery Lea Michele starred as Rachel Berry on ‘Glee’ ( Fox )

“My nostalgia and love for that show is enough that I’m like, ‘Well, maybe people would like to see a new incarnation of that in some capacity.’ So yeah, I love that show and I loved what it became and what it meant to so many people,” he continued.

After their initial collaboration with Falchuk on Glee, Murphy and Brennan have continued to work closely together on Scream Queens, The Politician, and most recently the Monster series.

The fourth installment of that series, Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story, was released Thursday on Netflix.

Starring Ella Beatty, Billie Lourd, Charlie Hunnam, Rebecca Hall and Vicky Krieps, the series is an adaptation of the true story of Lizzie Borden, the murder suspect who was tried and acquitted of killing her father and stepmother in the late 1800s.

News.content:

Police have confirmed that human remains found in woodland in southwest London following a wildfire are those of a Southampton mother-of-three who went missing nearly seven years ago.

The Metropolitan Police were called on the evening of 12 August after bones, thought to belong to a woman aged between 25 and 45, were found near Padstow Walk in Feltham after the area was affected by a fire.

Detectives had launched a murder investigation, but Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary have now taken over the probe after the remains were identified as those of Joanne Sheen, the Press Association has learned.

A 56-year-old man from Southampton was arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to commit murder on Thursday, and remains in police custody.

Sheen, 44, had not been seen since she travelled from Fareham, Hampshire, heading to her home city of Southampton, on 5 December 2019.

She was reported missing by her family in February 2020.

open image in gallery Police were called to the woodland area last month ( PA )

The discovery came after extensive forensic examination and DNA testing of the remains.

A Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesperson told PA that more than 4,000 lines of enquiry have been raised, more than 300 statements taken, and detailed searches carried out at more than 10 addresses and on numerous vessels.

Specialist teams have also searched waterways and woodland around Southampton.

The spokesperson added: “As part of our investigation, we have today arrested a 56-year-old man from Southampton on suspicion of conspiracy to commit murder. He remains in custody at this time as our enquiries continue.

“As our investigation enters this next stage, we are working closely with our colleagues in the Metropolitan Police to establish exactly what happened to Joanne.

“Her death is being treated as murder, and we remain committed to identifying and bringing those responsible to justice.”

Detective Chief Inspector Toby Elcock, from the major crime team, said: “This is a significant development in what has been a long and complex investigation and provides us with several new lines of enquiry, which we are exploring with our dedicated team.

“While this tragic discovery is not the outcome Joanne’s family, or any of us, had hoped for, we hope the identification of her remains can at least begin to provide some answers after many years of uncertainty.

“Throughout this investigation, Joanne’s family have shown tremendous strength and dignity in the face of unimaginable circumstances, and our thoughts remain with them at this incredibly difficult time.

open image in gallery Police tape near to the scene, where a member of the public found human remains in woodland in Feltham, southwest London ( PA )

“As our investigation progresses, we remain committed to establishing exactly what happened to Joanne and ensuring that those responsible are held accountable.

“There may still be people who have information about Joanne’s disappearance, her movements before she went missing, or how she came to be in Feltham.

“The passage of time does not lessen the importance of that information. No matter how small or insignificant it may seem, we would urge anyone who may know something to come forward.

“We understand that coming forward may feel difficult, particularly if you are worried about the consequences, but we are asking you to think about the family who are left without their loved one and who are waiting for answers. Please do the right thing. If you know something, now is the time to come forward.

“We are also pleased that Crimestoppers has agreed to reinstate its £20,000 reward offer in support of our investigation. If anyone has information but does not feel comfortable speaking directly to police, I would encourage them to contact Crimestoppers anonymously.”

A Metropolitan Police spokesman confirmed that the remains were found by a member of the public after the nearby land was affected by a recent wildfire.

The site is close to Bedfont Lakes Country Park.

A former senior budget official for Connecticut's Democratic governor is now a fugitive in Greece after fleeing the U.S. by boat and plane ahead of his sentencing for corruption, his lawyer and prosecutors told a federal judge on Thursday.

Konstantinos “Kosta” Diamantis, 70, also sent his attorney a 10-page email accusing Gov. Ned Lamont of weaponizing the justice system against him, denying wrongdoing and saying his life, reputation and family relationships were ruined by the prosecution. He could have faced more than 10 years in prison at his sentencing Thursday in federal court in Bridgeport.

Diamantis, who was also a former Democratic state representative, was convicted by a federal jury last year of extorting private contractors for thousands of dollars in bribes from 2018 to 2021, in exchange for helping the companies keep and obtain work on multimillion-dollar school construction contracts. He told reporters at the time that he was afraid to go to prison.

The prospects of returning Diamantis — who holds both American and Greek citizenship — to the U.S. are unclear. Greek courts have upheld the claim that extradition of Greek nationals is forbidden.

Diamantis flew to England after traveling to the Bahamas by boat, officials say

Authorities and Diamantis' lawyer, Norman Pattis, did not say when Diamantis left the U.S.

Federal prosecutors said he traveled by boat from Florida to the Bahamas, then boarded a plane to London. They said that although Diamantis had surrendered his U.S. passport, he obtained a Greek passport. Pattis said he was told by Diamantis during a phone call Wednesday night that he was in Greece and would not be attending the sentencing.

U.S. District Judge Stefan Underhill set a new sentencing date for Sept. 30 that would go forward with or without Diamantis in attendance.

Connecticut officials were quick Thursday to condemn Diamantis for fleeing the country and took steps to stop his state pension payments.

“Kosta Diamantis betrayed the public’s trust and needs to be held accountable for his actions,” the governor said in a statement. “His repeated efforts to skirt justice are shameful. I hope he is apprehended and made to face the music as soon as possible.”

State Attorney General William Tong, also a Democrat, added in a statement, “His disappearance this morning is a shameful insult to every person in Connecticut and will not deter our efforts to fully protect the state’s interest and taxpayer dollars.”

Prosecutors sought a decade-long prison sentence

Prosecutors asked the judge to send Diamantis to prison for 10 to 12 years, while Pattis argued in court documents for a sentence that included no prison time but strict conditions of release.

After the court hearing, the defense attorney told reporters that he was surprised that Diamantis fled the country.

“I think that Mr. Diamantis was facing a tough day here today and would have gotten at least four or five years, perhaps 10 to 12,” he said. “So as a lawyer, I cannot support his decision to take the law into his own hands. But as a fellow human being, I understand why he did what he did.”

Diamantis maintained his innocence since his arrest

Pattis provided copies of the email Diamantis sent to him to media outlets.

“The injustice that has occurred to me and my family by political weaponization is beyond rational belief,” Diamantis wrote in the email. “I have lost everything that took me an entire lifetime to earn and more. It is devastating to lose your home, your children's home, your car, your job, the ability to get a job, your law license, your honor, your dignity and pride.”

He said he hopes President Donald Trump and the U.S. attorney’s office in Washington would take a look at his case. Diamantis claimed Lamont used “the power of his office and his powerful friendship with President Biden to create an insular system of justice” aimed at protecting the governor's own wrongdoing.

Diamantis has another pending criminal case in federal court, where he's accused of taking bribes to quash a state audit of an eye doctor accused of Medicaid fraud.

Witnesses said they gave Diamantis envelopes of cash

In the school construction grants case, Diamantis was convicted of using his position as director of the state’s Office of School Construction Grants and Review to demand and ultimately receive thousands of dollars in bribes from contractors to steer building contracts their way, from 2018 to 2021.

He was accused of threatening to terminate those contracts if he wasn’t paid.

During the trial, witnesses testified about handing Diamantis envelopes of cash at various locations, including a men’s room at an upscale restaurant, a doughnut shop and his home. Some payments were referred to in messages as “birthday cards,” “pars” and “birdies.”

Diamantis, who testified in his own defense, admitted that he received the money but insisted it was legitimate consulting income.

A federal judge has ordered Donald Trump’s administration to provide at least 30 days’ notice before making any physical changes to the Kennedy Center — including demolishing it.

The judge responded to a series of court filings on Thursday after the president suggested the memorial to John F. Kennedy could be “ripped down” following a board vote to shutter the institution for repairs after he failed to stamp his name on the building.

The Department of Justice insists that the Kennedy Center is only “temporarily” closing for seven days to address “advanced deterioration,” fueling speculation that the president could try to tear it down altogether.

The venue’s closure may be “extended” after workers “assess existing safety risks in those portions of the main building exhibiting severe structural deterioration,” according to the Justice Department.

The latest wave of legal filings follow an extraordinary 24 hours for the living memorial to the assassinated former president, as workers installed fencing and orange barricades around the property while Trump publicly mulled whether to demolish the building entirely after courts blocked his attempts to rename it after himself.

open image in gallery Donald Trump appeared to review a placard about the Kennedy Center while onboard Air Force One one day after the venue’s board voted to close it down without his name on it ( AFP/Getty )

Democratic Rep. Joyce Beatty, a Kennedy Center board member who is leading the legal battle against Trump’s efforts, requested an emergency court hearing on the building’s closure, which her legal team says violates an injunction that was issued earlier this year.

She alerted Washington, D.C. Judge Christopher R. Cooper to Trump’s remarks on Wednesday night, telling reporters that the building “will end up being ripped down” unless the president is given “recognition” for his takeover of the memorial.

He later appeared to be reviewing a placard reading “Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED” while sitting on Air Force One — images that Beatty’s legal team have now included in court filings.

“Given the emergency nature of this matter and Defendants’ 10 a.m. filing deadline for their response to Plaintiff’s motion, Plaintiff wanted to make sure the Court and Defendants are aware of this new information,” her lawyers wrote.

Judge Cooper denied Beatty’s request for an emergency hearing.

But he clarified that the Kennedy Center must tell the court “if there is any change in the Board’s plans that would constitute a reversal of the Center’s position that the building will not be demolished and that no new structure will be constructed.”

Bill Pulte, Trump’s director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency and former Acting Director of National Intelligence, was aboard Air Force One when AFP photojournalist Brendan Smialowski captured images of the president reviewing the placard.

Pulte did not respond to a text message from The Independent asking for more information about the poster.

open image in gallery Workers installed fencing and barricades around the Kennedy Center on September 16 after the board voted to shutter the institution ( Reuters )

The board’s executive director and chief operating officer decided to temporarily close the Kennedy Center due to “acute risks to public safety resulting from continued structural deterioration” of the building, according to government lawyers.

That decision from Matt Floca was “separate from any Board decision related to closure for ongoing renovations,” lawyers with the Justice Department wrote in court filings Thursday.

Floca also claimed that a message over the Kennedy Center’s speakers telling people to leave stemmed from an improperly triggered alarm.

“I did not authorize that alarm, nor am I aware of a legitimate reason why that alarm may have been triggered,” he wrote in court filings.

Beatty’s legal team said Floca’s explanation for the closure “cannot be squared with the record.”

The Kennedy Center is only temporarily closing the building as “a plain pretext to justify shutting down the Center permanently,” her lawyers wrote in response to the Justice Department’s latest filings.

“It is a recipe for Defendants extending their shutdown forever and closing the Kennedy Center for the next two years — the very thing this Court said they could not do without its permission,” they wrote.

“It goes without saying that demolishing the Kennedy Center’s main building would violate the Court’s preliminary injunction,” they added.

open image in gallery A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to give at least 30 days’ notice before making any changes to the building — including demolishing it — after lawyers raised alarms following its abrupt closure ( Reuters )

In May, the judge blocked the president from renaming the venue after himself, writing that Congress made it “crystal clear” that the building is only to be named after former President John F. Kennedy, “and it cannot bear any other formal name or public memorial” based on a “unilateral say-so” from a Trump-appointed board.

Last week, Cooper blocked the board from trying to rename the venue after Trump, again, after board members proposed adding “renovated and restored by President Donald J. Trump” to the facade.

“The Kennedy Center is a sacred, living memorial to President Kennedy, not collateral damage in placating Trump’s ego,” Beatty said in a statement shared with The Independent.

“It is simply outrageous that we have gotten to the point of consistent judicial intervention to protect this historic institution from getting bulldozed by the President,” she added Thursday.

Last month, after government lawyers repeatedly argued that the performing arts venue is falling into “financial ruin” and rapidly deteriorating in a state of “terminal decline” without Trump at the helm, the Justice Department suggested that it could fall into such extreme disrepair that will require it “to be taken down.”

Trump, with his “unrivaled expertise and experience in real estate and construction” and “prominence” as president to raise money for the venue, must be memorialized on the building’s marble facade — or the Kennedy Center will “deteriorate further into an unsafe, decrepit structure that will be required to be taken down,” according to the Justice Department.

Andrew Feinberg contributed reporting from Washington, D.C.

News.title: Interest rate increase ‘likely’, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Andrew Bailey has said that interest rates are likely to rise if the Middle East war rages on, warning inflation is now on course to hit 4pc.

The Bank of England opted to hold borrowing costs at 3.75pc on Thursday, the sixth time in a row it has left them unchanged.

However, the Governor said a “material” increase in energy prices since July would push up inflation to twice the Bank’s 2pc target.

He warned the outlook for inflation “continues to be on the upside” and criticised the “seeming loss of urgency to find solutions” to the war in Iran.

Oil prices are back above $100 a barrel and analysts expect average gas and electricity bills to rise above £2,000 this winter as the conflict continues.

Mr Bailey said: “So far, higher global energy costs have had a limited effect on price and wage setting in the UK.

“But the longer this volatility persists, the bigger the impact it will have on inflation, and the more likely it is we will need to raise Bank Rate to ensure that inflation falls back to our 2pc target.”

Investors expect the Bank to raise interest rates as soon as November, which has pushed average mortgage rates to their highest level in three years.

The average five-year fixed mortgage deal has risen to 5.87pc, according to Moneyfacts, which is the highest level since November 2023 and up from 4.95pc before the Iran war.

Thursday’s rate hold leaves the Bank out of step with central banks around the world after the US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank voted to raise borrowing costs this month.

However, economists said there had been a change in tone from policymakers over the threat posed by energy prices and whether this would feed into the wider economy.

The Bank of England predicted that inflation would hit 4pc early next year, just as most workers are negotiating pay rises.

Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said: “It seems as though a majority of the MPC is on the cusp of wanting to tighten policy.”

In a warning on the impending pain facing households, Mr Bailey told the Chancellor that energy bills would rise by 24pc early next year under the Ofgem price cap.

This will push up annual average bills by £413 to £2,136, which the Governor blamed on the war in the Middle East.

The Governor is required to write a formal letter to the Chancellor every time inflation is more than a percentage point above its 2pc target.

Official data showed inflation rose to 3.1pc in August.

Mr Bailey said: “The energy price shock has been the most important factor driving recent short-term movements in inflation.”

Despite expectations of higher rates, the FTSE 100 rose on Thursday at its steepest pace since July, climbing more than 1pc, as the Bank of England eased the pressure on the UK bond market.

Policymakers also confirmed a Telegraph report that the Bank will stop selling the long-dated bonds it amassed during the financial crisis and lockdown.

The Bank will continue actively selling £20bn of government bonds per year until the rest of the stockpile is wound down to zero in 2034.

The announcement triggered a sharp fall in the cost of borrowing for the Treasury, with the yield on 30-year UK gilts falling at the fastest pace since May.

News.title: Next-generation antivenom fights India’s deadliest snakes
News.content:
The process to make antivenom has barely changed in a century: snakes are milked, their venom is injected into horses, and their antibodies are harvested to form the basis of the product. The resulting treatments are difficult to administer, can trigger severe side effects, and the quality varies from batch to batch.

“The big four snakes contribute to 70 per cent of poisonous bites [in India]… so 30 per cent of poisonous snakes are not covered, even to begin with,” said Dr Yogesh Jain, a public health physician in Chhattisgarh state and a member of The Global Snakebite Taskforce.

“But there are huge quality and efficacy issues even against these 70 per cent of bites. We’re relying on a 100-year-old technique of getting antivenoms, and at least 50,000 people are dying every year,” he told The Telegraph.

“There’s a real need for new technology. We don’t have a safe and appropriate antivenom for the largest majority of people in rural India.”

Now, scientists are hopeful that they have developed a potential alternative.

In the latest study, published last week, researchers showed that an experimental antivenom cocktail with five components protected mice against lethal doses of antivenom in Indian cobras, even when delayed by up to 20 minutes – a scenario that mimics the real-world lag between a bite and treatment.

“If you go 10 years back, people didn’t think you could make sufficiently simple products with new, modern biotechnology that could cover all these different snake venoms,” said Prof Andreas Laustsen-Kiel, head of the Section of Biologics Engineering at the Technical University of Denmark and co-author of the paper.

“People simply believed it was too complex, too expensive to manufacture, and so on… But the data we are gathering is convincing enough to say this is something that could make a huge dent in the lost lives and limbs snakebite causes every year.”

The antivenom itself was based on lab-made nanobodies – antibodies derived from a group of animals including camels, llamas and some species of shark. Scientists believe their structure means they could be a more potent, more precise, more temperature-stable alternative to man-made monoclonal antibodies – and cheaper to manufacture.

“The latest study builds on an earlier discovery of nanobodies that can protect across a broad spectrum of African snakes,” said Prof Nicholas Casewell, director of the Centre for Snakebite Research and Interventions at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, who has previously collaborated with Prof Laustsen-Kiel.

“In this paper they have iterated and demonstrated that a narrow number of nanobodies can protect against Indian cobras and king cobras. This demonstration brings the nanobody technology closer to market,” he added.

But that is likely still years away, depending on how much funding the researchers can attract. The next steps – a larger animal study, scaling up manufacture, and launching human trials – are expensive.

“If money was no issue, we could probably be testing in humans in 1.5 to three years from now,” said Prof Laustsen-Kiel. “But since money is a big issue, it is more likely that human trials won’t be able to start until 2.5 to four years from now.

“But I really think that this [study shows] there’s no doubt that biotech can deliver better antivenoms. The question is whether people are willing to fund it,” he said.

News.title: Manchester United hounded off pitch by own fans
News.content:
The joke goes that Michael Carrick has already bettered Ruben Amorim’s efforts by reaching the third round of the League Cup, but Manchester United will need to find a way past free-flowing Brighton if they are to go any further.

United were eliminated in the second round by League Two Grimsby Town last season, but start the competition a stage later because they are one of nine Premier League clubs playing in European competition.

Brighton knocked United out of the FA Cup in the third round, with Danny Welbeck scoring at Old Trafford, meaning the club played just 40 matches in 2025-26.

Carrick will want to make a better fist of the cup competitions, but he could really use a win of any kind after taking just four points from United’s first four league games of the new season.

The no-show at Hull and derby defeat by City’s 10 men were especially dispiriting, and the relationship between the club and supporters is becoming increasingly strained.

There were no flags on the Stretford End for the game against City, as fans voiced their opposition to what they view as a heavy-handed ticketing policy. The club says the measures are to stop ticket-touting but critics believe many innocent season-ticket holders are being caught in the crossfire and having their tickets revoked.

Discontent is never too far away given the continued presence of the Glazer family, and confidence is fragile regarding the club’s sporting direction under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

The news that 15-year-old JJ Gabriel, possibly the country’s outstanding academy player in his year group, wants out (broken by Matt Law in a Telegraph Sport exclusive) nagged at some of those fears.



Gabriel could have been in contention for a place on the bench this evening, but that is now surely out of the question even if United say they have not given up hope of persuading him to stay.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Spurs finally score... but still lose
News.content:
“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

News.title: England cruise to victory led by ‘absolute freak’ Brook
News.content:
Whatever his returns, there has been an extra focus to Brook’s approach this summer, possibly because he has learnt from a grievous indiscretion in Wellington last winter. While others chase the Indian Premier League, he is totally committed to England, taking his break while that tournament is on and playing every match in all formats for his country.

Brook had come to the crease at the fall of the first wicket and, while it is early days, England appear to have added another arrow to their quiver. They handed a debut to opener Aneurin Donald, with his cap presented in the pre-match huddle by Pietersen, the new “specialist mentor”.

Donald has been selected as an “intent merchant”, charged with going extremely hard from the first over, aping Phil Salt, who is missing with a quad injury. He did what he was asked to do, smearing his first ball for two, then pulling six to leg and hammering four through the offside before the first over was out. Another big shot, off Wellalage, in the second saw him well caught in the deep, but 12 off five had kickstarted the innings.

News.title: Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town
News.content:
At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit 19-year high as global bond rout intensifies
News.content:
The cost of UK government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007 in a fresh global debt sell-off.

The yield on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, rose from 5.37pc to a fresh 19-year high of 5.41pc on Tuesday as rising oil prices risk reigniting inflation.

Mortgage experts have warned that residential and buy-to-let mortgage rates are set to climb towards 5pc, as market turmoil threatens to filter through to household finances.

Short-term debt costs have also jumped, with the yield on two-year UK bonds surpassing 4.9pc for the first time in three years.

The bond chaos came as Andy Haldane, a former Bank of England chief economist, warned that Labour risked becoming “just a traditional tax and spend socialist government with better TikTok videos”.

He told LBC that John Healey’s original plan for a “low drama budget” had been “torpedoed” by higher borrowing costs and “events over the last couple of weeks”.

He said: “I think that [the bond market turmoil] will mean some hard choices next month at the Budget.”

“Few hard choices so far, but one is looming on the horizon, how any hole to the budget headroom is made good on. Is that a question of tax rises, or is it a question of taking the knife to public spending.”

Mr Haldane has been advising Labour since Andy Burnham took power.

It comes as the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of England face pressure to raise interest rates this week to combat rising prices.

Anthony Brinkman, a portfolio manager at Principal Asset Management, said: “The recent gilt market movements seem to be intent on showing central banks they are out of time – the market is expecting action.”

Borrowing costs around the world are rising after a 20pc surge in oil prices so far this month.

Brent crude tipped above $109 a barrel this week after Houthi rebels in Yemen, considered a proxy for Iran’s forces, seized control of a key port in the Red Sea, threatening shipping.

The US Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates on Wednesday in the face of the inflation threat.

As a result, the yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds has surged above 5pc for the first time since 2007.

News.title: AI could transform global inequalities or ‘widen the gap’, warns Bill Gates
News.content:
“AI could be a great equaliser, or [it could] widen the gap”, says Mr Gates. “This is not a long-range prediction. It’s a present-tense choice”.

“We can harness AI for good. But it won’t happen by accident. After all, the market is an extraordinary engine of innovation, but a terrible guarantor of equal opportunity.

“With AI, the gap could grow even faster … That is what makes this moment so urgent. Things are changing rapidly, and the window to shape who benefits from AI, and how soon, is short”.

The key issue holding back the deployment of AI in the developing world revolves around the availability of local data and, in turn, the ability for the technology to scale in environments very different from where it is currently being created.

An app that is trained on billions of hours of American English, will struggle at first with British English (see your spell check) but is next to useless if your local language is Swahili or Chichewa.

More profoundly, an AI tool that allows a farmer in Hampshire to control his combine harvester remotely, will offer little to a smallholder in South Sudan who works the land by hand and faces a completely different array of pests, weather conditions and costs.

The same is true for health. “A community health worker in Rwanda examining a baby with a fever faces different questions than a clinician in a well-resourced hospital - and the AI supporting her needs to reflect that”, says Mr Gates.

He adds: “Most of the world is invisible to today’s AI models. These AI systems were trained primarily on what exists on the internet – and the internet reflects a deeply unequal world. More than 90 percent of the data used to train early, large language models came from English-language sources. The communities that stand the most to gain from AI are largely absent from the knowledge base these tools are built on. They are not just underserved. They are not in the picture at all”.

The new investment aims to help correct that. Mark Suzman, CEO of the Gates Foundation, says investments are already being made with companies including Microsoft and Google to build databases of a much wider range of languages, for instance.

Africa alone has more than 2,000 languages, and for AI’s to be effective there they have to understand what and how people actually speak - “their dialects, accents, and slang, too”.

The investments, he says, are being made on the condition that the intelligence and knowledge they accumulate are made freely available for others to use.

Languages for AI “are true public goods, almost definitional public goods. They need to be freely available to everybody. Once they’re created, they are public goods that can be uploaded onto any AI,” said Mr Suzman.

Sports.title: FA chief demands full Fifa probe into Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell plot & Donald Trump’s secret call to unban star
Sports.content:

FA CHAIR Debbie Hewitt wants Gianni Infantino to release all the documents concerning his radical plan to flog stakes in the World Cup.

Hewitt, 63, wrote a letter to the Fifa president this week and it was also sent to the governing body’s secretary general Mattias Grafstrom.



The Fifa Council are due to meet next month and Hewitt believes all members should have the files relating to Infantino’s scheme before then.

She has also called for an explanation over the decision to suspend USA striker Folarin Balogun’s ban at this summer’s World Cup.



Balogun was due to miss the last-16 tie with Belgium after being sent off in the previous round against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

But, following a call from president Donald Trump, the ban was suspended for a year and the striker was able to play.

Infantino’s plan to sell shares in the World Cup to private investors was revealed after the tournament and sparked outrage.

The proposals have now been scrapped but Hewitt, who is a Fifa vice-president, believes there should be an independent review.

Infantino, 56, has remained defiant during the backlash and confirmed he plans to stand for re-election next March.

But the leaking of the sell-off idea – dropped amid the worldwide condemnation – saw opponents, led by Uefa, gather their forces.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Uefa threatened to withdraw from all future Fifa tournaments unless Infantino quit – although that idea was pulled back in August after the governing body gave a commitment that there would be no return to the project.

Even so, Uefa, Asia and the North and Central American confederation Concacaf launched legal proceedings alleging Infantino’s effective £15billion valuation of the tournament would have amounted to fraud.

The three confederations want Swiss authorities to intervene but also lodged legal suits demanding “disclosure” of documents in three US states – New York, Florida and Colorado.

And a number of national bodies, including the FA, have officially withdrawn their letters of support for Infantino.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick must fix glaring problem if Man Utd are to win as horror stats reveal why Red Devils can’t compete
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED’S issues on the football pitch so far can be boiled down to one of the oldest problems in the book.

On Wednesday the season went from bad to worse as Michael Carrick‘s side fell to a shocking 2-3 defeat to Brighton in the League Cup, losing at Old Trafford after leading 2-0 for the first time in 42 YEARS.



But glaring issues in recruitment, squad profiling, and retaining stars far past their sell by date are merely the surface issues plaguing them at the moment.

Instead, Man Utd can put a large portion of their issues down to something that is totally unforgiveable to fans; they don’t run enough.



Man Utd have looked leggy in the latter stages of matches this season, which is a huge issue given the modern Premier League has some of the fittest players in world football across the league.

Indeed, in every Premier League match this season they have been outrun by their opponent, except for their loss to Manchester City – who played with 10 men for the majority of the game after Phil Foden‘s sending off.



The opener against Hull saw Carrick’s side run 1.9km less than the Tigers in the 2-0 defeat, with the home win over Ipswich seeing the Tractor Boys run 112.8km to Man Utd’s 112.1km.

Then against Everton the difference was the Toffees 112.5km to 110km by United.

Running, sprinting distance and number of sprints also saw Carrick’s side behind their opponents in each game bar the City defeat.

The overall numbers against the wider league do NOT paint a pretty picture either.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

They rank 14th in the league for total distance covered at 449.1km.

And if that wasn’t bad enough, they rank down in 18th for sprints (379), sprints per km covered (0.84km), and then 19th for high speed runs (1,364) and high speed runs per km (3.04km).

Following his arrival last season, Carrick was credited for making training sessions shorter and sharper following the Ruben Amorim era.

It paid dividends as they reacted to make the top four and earn a spot in the Champions League.



Man Utd ratings vs Brighton: Lacey a shining light on dark evening as Heaven and Yoro ripped apart MANCHESTER UNITED suffered a humiliating Carabao Cup exit at Old Trafford as Brighton came from two goals down to reach the last 16. It is the first time in 50 years that United have held a 2-0 lead at Old Trafford and lost the game. The Red Devils were in dreamland after early goals from Shea Lacey and Mason Mount, before the Seagulls took control and mounted a stunning comeback. United have not won a domestic cup match since beating Leicester in the FA Cup in February 2025 and again crashed out at first attempt of the Carabao Cup following last season’s horror show at Grimsby. Michael Carrick is feeling the heat after goals Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper ended one of two potential trophy hopes this season. Here’s how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated the United players from Old Trafford, as Brighton picked up a fifth straight victory in M16...

However, a pre-season interview with Rio Ferdinand and Youri Tielemans saw the new signing admit there hadn’t been loads of running, which explained was the case given the minutes at the World Cup.

And those methods and the apparent lack of fitness work being done to make the squad physically fit enough to compete for a full 90 minutes could be part of the reason Man Utd are struggling this season.

Conversely, their next opponents, Fulham, are top of the league when it comes to distance covered – having covered a whopping 6.6km more on average per match so far this season.

It has been made abundantly clear Man Utd players aren’t good enough to walk through matches, so hard work is the bare minimum required to win.

Man Utd are yet to win away from home this campaign.



But rewarding the travelling away support with a precious win in London would be a huge step in attempting to course correct the season before it becomes a write off.

Sports.title: First look at The Real Rooneys shows fuming Coleen telling Wayne off for staying out late with pals on holiday
Sports.content:
Next

WAYNE Rooney jokes about having several “doghouse manuals” over his boozing and bad behaviour in his new TV series.

Wife Coleen is seen giving the ex-England and Manchester United striker a dressing-down on holiday after he stays out late with pals.



In a trailer for The Real Rooneys, she tells him: “It’s meant to be a family holiday. You can’t keep doing what you do.”

It then cuts to a sheepish-looking Wayne back at home who laughs: “The doghouse manual… I’m on my third book.”



The couple, who met as kids in Croxteth, Liverpool, have been rocked by Wayne’s off-field exploits over the years, including a boozy all-nighter in a hotel room with three women in 2021.

Wayne has since said he would be “dead” if it was not for his wife’s support.

The couple, both 40, have now let cameras into their Cheshire mansion, also home to their four sons — Kai, 16, Klay, 13, Kit, 10, and Cass, eight.

Coleen has gone from stay-at-home mother to in-demand star after a stint on I’m A Celebrity, as well as her famous legal battle with Jamie Vardy’s wife Rebekah.

She says on the teaser for the Disney+ series: “Since the court case and then the jungle, it’s opened up a lot of doors.

“So I’m getting back to work and Wayne’s helping out with the school run.”



At one point, Klay is asked: “Who’s more famous? Mum or dad?”

He replies: “My dad. My mum is only known because of my dad.”

Moaning about their chaotic home life, Wayne says: “Why did I have kids?”



Asked if he’s got any more planned, he laughs: “I’ve had the snip.”

Now a BBC pundit after several stints at management, he is also seen with Coleen floating in icy water wearing orange suits.

Wayne laughs: “I never thought when I was growing up in Crocky that I’d be dressed as a squid drinking champagne.”



However Coleen is also shown breaking down as she says: “There’s a lot of pressure.

“It’s just a bit hard juggling everything. The house is not happy.”

The Real Rooneys starts on September 24.

Sports.title: Met Police release statement over first Millwall vs West Ham clash in 14 years as they reveal huge operation for derby
Sports.content:
Next

THE METROPOLITAN POLICE have issued a statement ahead of the first Millwall vs West Ham clash in 14 years as officers prepare for a major operation around this weekend’s London derby.

The two sides will meet at The Den at 12.30pm on Saturday, renewing one of English football‘s fiercest rivalries.



The Met Police confirmed that additional measures will be in place to help ensure the match passes off safely.

In a statement posted on X, the force said: “On Saturday, 19 September at 12:30hrs, @MillwallFC face @WestHam at the Den – the first time the two clubs have met since 2012. We want fans to enjoy the match safely and have worked with both clubs to help this happen.



“As with any fixture, the Sporting Events Act 1985 is in place, which means entering or attempting to enter a ground while intoxicated is strictly prohibited. A Section 35 dispersal order will also be in place, allowing officers to remove anyone causing disorder. It will cover this area.”

The fixture will see the clubs renew a rivalry that dates back more than a century.

Millwall and West Ham first met in a friendly in 1897, with the rivalry developing due to the close proximity between the two clubs.

Their former home grounds, The Den and West Ham’s Boleyn Ground, were just under seven miles apart.

The rivalry has also been marred by a number of violent incidents involving upporters over the years.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



The 2009 League Cup match at Upton Park was won 3-1 by the Hammers after extra-time, but the game was overshadowed by pitch invasions and disorder around the stadium.

A Millwall supporter was stabbed during the disturbances, which continued in the streets surrounding the ground.

This historic clash hasn’t occurred too often down the years as the two clubs have mostly been in separate divisions.

But West Ham’s relegation from the Premier League in May has brought them back together in the Championship.



This weekend’s derby arrives with both clubs having plenty to play for on the pitch.

West Ham currently sit top of the Championship with 14 points from a possible 21 – ahead of Swansea, Middlesbrough and West Brom on goal difference.

Millwall are 11th on ten points but will be looking to build on a strong campaign last season.



The Lions narrowly missed out on automatic promotion by a single point to Ipswich before their play-off campaign ended against Hull.

Sports.title: Gary Neville and Roy Keane slam JJ Gabriel’s representatives for taking ‘nuclear option’ in demanding transfer exit
Sports.content:

MANCHESTER UNITED legends Gary Neville and Roy Keane put JJ Gabriel’s representatives on full blast after the wonderkid expressed his desire to leave.

United Academy star Gabriel, 15, wants out amid interest from Barcelona, Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich and rivals Manchester City as well as Chelsea.



The striker had been in line to play a part on Wednesday’s disastrous Carabao Cup elimination to Brighton at Old Trafford – so much so that his name was included in the matchday programme.

But a tantrum over a lack of first-team minutes so far this term saw the England Under-17 international refuse to train and subsequently dropped from manager Michael Carrick’s matchday squad.



Gabriel, who is represented by his father and former footballer Joe O’Cearuill, is said to believe Man Utd have had ample opportunities to play him in the first team this season, including in the Champions League.

And according to talkSPORT, the young prospect dubbed Kid Messi has sent in formal notice to cancel his registration at the club in order to become a free agent.

However, club greats Neville, 51, and Keane, 55, have taken exception to the teenager’s decision of choosing the “nuclear option”.

The England legend suggested it was the player’s camp who leaked the news about him wanting to leave, which is not in the United Under-18 star’s best interest.

Neville told Stick to Football: “There was this big announcement from a prominent journalist that’s obviously been leaked.

“If the club’s not going to leak that, it’s not in the club’s interest to leak this, not on the back of the weekend. So, the player’s representatives have definitely leaked this.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“They’ve decided they want to go the nuclear option and go: ‘Bang, we’re JJ Gabriel to leave Man Utd’.

“That to me is my concern is that who’s representing him thinks that’s good for the kid.”

Keane criticised Gabriel’s lack of patience as he insists there is still plenty of time to properly grow within Man Utd’s first team.

The legendary midfielder added his former team needs wins and momentum after a disappointing loss to rivals Man City in the Prem and a heartbreaking Carabao Cup exit.



Therefore, the timing is not right to introduce young players under such pressure.

Keane said: “Are you telling me he can’t wait? If you are 15 years of age and you’re talking about playing for Man Utd’s first team, just wait. Can you wait another six weeks if United get through the cup?

“Carrick’s under pressure. Obviously, [Sir Alex] Ferguson would throw young lads into the first team. But United, they need wins [right now].

“I don’t think United are in a position where they go: ‘We can write off a cup game tonight and play a couple of young lads’.

“‘We need to get momentum into the season. If some 15-year-old is spitting his dummy out, we’ll deal with that.’”



Neville is adamant United and Gabriel should learn from the way Arsenal have been handling their own wonderkid Max Dowman.

Dowman, 16, has already made history in the Premier League after becoming the competition’s youngest ever goalscorer last season at the age of 16 years and 73 days.

However, the Gunners have found a balance with the way they treat Dowman as they hand out opportunities in the way that adds necessary protection for the youngster.

Neville added: “I just don’t see the logic from any representatives of a 15-year-old boy who think it’s a good idea to put his name in lights right now.

“You want to try and sort of douse the flames, don’t you? You don’t want to add fuel to a fire.

“Max Dowman, if you remember last year when he came on, you know, Sky probably asked for an interview at the end of the game.

“Arsenal said no. They got him straight back into the changing room. He’s back at school on Monday morning.”

Sports.title: Michael Carrick given breathing room at Man Utd despite shambolic results as Roy Keane blasts culture after cup KO
Sports.content:

MICHAEL CARRICK still has the backing of Manchester United bosses despite the club’s shambolic start to the season.

Old Trafford chiefs are not panicking after the Carabao Cup exit, which saw United defeated for the third time in six matches, following only four points from four Prem games.



But Carrick knows he needs a positive result at Fulham on Sunday to give himself more time to turn things around during the three week international break.

There is no real sense that the hierarchy has lost faith in Carrick, who secured Champions League football before being left short in the transfer market.



United crashed out of a third straight cup competition at the first hurdle and head into this weekend 13th in the table ahead of their trip to winless Fulham.

Ineos only gave Carrick a two-year contract in May, so it would be a shocking U-turn if they sacked a third manager in two years.



But the dismal nature of the two home defeats in four days – to a City side reduced to 10 men after 23 minutes and a much-changed Brighton team who became the first in over 50 years to win at Old Trafford after trailing by two goals – has sent shockwaves through the fanbase.

Carrick’s players must step up as performances have been dreadful. United have only played well in the second half against Ipswich Town and the first 10 minutes against Brighton.

United have been dreadful across defence, while Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo have not hit the ground running this season.

The decision not to sign a left-back has been made a mockery of by the injury that has kept Luke Shaw out for three games, with neither Patrick Dorgu nor Noussair Mazraoui able to fill the void adequately.

Carrick lined-up in midfield the last time United lost at Craven Cottage in December 2009 and he has been around long enough to know the pressure losing runs can build.

Meanwhile, United legend Roy Keane has called out the culture of the club from the top down.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick told who is putting his Man Utd job in 'danger' as players absolved
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick told who is putting his Man Utd job in 'danger' as players absolved

Manchester United have had a week to forget and will look to bounce back when they take on Fulham on Sunday afternoon

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has been warned about his Man United job. (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has been told that his tactics are putting his job at Old Trafford in danger. The team have suffered a difficult week, losing to both Manchester City and Brighton.

‌



The Manchester derby saw United unable to overcome 10-men for the majority of the game. Wednesday night then saw the team pegged back from 2-0 up to lose 3-2 against Brighton in the Carabao Cup.

‌



The full-time whistle was greeted with boos from around the stands, with some questions now being asked of Carrick. The former midfielder was appointed permanently in the summer, after leading United back to Champions League football.

‌



Former United striker Louis Saha has now hit out at Carrick’s tactics and highlighted what he believes could be improved. Speaking to Betano , he said: “The problem with Manchester United this season is not the players. Benjamin Sesko missed pre-season after his injury.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“Some players took their time to return after the World Cup. In truth I don’t think it was a good summer transfer window for Manchester United. But Michael Carrick has to adapt.

“I don’t see a team that has the animation it needs. Manchester United needs a system to play good football, with patterns of play.

“I think the way they are playing now is dangerous to Michael Carrick because this is not down to the players. Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, even Bruno Fernandes need a team that is playing with more fluidity, and I don’t think their teammates are doing that at the moment.

‌



“The two defensive midfielders look too comfortable passing the ball slowly, side-to-side. It does not provide the sort of passes forward to create those one-on-one moments.

“In transition they are too slow. It doesn’t matter who you put in these situations, whether it’s Sesko or Cunha or Mbeumo, if one of them isn’t taking more risks and pressing forward, it’s not going to help advance the play.

View 3 Images Man Utd crashed out of the Carabao Cup against Brighton

‌



“United create some chances but they are not clear cut chances, and they aren’t using the acceleration of Marcus Rashford to get behind teams, so they don’t have that dimension either. It’s all too slow.”

Midfield was a priority in the summer transfer window. United spent a total of £155 million on signing Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba.

But, despite the arrivals, it’s the exit of Casemiro, who left on a free transfer in the summer that Saha says has had the biggest impact.

‌



“How can Michael Carrick avoid falling short as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer did? What he must do now is support the team to animate the system, a way of playing, a certain motion and rhythm to what they do,” he added.

“Some of this comes naturally from the players you have but everything else must come from the manager. Last season a lot of that came from Casemiro. They still have not replaced him.

View 3 Images Casemiro left the club in the summer (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

‌



“People said he had no legs left but look at what Manchester United have lost now. He was the animator of the team. He gave everyone a belief in what they were doing.

“He was ready to seize the moment and take a risk and you could feel it in how they played. That’s why he is a great, great midfielder and has shown it over the years because he brought that balance.

“I think they can have that again with the players at the club but now it is Michael Carrick who must give this balance to the team as the manager. Maybe Carlos Baleba can offer this when he comes back from injury, which would also allow Bruno Fernandes to facilitate the strikers too.

Article continues below

“United need someone who excites the team, winning the ball, feeding the runners, lifting the crowd. United need something special there because they are missing a player who is dynamic and creative.”

Sports.title: Ex-West Ham star Michail Antonio found guilty over Lamborghini incident in London
Sports.content:
Ex-West Ham star Michail Antonio found guilty over Lamborghini incident in London

Footballer Michail Antonio has been found guilty of failing to identify the driver of his Lamborghini when it was suspected of involvement in a motoring offence in London

View 2 Images Michail Antonio now plays for Watford (Image: Getty Images)

Former West Ham striker Michail Antonio has been found guilty of failing to identify the driver of his Lamborghini when it was involved in an incident in central London.

The footballer, aged 36, was charged by the Metropolitan Police with failing to assist an investigation when his car had been spotted being driven without due care and attention late at night in Pall Mall last November.

‌



Antonio told Uxbridge Magistrates’ Court he was not the driver that night, having allowed his Lamborghini to be loaned out by his cousin while he was away in Manchester.

‌



The star claimed he had not received the initial police letter, asking for the driver’s identity, suggesting it was lost in the post.

View 2 Images Michail Antonio during his time at West Ham in December 2024 (Image: PA)

And he gave evidence that he was "shocked" to discover, in February, that he had been charged with a failure to identify the driver. Antonio told the west London court that he left his cousin to reply to the charge, believing he had also provided details of the guilty driver.

‌



Today, magistrates found him guilty of failing to give information relating to the identification of the driver of a vehicle when required.

He was handed a six-month driving ban and ordered that he pay a fine and court costs totalling £2,050.

Magistrate Ian Comfort said the panel was sure the police letter had arrived, and found that Antonio had failed to respond according to the legal requirements.

‌



Antonio already had six penalty points on his licence, after being convicted of driving without insurance in July 2025.

He was given a further six points on Thursday, leading to an automatic six-month disqualification, and he was ordered to pay a £1,000 fine, £650 in prosecution costs, and a £400 victim surcharge.

Antonio was the registered keeper of the Lamborghini Urus at the time of the incident on Pall Mall at 12.38am on November 5 last year. The Metropolitan Police then wrote to him on November 12 to seek the identity of the driver but when a response was not received, a criminal prosecution was started.

‌



Giving evidence, Antonio said he was visiting his children in Manchester from November 3 to 6 last year, and said he had handed over the keys to the Lamborghini to Tarique Josephs who runs a company loaning out cars. He said he called Mr Josephs in February after receiving a notice of the criminal charge.

"I was in shock", Antonio said, of his reaction to finding out he was being prosecuted. He continued: "How can I be charged with something I haven’t done? This is the first time I was aware of that."

He gave evidence that Mr Josephs "rents my car every now and then", telling the court: "When someone calls up for a Lamborghini, he will call me and say can I use your Lamborghini.

‌



"I worked out he had the car at the time, he has come across to me to collect the forms, and said he would send the details." Mr Josephs told the court he filled out the response to the prosecution, entering a not guilty plea and giving a brief explanation that the car had been on loan.

When questioned why he had not mentioned the other driver’s details on the form, he claimed to have included a copy of the loan agreement in the same envelope when posting it back. The court also heard evidence from Sunita Bains, Antonio's girlfriend.

The woman explained she handles the mail to their £2.2 million mansion in Buckinghamshire, saying she does not believe the initial police letter ever arrived.

Article continues below

Antonio’s footballing career was derailed in December 2024 when he crashed a Ferrari in Epping Forest in Essex, suffering a badly-broken leg. The star, a Jamaican international, spent three weeks in hospital and was out of the game recovering from his injuries for more than half a year.

Antonio, who has played for Reading, Sheffield Wednesday and Nottingham Forest, became West Ham’s top scorer in the Premier League during 10 years at the club. He left in summer 2025, joining Al-Sailiya in Qatar where he made four appearances and then signed for Watford on a free transfer earlier this month.

Sports.title: Kevin Miller dies aged 57 as tributes paid to ex-Crystal Palace and Watford goalkeeper
Sports.content:
Kevin Miller dies aged 57 as tributes paid to ex-Crystal Palace and Watford goalkeeper

Kevin Miller, who played for clubs including Crystal Palace and Watford, had been working as Wigan Athletic's goalkeeping coach before he passed away on Tuesday

View Image Kevin Miller has died at the age of 57 (Image: Allsport UK/Allsport)

Wigan Athletic have confirmed that goalkeeping coach Kevin Miller has sadly died aged 57. The ex-Crystal Palace and Watford star passed away unexpectedly overnight on Tuesday.

‌



Miller, a father and husband, joined Wigan this summer, reuniting with former Exeter boss Gary Caldwell. The Latics posted on their website: " Wigan Athletic is deeply saddened and devastated to learn about the sudden passing of Goalkeeping Coach Kevin Miller.

‌



"Everyone at Wigan Athletic is deeply saddened and devastated to learn about the sudden passing of Goalkeeping Coach Kevin Miller. Kevin joined the Club earlier this summer, linking up with Gary Caldwell, a close friend and colleague, and the wider First-Team staff after more than three years as Goalkeeping Coach at Exeter City and an impressive playing career that spanned over 18 years.

‌



"Although Kevin's time with Latics was far too short, he quickly became a much-loved and respected member of our First-Team staff. His experience, professionalism and passion for goalkeeping were clear for all to see, while his uplifting personality made a lasting impression on everyone who had the privilege of working alongside him.

In a playing career of almost two decades, Kevin made more than 700 career appearances, including in the Premier League. He began his professional career with Exeter City, helping the Club to the Fourth Division title, before going on to represent Birmingham City, Watford, Crystal Palace, Barnsley, Bristol Rovers, Derby, Southampton and Torquay.

"Following an impressive career, Kevin moved into coaching and management, eventually returning to St James Park as Goalkeeping Coach in 2022, where he was able to pass on the considerable knowledge and experience he had gained throughout his career to the next generation of goalkeepers.

"Kevin's contribution to football was significant, but for those who worked alongside him, it was the person he was that will be remembered most. Kevin was a husband, father, hugely respected colleague, dedicated coach and someone who made a genuine impact on those around him, both on and off the pitch.

‌



"His sudden passing has left everyone at the Club deeply saddened and devastated. Our thoughts and prayers are with Kevin's wife, Fiona, daughter, Esme, close family, friends, colleagues and all who knew and loved him.

"The Club asks for total privacy for Kevin's family and friends at this difficult time. Everyone at Wigan Athletic sends its deepest condolences to Kevin's loved ones."
