‌



Exeter also shared a heartfelt tribute on their social media channels. "We are deeply saddened to hear of the sudden passing of club legend Kevin Miller at the age of 57," the Grecians began.

"Kevin was an incredibly popular figure during his time at St James Park, earning a place in the hearts of supporters with his performances between the posts and his wholehearted commitment to the club. As a player, Kevin had a commanding presence and a fierce competitive spirit.

"He joined Exeter City in 1989 under Terry Cooper and went on to make over 250 appearances for the Grecians over two spells as a player. He was a key part of the team that won the fourth division championship in 1989/90.

Article continues below

"Kevin rejoined City as Goalkeeper coach in December 2022 under Gary Caldwell where he used his wealth of experience to play a key role in the development of City's goalkeepers. At just 57, his passing is a huge loss to his family, friends and everyone who knew him.

"Exeter City Football Club sends its deepest condolences to Kevin's family and friends at this incredibly difficult time. Our thoughts are also with Gary Caldwell and our former staff at Wigan Athletic. His time in Devon left a lasting impression on those around the club, and his contribution remains a big part of Exeter City's story.

"The club will be supporting those who were close to Kevin and will be commemorating Kevin's time with us and his memory in an appropriate way. Once a Grecian, always a Grecian. Rest in peace, Kevin."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick is already under pressure at Man Utd - another defeat would be unthinkable
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is already under pressure at Man Utd - another defeat would be unthinkable

Michael Carrick picked Manchester United up by the bootstraps and through a wave of positivity took them back to the Champions League - now the mood is very different indeed

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is under pressure after a sticky start to the new season

Michael Carrick rode the crest of a wave last season to get Manchester United back on the biggest stage.

‌



This season, Carrick looks as if he is drowning in the expectation levels, demands and ongoing soap opera at Old Trafford.

‌



Make no mistake. Carrick is now under the cosh. United go into this weekend 13th in the table after a disappointing start. They are out of the Carabao Cup.

‌



And, worst of all, the United fans made their feelings plain. They booed Carrick and his players off the pitch after the defeat to Brighton. It felt a big moment in Carrick’s reign.

United’s fans are notoriously loyal, supportive and pride themselves in backing managers - rather than calling for them to be sacked. It is genuinely one of the best things in football.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The self-proclaimed biggest club in the world probably have more right than most to boo, jeer and get angry.

United have been stuck in a cycle of under-achievement and yet the fan base bought into Carrick because he is a club legend. Just like they did with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. They are desperate for it to work. And yet United are in serious danger of making the same mistakes all over again.

‌



Carrick gave the club such a lift as interim boss after Ruben Amorim’s spell in charge. After the shackles of Amorim’s rigid and failing tactics, Carrick felt like a breath of fresh air. He did a fantastic job. The upturn was remarkable.

It swept United along into the Champions League places and we were all guilty of making the same mistake: saying he deserved a chance. And, to be honest, it still feels like he did.

View 3 Images Those positive early days under Carrick now seem a long way in the rear-view mirror (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

‌



But this is Manchester United. You do not win prizes or become successful by making popular decisions. The summer was when United should have thought about bringing in a stellar name, elite manager and one who could have taken the club on the next step of the journey.

Sadly, it still feels like Carrick is the interim despite being given the job on a permanent basis. That is down to perception and also perhaps Carrick and his staff - including the vastly experienced Steve Holland - failing to convince us otherwise.

It was a patchy transfer window to put it mildly. Youri Tielemans was a good buy. Carlos Baleba is one for the future. Andrey Santos for £48m is mind-boggling. He was not a fixture at Chelsea.

‌



In the summer of 2025, United beefed up the attack - and yet still the three big purchases do not always start together. Benjamin Sesko is still largely a sub. Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are more regular starters but we’re still not sure how they dovetail together.

The defence lacks strong foundations. The midfield is a work in progress. And the heat is on the manager. To make matters worse, the academy’s jewel in the crown, JJ Gabriel, wants out.

‌



United could look to blame VAR for the Manchester City defeat. But excuses run out when you throw away a two-goal lead (the first time in 50 years at home) against Brighton.

This season was always going to be the real test. European football, bigger expectations and building on last season all with extra fixtures and a demand for silverware.

Carrick says he can deal with the pressure. Though that was not the case as he got bad tempered and snappy after the defeat at Hull City. He said, after they beat Ipswich the following week, the criticism was too much. No, it’s to be expected when United lose at Hull.

‌



View 3 Images Defeat to Fulham this weekend will leave Carrick under serious pressure

Now, United go to Fulham on Sunday knowing that another defeat will raise a hell of a lot of questions about Carrick ahead of a painfully long international break.

If United lose then the 20 days before their next game will be torture. Carrick will feel heat like never before. The longer break will only increase the pressure.

Article continues below

But it already feels like United are in danger of enduring another wasted season and going for the romantic, popular decision by appointing the likable club legend will have backfired badly.

Sports.title: Alexis Mac Allister's dad delivers honest truth about Liverpool exit talk as Real Madrid eye deal
Sports.content:
Alexis Mac Allister's dad delivers honest truth about Liverpool exit talk as Real Madrid eye deal

The father of Alexis Mac Allister's has spoken out about his son's situation at Liverpool

View 3 Images Alexis Mac Allister has openly commented about his Liverpool contract situation (Image: Gaspafotos/MB Media, Getty Images)

Alexis Mac Allister's father has moved to quash speculation that the Liverpool midfielder is looking to quit the club amid the impasse over a new contract. Carlos Mac Allister insists it is entirely within the club's remit to decide when they wish to open talks over fresh terms.

‌



That follows a candid admission of frustration from the Reds star last week. Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch, who arrived at the club in the same summer as Mac Allister in 2023, have both been handed contract improvements this year, prompting the former Brighton man to say he was "very, very sad" about his own situation.

‌



But his father - himself a former Argentina international - has sought to downplay the matter. Acknowledging that Liverpool had yet to make contact following last week's remarks, he told Scores 365: "No one from Liverpool's management has contacted us to renew his contract yet.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"We have a contract that is valid and we are committed to it with Liverpool. And if the club does not offer to renew the contract, it is their right. For now, Alexis has to give his best for the club in every game over the weekend.

"Alexis is not disappointed. This is a decision that the club makes, and we don't judge their decisions, we just prepare for what's to come."

‌



Rumours linking him with a move to Real Madrid have been dismissed, with Carlos stating: "No-one from Real Madrid has contacted us at any point in the entire career of Alexis."

Mac Allister made his eye-opening comments ahead of last week's Champions League victory over Atletico Madrid, another club he was linked with in the summer. He said: "There were options to leave this summer.

View 3 Images Dominik Szoboszlai has signed a new deal recently (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

‌



"I think as everyone knows I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract, which of course makes me very, very sad.

"I think I give 100 per cent for this football club every single day in training, games. Of course, I can have very good games, bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

"I see Dominik and Ryan renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it, but at the same time, it makes me a little bit sad I didn't get mine.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Mac Allister is in great form despite his unhappiness over his contract situation (Image: Liverpool FC, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

"Of course, there is still time, the fans don't need to worry because I will give 100 per cent until the last day I am here. We will see what happens. But I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give my 100 per cent to the club."

The in-form Mac Allister, who has netted twice in his last two games, is set to feature when the Reds visit Bournemouth on Sunday.

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho 'behind' as ex-Man Utd star facing brutal Aston Villa reality
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho 'behind' as ex-Man Utd star facing brutal Aston Villa reality

Alejandro Garnacho left Manchester United in the summer of 2025 to join Chelsea, but the former Red Devils forward has struggled for minutes while on loan at Aston Villa

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho moved to Aston Villa in the summer but has struggled for minutes so far (Image: Nigel French/PA Wire)

Aston Villa star Alejandro Garnacho has been given some words of advice by manager Unai Emery after missing out on minutes in the Carabao Cup. He was left on the bench for the 3-1 win at Coventry City on Wednesday night.

‌



Garnacho left Manchester United in the summer of 2025 to join Chelsea on a permanent move worth around £40million. It was this summer that saw Garnacho on the move again after making just 43 appearances for Chelsea, where he went on to sign for Villa on a season-long loan, which also includes an option to make the deal permanent.

‌



However, Garnacho has been restricted to just three substitute appearances for Villa since his move to the Midlands, all of which have come in the Premier League.

‌



Garnacho would have hoped to get minutes in the Carabao Cup third round tie against Coventry on Wednesday night, but was an unused substitute as Emery decided not to give the former United winger any time on the pitch.

La Liga clash postponed minutes before kick-off after tunnel flooded by torrential rain READ MORE :

Roy Keane tells Man Utd exactly what to do after JJ Gabriel exit threat READ MORE :

When pressed on his decision not to give any minutes to the former United star, Emery offered advice to the Argentina international.

"Continue working. Work, work, train, work," he said, via BirminghamLive. "When he can have minutes to play, try and play well. He is progressing, but we have players in front of him now.

‌



"George [Hemmings] is playing fantastic. Alysson is also understanding things well and is giving us things I want. [Ibrahim] Mbaye also responded well.

"We want a competitive team and players to compete in the style we have. Garnacho is a little bit behind because of some circumstances we had in pre-season. It is time to be patient for the time he needs."

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho moved to Aston Villa in the summer (Image: Matt McNulty/Getty Images)

‌

Emery has previously made clear his desire to retain Garnacho at Villa for a "long time" as he outlined the club's ambitions for the former United star.

"We want him at the same level he was for Chelsea in the first part of last season and in Manchester two years ago," the Villa boss said last week.

Article continues below

"He is a player we have signed for a long time, and we will help him to feel comfortable and confident to get his quality."

Sports.title: Kieran McKenna spotted in Man Utd directors' box as pressure on Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Kieran McKenna spotted in Man Utd directors' box as pressure on Michael Carrick

Brighton & Hove Albion beat Manchester United in the Carabao Cup third round at Old Trafford with Kieran McKenna watching on from the Old Trafford directors' box

View 2 Images Kieran McKenna was at Old Trafford to watch Manchester United play Brighton & Hove Albion (Image: Getty Images)

Kieran McKenna watched Brighton & Hove Albion beat Manchester United in the Carabao Cup third round from the Old Trafford directors' box. The former Ipswich Town manager spent over five years as an academy and first-team coach at United before beginning his managerial career.

‌



McKenna, 40, decided to take time away from football this summer after stepping down from his position with The Tractor Boys. He spent five seasons in Suffolk, winning three promotions, including two to the Premier League.

‌



During that time, Brighton reportedly wanted McKenna to replace Roberto De Zerbi. Chelsea also apparently contacted Ipswich about their manager.

‌



United were another club credited with an interest in rehiring their former under-18s head coach after the 2023/24 season. McKenna, though, signed a new four-year contract before the end of May.

Around a month later, United triggered a one-year extension to Erik ten Hag's contract before sacking him less than four months later. Approaching two years later, the successor to his heir, Ruben Amorim, in Michael Carrick, is under increasing pressure.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

United lost to Brighton despite leading 2-0 after ten minutes. It is the first time they have been defeated at home in such a manner for half a century. McKenna witnessed it live just over three months after deciding to step away from football management.

He said at the time: "I now look forward to taking a break from management and dedicating some time to my family, who have been with me every step of my career so far."

‌



He said at the time: "I now look forward to taking a break from management and dedicating some time to my family, who have been with me every step of my career so far."

The London-born Northern Irishman was linked with Celtic throughout last year. That speculation followed the departures of Brendan Rodgers and Wilfried Nancy. A vacancy could well open up again at Parkhead before long. Martin O'Neill is feeling the heat after losing to Rangers in the Scottish League Cup quarter-finals.

View 2 Images Kieran McKenna and Michael Carrick worked with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Manchester United (Image: Tom Purslow/Getty Images)

‌



Carrick returned to United in similar circumstances and is now under the spotlight after back-to-back defeats. However, he says: "I don't feel under pressure.

"Either way, that doesn't bother me one bit. I understand what goes on outside and how the world works, but it doesn't bother me. What bothers me is winning games, having a good feeling around the place and a good feeling around the group to know we're moving in a good direction."

Next up for United is an away match against Fulham. After that, there are almost three weeks between matches due to the international break.

Sports.title: Somerset's title hopes hit while Stokes stars with ball for Durham
Sports.content:
Dom Bess dented the Rothesay County Championship title hopes of old club Somerset after he struck 77 for Yorkshire to set a tricky final-day victory target of 287.

Spinner Bess walked to the crease with Yorkshire on 54-6 and after he joined forces with George Hill to take the hosts up to 128 at the end of day two, the duo kicked on during the morning session and put on 166 for the seventh wicket.

Hill narrowly missed out on a century with 89 before Bess was out for 77, which helped Yorkshire up to 275 before Somerset were reduced to 73-3 during a rain-affected chase, with a further 214 runs required to reclaim top spot.

Image: Somerset have lots of work to do to keep their County Championship hopes alive on Friday (SWpix)

Warwickshire's two-day triumph over Essex has sent them to the Division One summit, but the three-way title race may become a two-horse race after Nottinghamshire collapsed in their second innings at Hove.

After Nottinghamshire dismissed Sussex for 358 and crucially claimed a third bowling point off the last ball of the 110th over, Haseeb Hameed's team were undone by the bowling of Aristides Karvelas and Jaydev Unadkhat.

Nottinghamshire captain Hameed initially led from the front with 44, but his dismissal left his side on 86-2 and sparked a collapse, with Karvelas able to claim 4-34 before a stunning three-wicket spell by Unadkhat reduced the visitors to 149-7 - a paltry lead of 31 going into day four.

Sam Robson's top score of 92 got Middlesex up to 298-6 at Gloucestershire and a 328-run advantage, while Northamptonshire require 312 runs for a final-day win after Derbyshire were dismissed for 286.

Sports.title: Rai shares BMW PGA Championship lead with McIlroy three back
Sports.content:
Aaron Rai took a share of the BMW PGA Championship first-round lead alongside Joakim Lagergren as Rory McIlroy "stumbled" after a strong start to finish three off the lead.

Englishman Rai, who dazzled with his approach play, and Lagergren of Sweden posted scores of six-under-par 66 at Wentworth.

In windy conditions, 2013 Masters champion Adam Scott also surged up the leaderboard to tie Ryan Gerard, Ludvig Åberg and Nacho Elvira for third with a score of 67.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy stumbled in the closing stages to finish his first round at the BMW PGA Championship three under par

Race to Dubai rankings leader Patrick Reed was one of 12 players to tie for seventh place heading into day two, with Viktor Hovland, Ryan Fox and Robert MacIntyre joining him as they carded 68s.

Jon Rahm endured a tough day on the course and left himself plenty to do to make the cut on Friday, after he posted three bogeys and a double-bogey in his front nine, on his way to a six-over 78.

Justin Rose, who struggled with his putting, fought back from going three down through 14 holes, to end his day at one over, thanks to birdies on the 17th and 18th.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Justin Rose fought back at the end of his round, making back-to-back birdies on his final two holes to finish at one over

Rai, who started on the ninth, came out of the blocks firing, carding back-to-back birdies on holes 10 and 11, before doing the same on 13 and 14.

"I felt like I got into the round fast and got a couple of birdies early on and continued to just play well throughout the round and keep the momentum going when I was out of position," said Rai, who won the PGA Championship in the USA in May.

Scott similarly got off to a fast start and made birdies in clusters, going four under through his front nine.

The Australian could have joined Rai and Lagergren at the top of the leaderboard, but a wayward drive on the 17th hole cost him his only bogey of the day before he bounced back with a birdie on the 18th.

Image: Adam Scott surged to tied-third on the leaderboard after posting a first round score of five under

"I would say that was one of my best rounds, tee to green this year," Scott said.

"Not really sure why, just a nice tee shot off the first, kind of calmed any nerves and then went about my business from there. It's a nice way to play Wentworth when there's low stress.

"I know I'm going to have to dig deep to hang in there this week."

McIlroy comes unstuck late on

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy started his round in excellent fashion, going five under on his first 10 holes

It was a mixed first day for McIlroy who had a lot to be pleased about despite falling to tied-19th.

He began his round on the ninth and recorded birdies on the 10th and 12th, before making further gains on holes 16, 17 and 18.

McIlroy's wedges and putting were both excellent during his first 10 holes but his driving let him down, with the 37-year-old missing 10 fairways out of a possible 14 during his round.

The Northern Irishman would mix in a bogey and a birdie on the third and fourth holes, before going two over par in his final three holes, notably finding the water on the eighth hole, to end his round on a sour note.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy was encouraged by certain elements of his game following his first round

"A stumble home is a good way to put it," McIlroy said, reflecting on his closing holes.

"I wish I was standing here a couple of shots better. That's what I feel I should be, but overall, I saw some good signs in my game and saw some putts go in, which was encouraging compared to last week.

"It's definitely a score I can build on."

Sports.title: Hyrox athlete apologises for continuing race after soiling herself
Sports.content:
An Australian woman who was criticised for continuing to compete in a Hyrox event after soiling herself has apologised and said she will retroactively withdraw from the race.

Joanna Wietrzyk released a statement on Instagram, apologising for the incident during the indoor fitness competition in Beijing on Saturday.

Footage circulated on social media over the weekend showing Wietrzyk soiling herself, with the organisers Hyrox issuing a statement, apologising for how they handled the situation.

"I know my actions had an impact beyond myself, and I am genuinely sorry to everyone who was affected," Wietrzyk said in a statement.

Wietrzyk won the race but said she would forfeit and added: "I want to offer my sincere apology to the people of China, my fellow competitors, the spectators and the Hyrox organisers for what happened during the race in Beijing."

Hyrox said after the incident drew criticism that it had "clear bio contaminant and medical procedures in place".

Image: Hyrox is a fitness race that combines running and functional workout stations, testing both endurance and strength (AP Photo/Sakchai Lalit)

It said "an unforeseen situation arose" during which protocols became blurred, "creating ambiguity in how they were applied and understood".

In each Hyrox race, participants alternate between running a kilometre and doing fitness exercises, including a sled push, burpee jumps, indoor rowing and lunges while carrying a sandbag.

The competition has exploded in popularity since it was founded in 2017 in Hamburg, Germany, and is now held across the world. The sport debuted in mainland China in late 2024.

Sports.title: Hamilton responds to reports he has asked for Ferrari changes
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has responded to reports he has called for changes at Ferrari after two difficult weekends at Monza and Madrid.

Hamilton has fallen 101 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli with nine rounds to go, having scored just eight points in the last two races.

Ferrari brought an upgraded engine to their home event at the Italian Grand Prix but Hamilton only finished sixth, while Charles Leclerc crashed out, before a brake problem caused Hamilton to suffer his first retirement of the season in Madrid.

This week, reports in the Italian media have stated the seven-time world champion has been pushing team principal Frederic Vasseur to make operational changes, but Hamilton took to Instagram on Thursday to shut down the rumours.

"I've seen some of the stories that have gone out and I want to clear it up here. I've never asked for anyone on my team to be replaced. Everyone I work with works hard every day, and their dedication is what moves us forward," he wrote.

"I always try to empower and lift people to be the best versions of themselves or at least see the best in themselves. I may not always achieve that but it's my intention and what I'm here to do. We all work together and that will continue."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hamilton was forced to retire early at the Spanish Grand Prix

Hamilton called for "rules of engagement" at Ferrari after he was forced wide into the gravel by team-mate Leclerc at the Italian Grand Prix on the opening lap.

The British driver stated "the buck starts with Fred (Vasseur)" before Ferrari held talks with their drivers where Leclerc admitted he was at fault for the incident.

Hopes of a record-breaking eighth world title have diminished since the summer break with Hamilton not scoring a podium in the last five races.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle and Nico Rosberg debate who was at fault for the recent collision between Hamilton and Charles Leclerc

"I think there's no stopping him (Antonelli) and Mercedes this year," Hamilton told Sky Sports F1 after Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix.

"They've done a phenomenal job and they deserve it."

Sports.title: Will Palmer, Foden and Trent be recalled to England squad?
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer's outstanding form this season has put him in a strong position for an England recall, with the Chelsea man the most likely to be included from all the big names left out of the World Cup squad.

Palmer, along with Phil Foden and Trent Alexander-Arnold, was a headline omission from Thomas Tuchel's tournament squad in May, but he is one of the most startlingly in-form players in the Premier League right now, and the smart money is on him winning his international place back.

In the hugely oversubscribed No 10 role, the England boss went with Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers and Eberechi Eze in May, but Palmer is now fully fit after groin problems limited him to just 26 appearances last season, and his form has flourished.

Two goals and two assists show that. Only his team-mate Joao Pedro has more in the Premier League so far this season and only Bruno Fernandes has created more chances and had more shots combined (25) than Palmer (24).

It also feels like a space may have opened up for Palmer, with Eze's indifferent form for Arsenal. While starting in Europe and the Carabao Cup, Eze has yet to start in the Premier League so far this season.

Morgan Gibbs-White is in with a shout, after an impressive start to the campaign. But Tuchel constantly talks about "connections" between players as the key to England's success, and right now it is hard to argue there is a better attacking connection in the Premier League than Palmer and his close friend Rogers. There certainly is not an all-English one.

Will Tuchel try to change England 'DNA'?

This squad selection will be the first staging post in Tuchel's brave new post-World Cup era. Having stated publicly that England's DNA does not allow for ball-retaining passers, can he continue to leave Palmer, Foden and Alexander-Arnold in exile - three generational talents in terms of their passing and attacking prowess?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie O'Hara discusses why he still cannot forgive Tuchel for England's exit against Argentina in the World Cup

The issue here is that Tuchel is not a man to admit he was wrong. Like many, if not all, of the very best coaches in the world, there is an in-built self-belief - an arrogance, some would say - which is very hard to shake. It is partly what gives him his aura.

And if Tuchel does recall one of those big three, does that show the mask is slipping? Plenty in the media will pounce and take it as proof that the England boss got it wrong on the biggest stage when he named his World Cup squad three months ago. But he will also be criticised if he leaves those superstars out again. It is a lose-lose.

Despite his sending off in the Manchester derby last weekend, Foden has started the season in fine form. He leads the Premier League in assists after a ball carry (2), alongside Cody Gakpo and Julio Enciso. And of all the English players at Tuchel's disposal, he is probably the most technically adept with the ball at his feet. It remains to be seen whether Foden fits into the England plans right now.

Issues in defence

Alexander-Arnold may struggle to force his way back in, despite the glaring right-back issues Tuchel faced at the World Cup. Reece James and Tino Livramento both suffered injuries, leaving many to lament the Real Madrid star's absence, especially when centre-back Trevoh Chalobah was called up as a late replacement for Livramento instead.

But Tuchel has been adamant that the former Liverpool full-back's profile does not suit how he wants his England side to play, and it would be a big shift in the manager's philosophy if he went back on that now.

Alexander-Arnold has started only two LaLiga games this season, yet he has managed more successful crosses than all but two defenders in the league (6).

Tuchel knows top-quality delivery comes standard with Alexander-Arnold, but the manager has always thought defensive prowess matters more.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner believes good performances from Morgan Gibbs-White could warrant a return to the England squad

Tuchel does have something of a defensive crisis. The absences of John Stones, Dan Burn, Djed Spence and Ben White due to injury mean there are plenty of opportunities at the back. James has also missed Chelsea training this week, but has not been ruled out.

Despite those doubts, it still feels unlikely that Harry Maguire will get the nod for an international recall. Speaking out in frustration about his World Cup omission - the day before Tuchel publicly named the squad - was not well received by the England hierarchy.

The 33-year-old has been ever-present and impressive in Manchester United's four league games so far this season. He is currently ranked third in the Premier League for ball-carrying.

Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall - another controversial omission from the World Cup squad - is expected to get the chance this time in the Nations League. His consistency is clear and he has been excellent again this season - the best in the Premier League for winning possession in the defensive third (19 times) and fifth for successful blocks (5).

Whether Maguire's United team-mate Kobbie Mainoo is included in this Nations League squad remains to be seen. He did not play a minute of football at the World Cup, and was thoroughly disillusioned by the end.

Sky Sports News expected him to be selected for the third-place play-off match, but back pain developed in the final training session before the game, ruling him out. Nevertheless, his form for Manchester United so far has made him a strong England candidate.

Who will support Kane up front?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tim Sherwood tells Sky Sports FC he cannot see Dominic Calvert-Lewin being selected for Tuchel's next England squad ahead despite his blistering start to the season

Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin is pushing hard for a recall after an explosive start to the season. His double against Newcastle on Monday means it is four goals in six games so far.

It is form Tuchel cannot ignore, especially since Calvert-Lewin's main rival Ollie Watkins is now playing in the Saudi Pro League. Watkins' move to Al Hilal has seen him start in sparkling form, however, with three goals and two assists in four appearances.

Ivan Toney, who was the surprise inclusion at the World Cup, is unlikely to be considered for selection this time. He is due to be in court in Westminster in the middle of the international break to answer charges of assault causing actual bodily harm. His lawyer says he is looking forward to the opportunity to clear his name.

Despite the excitement around Max Dowman's performances for Arsenal and his two goals in the Carabao Cup win over Ipswich, no one expects an early call-up to the senior squad. The 16-year-old has not yet played for England's U21s, which is a more likely route as the FA, similarly to Mikel Arteta, carefully manage his minutes and his progression.

Dean Henderson has a foot injury, meaning there is space for a third goalkeeper to be called up alongside the guaranteed Jordan Pickford and James Trafford.

Sports.title: Tuchel considers England recall for Cole Palmer in Nations League squad
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel is considering an England recall for Cole Palmer and could include Alex Scott in his squad for the Nations League.

Tuchel’s first selection since the World Cup will be confirmed on Friday morning and the head coach has been weighing up claims from a host of players who failed to earn a place in his plans last summer. Palmer was one of those to miss out after struggling for form and fitness but the Chelsea attacker has started the season with four goals and two assists, raising optimism around his hopes of inclusion.

England, who finished third at the World Cup but faced criticism for their performance in their semi-final defeat by Argentina, have a host of players competing for the No 10 spot. Tuchel took Jude Bellingham, Eberechi Eze and Morgan Rogers to the World Cup and snubbed Phil Foden, Morgan Gibbs-White and Palmer. Gibbs-White has started the season well for Nottingham Forest and is in contention. Fulham’s Josh King is another contender for a spot.

King was one of four youngsters included as a training player for England’s camp in Florida before the World Cup. Scott, the Bournemouth midfielder, was also selected after failing to make the cut. The 23-year-old is in impressive form and was close to going to the World Cup. Scott is yet to make his international debut but is admired by Tuchel, who regretted not taking the Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha to the World Cup.

England are likely to name an extended squad as they open their campaign in Nations League Group A3 with games against Spain and Croatia and a double header against Czechia. Tuchel could shake things up, especially as some players who went to the World Cup are injured. Dean Henderson, Djed Spence, Dan Burn, John Stones and Jordan Henderson have fitness issues.

Players hoping to catch Tuchel’s eye include the Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin and the Forest forward Liam Delap. The Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton is yet to convince Tuchel. Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite and Chelsea’s Levi Colwill are options in central defence and Newcastle’s Lewis Hall could provide competition at left-back.
