Brentford v Chelsea: Recent head-to-head record Chelsea 2-0 Brentford - January 2026 - Premier League Brentford 2-2 Chelsea - September 2025 - Premier League Brentford 0-0 Chelsea - April 2025 - Premier League Chelsea 2-1 Brentford - December 2025 - Premier League Brentford 2-2 Chelsea - March 2024 - Premier League

Brentford v Chelsea: Team news

Brentford will be without the services of Joshua Dasilva, Antoni Milambo, Nathan Collins, Sepp van den Berg, and Kafe Furo for the derby.

Additionally, Mathias Jensen is a doubt for the Premier League clash and Igor Thiago will be aiming to score his first goal of the campaign.



As for Chelsea, Pedro, Caicedo, and James both missed training on Tuesday, yet there's been no suggestion of an injury.

On the other hand, Palmer and Rogers have been in excellent form this season and will be certain starters for the fixture.

Brentford v Chelsea: What's been said?

Following Pedro pulling out of the Brazil squad, Alonso said on Thursday: "In terms of injuries and the squad, we are having the last training session tomorrow so no one is ruled out for us for Friday.

"I prefer to be cautious. We will take the final decision on every player.



He added: "He's [Moises] getting closer and tomorrow we will make the final decision.

"Moi is one of the top midfielders in the world. Any team with Moi in the middle is a better team - and we are aware of that.

"We will see tomorrow, he has not been able to play and we've had to cope with that situation."

On James, he said: "No, it was just a decision for Tuesday. Tomorrow, we will decide."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel MUST start offering solutions after England's World Cup agony: The stubborn German needs to meet his critics halfway for a truce to be called in build-up to Euros, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
It was in Miami, before and after the circus act of the World Cup bronze-medal match, that you wondered if Thomas Tuchel had begun to question whether the high-wire act of managing England was really worth the merciless and aggressive inspection.

The inquest into the semi-final defeat by Argentina a few days earlier had been unforgiving. Tuchel was to blame. He did not like the tone of the criticism, nor its verdict. His feelings, we are told, have not changed.

'It (the criticism) felt as if we went out in the group stage without a win,' he told us after the valiant, if somewhat comedic, 6-4 win over France.

But the German was not joking. He was not smiling. There were no handshakes or tournament farewells. He made his point, celebrating the third-place finish, and left. He did not say this, but if you wanted a crude summation of his mindset, 'ungrateful b*******' would be just about right.

On Friday, he faces the media - and the music - for the first time since. Unlike his sit-down with Daniel Sturridge this week, as part of an FA film reflecting on the World Cup, the first question will not be: 'Well Thomas, it's almost two years in this role?'

Rather, he will be asked if reaching that anniversary was ever in doubt following the castigatory assessment of his part in England's World Cup exit. The answer, you suspect, will be a steadfast 'no', certainly judging by his upbeat mood and conviction of self in conversation with Sturridge.

Thomas Tuchel will face the media for the first time on Friday since the World Cup in July

His defensive tactics during England's World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina still lingers

And that is no bad thing. Tuchel's belief in himself is one of his greatest strengths. You watched Michael Carrick wobble after a third-round Carabao Cup defeat this week and you know that will never be Tuchel. He is a good man and a very good manager.

Yet, there is a feeling that he needs to meet his doubters halfway, if anything resembling a truce is to be called ahead of a 21-month runway to the European Championship. A line has not been drawn under Argentina, and the fault-lines will be stress tested if England underperform against Spain in their Nations League opener a week on Saturday.

They are the best and worst of opposition. A defeat by the world champions can be mitigated against more so than falling to Senegal or Japan. A win and all is wonderful again. But when the likelihood is of a demonstration of the qualities England continue to lack - manage the ball, manage the game, manage the moment - then the 'scars' from Argentina that Tuchel talks about are sure to be picked at.

Part of the backlash against Tuchel post semi-final was the suspicion of self-preservation when he pointed to a flaw in the 'DNA' of English players. Even if the diagnosis was correct, it was his job to reverse the coding and lead them to victory. To that end, he did concede some ground this week. Conceding ground, of course, was the root of the problem in Atlanta.

For the first time, there was an admission that his 'solutions' during the second half against Argentina did not work. He did not, however, go as far as to say he should have done something different - critics wanted England to attack, not defend - and so the wounds on both sides of the argument remain raw.

'No one knows what would have happened,' said Tuchel, when an alternative to his 'defensive changes' was broached by Sturridge. 'We could have done it and maybe lost 2-1. And people would go, "Is he crazy? He did it against Norway, finished the game with five at the back, so why not finish the Argentina game off with five?".

'From what I saw - the experience, the information, and the level of craziness that Argentina put in, one offensive change after the other - that was just my solution to the problem. I tried to help.

'If we would have been more stable in the game, let's say with more percentage of ball possession, I would have not changed the structure - why would I? And I would've gone for offensive changes.

'But it's my scar. I have to live with it. No one is more hurt than me. No one wanted it more. And you can now endlessly torture yourself and think, "If I would have done a different substitution, then we would've won the match". You just don't know it.'

Leading 1-0 with a lot of the second half to go, Tuchel deployed a back-five which didn't work

Tuchel described his players' retreat at 1-0 up as 'waiting for death' and that is why he intervened, reverting to the back five which had worked in previous knockout matches. He is right when he says the alternative could have been equally ill-fated.

But he is wrong to offer Argentina's 'f*** it football' as reason for their sudden liberation and England becoming prisoners in their own penalty box. Because what happens the next time opposition with nothing to lose throw everything at them? When Tuchel talks about DNA, soundbites such as this hardly help to evolve the genetics.

What he is yet to tackle properly - and he must on Friday - is the solution. The solution he could not find in the United States when his players needed it most. The solution that makes sure it does not happen again.

Tuchel has eloquently - and entertainingly - identified the problem. But listening to him this week, it felt like the defeat against Argentina was pre-determined once the second half began to play out the way it did. In short, there was nothing I could do. If so, what are you doing here?

The head coach says his mind 'only works forward'. Friday's squad announcement will be a sighter of how that looks personnel wise - Alex Scott, Rio Ngumoha, Josh King, Jarrad Branthwaite and Liam Delap are younger names pushing for involvement. But what is his plan technically? Tactically? Psychologically? That is the conversation England need to have now.

Tuchel survived the fall in Atlanta. Next time, there will not be a safety net beneath him.

Sports.title: 'I'm f****** angry... we're stuck on a hamster wheel and people are killing themselves': Former Wales star ALIX POPHAM bares his soul as rugby's civil war over brain injuries drags on - and insists he is not trying to 'ruin' the sport
Sports.content:
As he relaxes on the sofa in his home on the outskirts of Newport, South Wales, a pair of crutches lie next to Alix Popham – an aid to help with recovery from a recent hip replacement.

‘I’m 46 – young to have one,’ the former Scarlets, Newport and Wales back-rower tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘I got told five days before having this operation my other hip needs doing as well. I'm not complaining.

‘I knew that could happen from rugby. When I was playing, I saw ex-players who were wobbling around clubhouses due to bad backs, shoulders, knees and hips.

‘That, for me, was part of the game. But because brain injuries are invisible, they were never discussed then. We've opened the can on that.’

It has now been six years since Popham, to use his own words, ‘opened the can’. In April 2020, he joined England's 2003 World Cup winner Steve Thompson and others in revealing he was struggling with neurodegenerative diseases such as early onset dementia.

Their revelations launched legal action against rugby’s authorities, claiming their issues were as a result of their playing careers. Since then, the reality is little has changed.

It has been six years since Alix Popham joined a host of rugby players in revealing he was struggling with neurodegenerative diseases such as early onset dementia

The former Scarlets, Newport and Wales back-rower says he is 'f****** angry' at the lack of progress he and fellow ex-pros have made in their legal fight

Despite constant legal wranglings, countless court hearings and spicy media headlines, there has been no sign of a resolution to the case.

Last month, the legal action involving Popham and more than 500 rugby claimants was brought back from the brink of collapse after the High Court gave a reprieve to those who had previously been struck out from the case for failing to disclose necessary neurological testing information to the defendants.

‘I’m f****** angry,’ says Popham, his voice regularly cracking with both raw emotion and genuine fury. ‘We’re six years down the line and we aren’t any further ahead. We're on a f****** hamster wheel that’s just going around and around and around. The job of the defendants is to kick the can down the road for as long as possible.

‘We’re not even arguing over f****** brain damage yet. It’s f****** been six years. What’s being lost in all this is the impact on the humans involved. Think of the people we've lost since 2020.

‘Ex-players have killed themselves because of their suffering – Shane Christie and Billy Guyton in New Zealand. Lots of ex-players are struggling badly. Some have lost everything.

‘They are sofa surfing or washing in streams. Some are homeless. We’ve got a lot of vulnerable ex-players who want their day in court.’

That day still looks a long, long way off. After ditching their previous legal team – led by Richard Boardman of Rylands Garth – Popham and his fellow claimants now have new representation in their search for victory over World Rugby, the game’s governing body, as well as England’s RFU and the Welsh Rugby Union.

In November, the claimants’ new legal team KP Law must satisfy the court they are able to provide the documentary information required for the case to continue.

Popham is frustrated that in the six years since he and Thompson raised their heads above the parapet, rugby’s safety has not improved

'I don't think people appreciate the ripple effect that comes when you’re suffering with these issues,' says Popham. 'It’s a rollercoaster of emotions'

The inertia is doing no good to anyone. Not the ex-players who are struggling, nor the game’s standing and reputation. Popham believes rugby’s authorities are looking to delay a trial for as long as possible. But there can be no doubt that the claimants have questions to answer too.

Popham admits it was ‘tough’ to move on from Boardman and that he did an ‘unreal’ job, but the reality is the size of the case was too big for his small firm.

He is frustrated that in the six years since he and Thompson raised their heads above the parapet, rugby’s safety has not improved.

‘Seasons are longer. There are more games,’ says Popham. ‘They’ve put in guidelines for the number of games players should play (30 full matches in a season). But guys like Maro Itoje, Tommy Freeman and Henry Slade have gone over them. What’s the point in those guidelines if they’re broken?

‘They’re a PR tick to say we’re looking after players. It's the same with the guidelines on contact in training. It's all smoke and mirrors to portray that they care. Do they f***.

‘I can't wait for it to get to court. We just want to know our story has been listened to. If we go to court and we lose, we lose. I want to see it all the way. My personal view is we wouldn’t be happy to settle before court because that wouldn’t lead to changes to make rugby safer.

‘A similar case in the NFL ended in a settlement, but they didn’t accept their role in causing the problem. We would want some changes made that would make rugby as safe as it can be. We’ve got to leave rugby in a better, safer place.

‘That’s what we want. Rugby can continue, but there's got to be huge, huge changes. Players are getting bigger, faster, stronger. There's more internationals and that's to make more money. There is so much rugby. A model like the one Mike Tindall was trying to do with R360, where players were only going to be playing 16 or 17 games a year, is the only way you’re going to stop what’s been going on.

‘They’ve put in guidelines for the number of games players should play. But guys like Maro Itoje have gone over them. What's the point in those guidelines if they’re broken?'

Steve Thompson, a World Cup winner with England in 2003, has early onset dementia and probable CTE

‘I still love the game, but we're not being honest. I've had so much s*** from people saying I’m trying to ruin it. I couldn’t look in the mirror if I stuck my head in the sand and was not being truthful about what is happening. I'm happy to shout from the rooftops about this. I genuinely don't give a f*** about what people think of me.

'I'm not trying to ruin rugby. Rugby is ruining itself. The game as it is, is not safe. So many lives are being affected by it. Kids are starting contact in rugby at nine and should not be doing it. No way.

'Parents aren’t being told the truth. I won't let Darcy my youngest even play touch rugby anymore. It’s sad to say because I love rugby. But I've changed over this six-year period as I’ve become more educated on this issue.'

November is likely to be a last chance saloon for Popham and Co. He says the difference between KP Law’s work and that of Rylands has been ‘night and day’ though the former still have a significant task at hand to appease those heading up a legal case which retains the potential to be one of the most seismic ever seen in professional sport.

If the claimants successfully prove their neurodegenerative diseases are a result of head injuries suffered while playing and that the authorities were negligent in not helping to prevent them, a significant payout would be expected.

A repeat of the more than $1billion handed out by the NFL would ruin World Rugby, the RFU and WRU altogether.

Rugby's authorities deny breaching a duty of care and say safety rules have been updated.

World Rugby said last month: ‘With new legal representation now in place for the players, we hope that the litigation can move forward in accordance with the court’s expectations and in the best interests of the players and the sport.’

'I think of my brain like a kettle and I never allow it to boil over,' admits Popham. 'It's not normal'

Popham, who won 33 caps for his country, says: ‘We just want to speed up this process now to be able to move forward. Hopefully, we’ll get a date for trial in the next two years maximum.

'I don't think people appreciate the ripple effect that comes when you’re suffering with these issues. It’s a rollercoaster of emotions you go through and that can have a big impact on someone who doesn’t have a strong family network. It’s tough.

'I’ve only got a certain bandwidth for how I live day to day. I haven't got the brain capacity of a normal person, so I just try to manage it. I think of my brain like a kettle and I never allow it to boil over. It's not normal. I really, really struggle with sensory overload. If I allow myself to live how I was living before, that's when things build up and there'd be an explosion.

‘It's not a case of living normally as I should be as a 46-year-old. I’ve got brain damage in 14 areas that affects my day-to-day life. It’s as a result of playing rugby.’

For confidential support, call Samaritans on 116 123, visit samaritans.org or visit https://www.thecalmzone.net/get-support

Sports.title: Liverpool Confidential: Latest on new deal for Rio Ngumoha revealed, the clubs keen to poach him, why he's guaranteed more minutes this season, how Lewis Koumas reached 'dreamland' and injury updates on three key defenders
Sports.content:
Liverpool have issued a hands-off warning to clubs circling Rio Ngumoha and remain extremely keen to extend his contract.

There has been a flurry of talk about the 18-year-old’s future in the last week with Arsenal mooted as a club following his situation. Bayern Munich also expressed an interest in the summer transfer window.

Sources have told Confidential that the Gunners’ interest is not advanced and more exploratory. It is genuine, however, with the English champions keeping tabs on the situation in case the teenager struggles for game-time and gets itchy feet following the arrival of two new wingers – Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz – at Anfield.

Liverpool, though, would not entertain any offers for Ngumoha. His contract runs until 2028 and they plan to keep him beyond that. They see him as a future world-beater and believe he will get plenty of minutes this season.

It is understood Ngumoha is aware of interest from elsewhere – not just Arsenal and Bayern Munich – but is happy at Liverpool.

Ngumoha signed a three-year professional contract on September 25 of last year. That was the longest deal a player of his age could sign and the club also has a salary cap for youngsters – though the player will be remunerated well from bonuses.

Liverpool are keen for Rio Ngumoha, 18, to extend his contract at the club

Ngumoha could be named in the England squad for their upcoming Nations League matches. He shone on debut in a World Cup warm-up match in the United States

Sources close to the situation this week insisted there is no update on a new contract just yet but Ngumoha is enjoying life at Anfield. Liverpool are keen to reward him for his meteoric rise in the last 12 months.

Ngumoha moved to Liverpool in 2024, when they poached a winger described as the best talent in Chelsea’s academy. A tribunal ruled in February that the Reds must pay £2.8million to Chelsea, which could rise to £6.8m with bonuses.

He made his senior England debut in a World Cup warm-up match, starring against New Zealand. Thomas Tuchel is a big fan and Ngumoha could be named in the England squad announced this Friday for upcoming Nations League matches.

Ngumoha started against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League and Tottenham in the Carabao Cup in the last week and although he might privately feel uneasy about the arrival of £123m Barcola, the teenager will get lots of minutes this season given Andoni Iraola’s desire to rotate his wide men.

He started nine times last season and is already nearly halfway to matching that tally this time after just one month of the campaign. Due to his tender age, Liverpool were careful with his minutes last term.

They will still not push too much, too soon but Ngumoha is now trusted for more starts and longer appearances than mere cameos. Iraola likes to change his wingers mid-game which means all four – Ngumoha, Barcola, Cody Gakpo and Munoz – will get lots of game-time.

Ngumoha faces competition for his place from Liverpool's new £123m signing Bradley Barcola

Clubs including Arsenal and Bayern Munich have shown an interest in Ngumoha

KOUMAS IS IRAOLA'S DREAM

Confidential readers will recall last week’s musings on how it was obvious why Iraola adores Lewis Koumas. If it was not evident then, it is plain to see now.

The Chester-born forward is living his dream and it is especially pertinent when there was a lot of talk this summer about the lack of a local academy graduate in the first team in light of Curtis Jones’s exit to Inter Milan.

Geography experts will (rightly) contest the suggestion Koumas is a Scouser but the 20-year-old has grown up around the academy, having joined aged 11 from Tranmere Rovers, who were annoyed about their talented kid being poached.

Koumas has had a crack at breaking through before. He was an unused substitute a few times under Jurgen Klopp in the German's final season, including in the Carabao Cup final, and started an FA Cup tie against Southampton in February 2024.

He scored in front of the Kop but might have thought his Liverpool career would be limited to just one appearance after he was loaned out to Championship sides Stoke, Birmingham and Hull.

Those loans were positive but it would also be fair to say he showed few signs that he was ready to crack it on the biggest stage. When Koumas was left on the bench for the Tigers’ play-off final success, he could not have seen the next few months unfolding as they have.

‘I would have woken up!’ he said, laughing, when asked how he would have reacted then if someone had told him he would soon make his Champions League and Premier League debuts, then win man of the match in the Carabao Cup against Tottenham.

‘I would have thought I was dreaming. It’s crazy. But I’m just really happy and very grateful for the opportunities I’ve been given.

Lewis Koumas impressed with his high-energy style against Tottenham yesterday

Koumas credits his time on loan - including a spell with Hull City last season - as vital to his development

‘I never showed a weak mentality about how the future would look for me at Liverpool. I always had the drive that I would get here. The reason for going out on loan was to prepare for this moment.

‘The past two years have been massive for my development. Going on loan helped me become the player I am today. I was able to impress the new manager in pre-season and it all worked out well.’

Confidential reported in our first column of this season that Koumas, midfielder James McConnell and defender Luke Chambers were set to stick around despite huge interest in taking them on loan. It is understood Iraola made that decision early in pre-season due to their versatility, attitude and tactical skills.

Koumas, son of former Premier League midfielder Jason, can play as a striker, winger, No 10 and even operated as a wing-back for Hull. He is liked for his relentless and clever pressing, which is perfect for Iraola’s style of play.

It is reductive to simply say he is a good runner, as he is also adept on the ball. He scored important goals for Hull last season and does not seem fazed by big occasions.

The Wales international, who turns 21 next week, grew up idolising Gareth Bale and Michael Owen – though the latter's Liverpool career was slightly before his time. ‘How I play is ultimately the Liverpool way,’ Koumas added on Tuesday night.

‘We’ve always been a club where players have to give absolutely everything on the pitch. We’re bringing that back now and the crowd are loving it. You never know when your last time on the pitch for Liverpool is going to be. I just try to leave everything out there every time.’

The best word to describe Koumas is one from Iraola: ‘Contagious.' His running sets the tone for others and his story – with those loans in the lower leagues – should inspire other youngsters that development might not always be linear.

Right now, young buck Koumas must feel on top of the world – but he will hope this is only the beginning.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (right) describes Koumas as 'contagious'

ZIDANE AND KLOPP TO GET HANDS ON LIVERPOOL STARS

International squads are to be announced in the coming days with some interesting news lines to watch from a Liverpool perspective.

Does new France boss Zinedine Zidane reward the impressive Jeremy Jacquet with a first senior cap? Does new Netherlands manager Xavi stick by captain Virgil van Dijk, who will turn 37 during the next Euros? Will Ngumoha get that England call-up?

Former Barcelona midfielder Xavi also has a decision to make over Jeremie Frimpong, who was omitted from the World Cup squad and has struggled in the early weeks of this campaign.

Klopp will get his first chance to work with Florian Wirtz at Germany, too. The midfielder has shown glimpses of class this term but is yet to discover any consistency.

Former Reds boss Klopp could help him along the way. The Liverpool legend has been working his way around Bundesliga stadiums but is yet to be spotted at Anfield to run the rule over Wirtz.

Meanwhile, young Liverpool full back Isaac Mabaya has switched allegiances to Zimbabwe and accepted a first call-up after previously featuring for England’s age-group sides. He made his first-team debut at Plymouth in February 2025 but has been plagued by injuries since.

The 21-year-old went on loan to Wigan but was recalled to do rehab work at the AXA Training Centre.

Will the new France boss Zinedine Zidane reward Liverpool's impressive defender Jeremy Jacquet with a first senior cap?

And will Virgil van Dijk, who will turn 37 during the next Euros, still be key to the Dutch national team?

ROLE-MODEL MILNER COACHING KIDS

James Milner has returned to Liverpool to gain experience in his coaching journey – and give his own experience back to youngsters.

The 40-year-old recently called time on a stellar player career that spanned 24 years and saw him break the record for most Premier League appearances. He is now working towards his UEFA Pro Licence and is helping out with coaching some of the younger age groups on a casual and not permanent agreement.

It is a similar story with Conor Coady, who has been spotted at the AXA Training Centre several times in recent months. He is on Lee Carsley’s England Under-21 coaching team.

James Milner is coaching with Liverpool as he works towards his UEFA Pro Licence

INJURY LATEST: BRADLEY AND LEONI STEP IT UP

There is light at the end of an extremely long tunnel for two Liverpool defenders.

As documented in this column in previous weeks, Giovanni Leoni is stepping up his recovery from an ACL injury that has seen him miss nearly exactly a year.

Right back Conor Bradley is also on the comeback trail and is now training alone, doing ball work after a knee injury suffered in January. Small steps on both counts but positive to hear.

Federico Chiesa has been missing for several weeks but is aiming for a late-September return to training. He and Wataru Endo have been omitted from the European squad list.

And Joe Gomez went off at half-time on Tuesday night and fans feared the worst given it was the injury-prone defender’s first game of the season after a lay-off. But it was a planned substitution – he is OK and in contention to make the squad for Bournemouth on Sunday.

Sports.title: Travis Kelce embroiled in fresh controversy as insider reveals furious pregame dust-up with Broncos players
Sports.content:
Travis Kelce’s rigid adherence to pregame protocol was on full display before the Kansas City Chiefs’ opener at Arrowhead Stadium, where the star tight end reportedly lashed out at Denver Broncos specialists.

With both teams sharing the field for warmups before the Chiefs’ 31-10 win, Kelce found himself in Denver punter Jeremy Crawshaw’s line of fire, according to ESPN’s Scott Coughlin.

‘The punters for the Broncos messed up their timing,’ Coughlin told Scott Van Pelt on the SVPod. ‘I don't know if they got out there late.’

Given the warmup delay, the Chiefs receivers had already begun catching passes by the time Crawshaw started kicking, which inevitably led to some friction.

‘The punts are coming over the 50-yard line and Travis' eyes lit up, and he sees the ball, and it's a Broncos ball, and it goes over towards the Broncos' side, and he catches his route, runs over [to] the ball, takes the Broncos ball and punts it almost to the second deck,’ Coughlin said, adding that Kelce is a ‘good punter.’

‘Now he's looking for another one,’ Coughlin continued. ‘Sure enough, he goes back, gives the ball up, goes back, runs his route, and he's just steaming. You could see it. Here comes another one. So now the Broncos ball boy is running over because he saw Travis [run over to catch the punt] again.

Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce (87) and Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) celebrate after a touchdown against the Denver Broncos on Monday at Arrowhead

Denver Broncos offensive tackle Garett Bolles, left, greets Travis Kelce after Monday's game

‘Travis is like, “nope,”’ Coughlin added. ‘He beats [the ball boy] to the ball, takes the Broncos ball, chucks it up in the stands.’

Video of that pre-game incident has not yet surfaced, but Kelce was caught on camera having a run-in with fans before Monday night’s game. The confrontation was brief, but a Chiefs fan seated in the front row appeared to grab for one of Kelce’s gloves as he went to the locker room. Annoyed, Kelce seemed to swipe the fan’s hand away before entering the locker room tunnel.

Kelce had a much more infamous pre-game run-in with then-Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker prior to the AFC Championship in January of 2024. With Tucker warming up on the Chiefs’ end of the field, Kelce began clearing the kicker’s equipment to give his own teammates space to warm up.

Tucker, who has a history of warming up on the opponent's side of the field, looked frustrated but didn't engage with Kelce.

Meanwhile, Chiefs wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling also got in on the action as he was spotted kicking over a stand.

Although he wasn't wearing any padding during pre-game warmups, Kelce did have a pair of gloves on as he caught a few passes before getting changed in the locker room. He'd later remove them as he walked to the locker-room tunnel, which is when things got a little uncomfortable.

Kelce is pictured warming up before Monday's season opener against the Denver Broncos

Kelce still had his gloves in his hand when he reached to bump fists with a few Chiefs fans seated in the first row. One fan presumably thought Kelce was giving him a glove as a souvenir

Kelce still had his crumpled gloves in his hand when he reached to bump fists with a few Chiefs fans seated in the first row at Arrowhead Stadium. One fan presumably thought Kelce was giving him a glove as a souvenir, but when he tried to grab for it, the 14-year veteran appeared to swipe at the overeager spectator's hand.

Nothing else came of the interaction, which was recorded and quickly went viral online before being deleted.

Many seemed to recognize the misunderstanding.

'Think he thought he was handing him it lmao,' one X user posted.

'I mean it kind of look like he was about to give it to someone or he just wasn't paying attention to where his hand was but dude still shouldn't have tried to reach for it,' another added.

But a few others saw the incident as proof of some moral failure on Kelce's part.

'Most unlikeable dude in the league,' wrote one critic.

Sports.title: Inside the Beat Luke Littler auditions: Hundreds of darts hopefuls queue for hours to get their shot at facing star live on Netflix and winning £501k... and even Fallon Sherrock turns up!
Sports.content:
Inside the Beat Luke Littler auditions: Hundreds of darts hopefuls queue for hours to get their shot at facing star live on Netflix and winning £501k... and even Fallon Sherrock turns up!

There are more than 3,000 hopefuls taking part in the auditions for Luke Littler's new big-money Netflix show in Stratford.

Doors open at 8am for entrants to start making their ways into the LMA at Here East. Queues are hours long, snaking around the Olympic Park. Across the road, West Ham beat Wrexham 6-0 in the Championship less than 12 hours ago – one loud-mouthed Hammers fan in a park nearby is keen to let everyone know.

The idea of the show is simple: can the everyday man or woman beat Littler in a leg of darts? Up to 20 will have a go live on Netflix on October 30 on Beat Luke Littler, with anyone that can topple the reigning world champion and world No1 taking home a life-changing £501,000. Gary Lineker will host the show, with Richard Osman providing expert analysis.

There are three stages to the audition process today. To our thanks, we are taken through a different entrance and fast-tracked through to the practice area for stage one. No time for work – we're trying to win half a million.

In the practice room, we are allowed a few darts to prepare. Around 12 participants are brought through at a time. A producer bellows out the rules before another asks questions on camera. What would you do with the money? How did you get into darts? Don't answer like this, answer like this. That's showbiz.

As we make our way through to the competition boards, surrounded by big purple and yellow advertising reading 'Beat Luke Littler', we are introduced to our referees – essentially there to make sure there's no cheating the automated scoring system. 'Listen, mate,' we tell ours. 'There's no chance we're completing this, so can we finish once we've officially failed?' He nods in agreement, with a small smirk.

More than 3,000 hopefuls auditioned for Netflix's 'Beat Luke Littler' in Stratford, London

Up to 20 people will be given the chance to win £501,000 on Netflix - all they have to do is beat Littler in a leg of darts

The aim of the first stage is to complete a leg of darts in 24 throws or fewer. No ifs, no buts, no second chances. It's no easy feat. This part-timer may achieve it on a good day – locked away in his spare room while music plays on late evening. Under this sort of pressure is a different story. As expected, failure was the outcome.

But a lot of these contestants don't crumble under the pressure – they thrive off it. 'I can beat anyone on my day,' one auditionee, who wrapped up his leg in 12 darts, tells Daily Mail Sport. Wrap things up in 12 again on October 30 and you will more than likely find yourself £501,000 richer, pal.

Two or three participants make it through to the next stage. They are awarded a green sticker. 'Thanks for coming, and, if you didn't make it, don't worry - it's hard,' shouts another producer.

There are various abilities on show. Some wear jeans and get nowhere close. Others don their own personal darts shirts but struggle for a double. Others ease through – including 'Queen of the Palace' Fallon Sherrock.

For Sherrock, who has won two matches at the World Championship before – it's all part of the day job. She's probably the most famous face here. Anyone who has never held a tour card can enter – Sherrock may have won matches at the Alexandra Palace, but she's never been on the tour.

'I did it in 18,' she tells Daily Mail Sport. 'My scoring wasn't very good, but I took out a 157.

'I don't need the money, but I have always said I would like more opportunities to promote the women's game, and this is the perfect opportunity to do it. Why wouldn't you? It would be stupid for me not to do it.

'The queue was very long. We joined at 8am and got in at near enough 11. But I can do it - and I do speak to Luke. I know him, I know his mum, his dad, Faith, and they are lovely, genuine people.'

Daily Mail Sport auditioned- but failed to make it past the first stage

Those fortunate enough to make it to the second stage will face an interview with the production team, where they will discuss their approach to the challenge, how they would prepare to face Littler, and how they perform under pressure.

Even fewer will then make it to the final stage. That involves a chat with an expert judging panel, including 16-time world champion Phil Taylor.

We are made to wait to speak to Taylor. So we spend a while longer observing the hopefuls – some bubbling with emotion.

Darts mastermind Barry Hearn walks past us. 'Alright, lads?' he quips to the press. We will be when Phil is ready, Barry.

We're welcomed into Taylor's dressing room at around 1pm. He has been here since eight, and will be until seven. This right now is a short break for lunch, which will be eaten in his dressing room.

'I think someone will win it,' he says. 'They have got a chance. It's all about holding your bottle on a double.

'It's been different. I've never done anything like this before. It's similar to the X-Factor, but you have to be a bit nicer with this one. I'm not Simon Cowell.

'It's about encouraging the players, especially the youngsters coming through. It's very nerve-wracking for them. But we are looking for confidence, ability, and they have to be dedicated. It's not easy - you have to be so professional now. I was 30 when I first turned pro - some of them now are 13, 14, 15. To ask them to be professional at that age is very difficult.'

Laura Turner (left), Barry Hearn (centre) and Phil Taylor (right) are on the judging panel for the final stage of the audition process

The volume of interest in the show runs in line with the growth of the sport since Littler burst onto the scene

Littler isn't here. He's taking some time off before getting back into action with more Players Championship events and the World Grand Prix among events to come soon. It's unclear what he really thinks about this show – nothing is really on the line for him compared to the competitors, bar maybe pride.

'If you can go out in 12 darts, and you want to beat Luke Littler in a game of 501, he has to go out in nine, or you're half a million richer,' Taylor tells Daily Mail Sport. 'That's the secret.

'Luke is very laid back, quiet, very talented. Nothing fazes him, but the one attribute he has for me is he isn't bothered about the money. It's a bonus. I was always bothered about the money when I started - I had children, a mortgage to pay.

'I have had a throw with him. Not competitive. But I would love to get my form back, I am practicing a little bit. I am a bit too old now. I love retirement - it's great being at home. I ask my wife if we should go on holiday and we don't want to go away anymore, we travelled that much. I missed my family.'

While Taylor trots off to eat his lunch ahead of the afternoon shift, we head to chat to one or two more competitors. One owns an international flavouring company. Another is an electrician. They both have their green stickers and are waiting to speak to producers before potentially being put in front of the judges.

Simple maths says around 600 dartists will make it through the first stage here in London. That number will be whittled down to barely double figures by the time they have met the judges. The same process will happen in Manchester. Those auditions take place on September 19 at Manchester Central Convention Complex – you can visit BeatLukeLittler.com for more information on how to apply.

We're taken outside the same side door we entered through four hours ago as we leave the venue. The queues are still as long as this morning. A member of the Netflix production team tells us they think way more hopefuls have turned up than expected.

One thing is obvious: this idea, so far, is a hit. The attraction and attention runs parallel with the rise of darts since Littler burst on the scene. Next month, those that look up to the 19-year-old will have the chance to beat him and win big money. It's quite the opportunity.

Watch Beat Luke Littler live on Netflix on October 30

Sports.title: Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac star in Spygate spoof: Wrexham co-owners mock Southampton ahead of weekend clash - after missing out on play-offs amid scandal
Sports.content:
Wrexham will take on Southampton in the Championship this weekend – and the Welsh side's Hollywood owners have taken it upon themselves to poke some fun at their opponents ahead of the game. Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac have taken Wrexham from non-league to the Championship since their takeover of the club in 2021, and haven't shied away from using their acting credentials for a bit of publicity. On this occasion, in a video shared to social media, the actors can be seen coming from behind a tree similar to that of which Southampton intern William Salt was caught spying near. Mac says: 'I'm Rob Mac, co-chairman of Wrexham AFC.' Reynolds then springs from behind the tree, and adds: 'I'm Ryan Reynolds, also co-chairman of Wrexham AFC. Today, for no particular reason, we want to talk about the importance of privacy.' Mac then adds: 'Specifically how to prevent spies from looking at what you're doing on the internet.' Thanks to @firefox for keeping moles out of our Racecourse and data. 😉 🔴⚪ #WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/vL1kQ9vTRx — Wrexham AFC (@Wrexham_AFC) September 17, 2026 Wrexham owners Rob Mac (left) and Ryan Reynolds (right) poked fun at Southampton in a spoof Spygate sketch The duo then continue to play out a sketch for the of Firefox, and the mocking of Southampton doesn't stop. Mac says: 'And this message isn't just for people in Wrexham. Or Oxford, or Ipswich, or Middlesbrough.' The latter three were the sides Southampton were found guilty of spying on. The video ends with Reynolds showing Mac a video on his phone, as he jokes he's watching the 'Southampton pickleball team' train. Youngster Salt was spotted by Middlesbrough filming their training session ahead of the Championship play-off semi-final and, following revelations by Daily Mail Sport, the Saints were eventually thrown out of the competition. There was considerable sympathy for Salt, who told an EFL panel that he did not have an opportunity to say no and was acting on instructions from those above. WhatsApp messages obtained during the EFL investigation reveal how Salt was told, ‘You legend. Manager loved it’, after a spying mission on Oxford United in December.

Sports.title: Chelsea Confidential: Blues face choice between EIGHT YEARS at Wembley or new Earl's Court stadium
Sports.content:
Officially, it is now Clearlake’s Chelsea. Unofficially, it has been that way for some time, ever since that summer of 2022 when Todd Boehly acted as interim sporting director in one wild window.

That was a fun spell at least, of Boehly asking Thomas Tuchel whether he would like Manchester United’s 37-year-old striker Cristiano Ronaldo as a gift, only for the now-England manager to advise his chairman to drop that deal despite having already held talks with Jorge Mendes in Portugal.

Instead, Boehly signed Raheem Sterling on a £325,000-a-week, five-year contract, and Marc Cucurella from Brighton because he had heard how Manchester City wanted him, among others.

Since then, Boehly’s internal influence had waned, and last night’s confirmation of him and Mark Walter selling their shares and Clearlake taking complete control only cemented what we already knew: that Behdad Eghbali is the most powerful person at Chelsea.

Eghbali and his business partner Jose E Feliciano are in charge of Clearlake, who say there will be ‘no changes to the day-to-day operations, leadership or strategy at the club’.

However, there is one item high on Clearlake’s agenda, per sources, and that is what to do with Stamford Bridge. Insiders say they have had to try to work harder and smarter than their rivals to get around how their home, which carries a modest capacity of 40,343 and scant scope for non-football events, leaves them playing catch-up to other Premier League clubs.

Todd Boehly (left) selling his shares in Chelsea confirms what we already knew - that Behdad Eghbali (right) is the most powerful person at the club

It is a complicated process – and one which we are warned should still be measured in years rather than weeks and months – but also accepted as an important one.

Boehly, who showed a fondness for speaking at sports conferences during his time at Chelsea, talked up the need for a swanky super-stadium like ‘Jerry World’ – the home of NFL side Dallas Cowboys built by owner Jerry Jones to serve as an all-encompassing entertainment venue – while hinting previously that differing opinions over the stadium project could ultimately force them into a divorce.

Now that mum and dad have separated, it is Clearlake who will lead that call on what to do with the family home, and Confidential can shed some light on which way we understand they are leaning.

Sources close to Clearlake suggest they have ruled out remodelling their current stadium, a stand-by-stand gradual upgrade not being seen as worthwhile. That leaves two options: knocking down and rebuilding Stamford Bridge, or moving to an entirely new site, most likely Earl’s Court.

There has been a misconception that the latter could not happen because the Earl's Court Development Company have already announced their masterplan without a stadium included on its site, but it is felt inside Chelsea there are enough acres spare to still find a solution.

While we must stress no final decision has been made, sources speaking anonymously have suggested that is seen as a logical option, even if it would require securing permission from the Chelsea Pitch Owners, who hold the freehold of their current home. No proposal has been put to the CPO to date. The Chelsea Supporters Trust add there has been no substantial progress.

But relocating is seen by some inside Chelsea as the more feasible solution for pursuing rather than forcing the team to temporarily relocate elsewhere.

Sources have suggested they estimate the club would need to play their home fixtures at Wembley Stadium for seven to eight years if they were to raze and rebuild Stamford Bridge due to how complicated it would be as a construction.

Sources close to Clearlake suggest they have ruled out remodelling Stamford Bridge, a stand-by-stand gradual upgrade not being seen as worthwhile

Chelsea have not officially committed to one option over the other as of yet. While we do not see it publicly, architectural plans have been worked on privately for both possibilities.

Clearlake sources say their objective is choosing the correct long-term solution for the club and its future generations, rather than simply opting for the quickest option. But supporters would not be against seeing some form of progress now they have clarity over who is at the helm.

CHELSEA NOT IN FOR ‘KID MESSI’

The links between JJ Gabriel and Chelsea were natural. One is a tremendous young talent. The other is a club that have spent the last few years chasing tremendous young talents.

However, Chelsea say they are not in for the 15-year-old sensation who has been nicknamed 'Kid Messi’ and has officially told Manchester United he wants to leave them.

It is also worth remembering the Blues were hit with a nine-month academy transfer ban in March. That restriction applies to youth players previously registered with another Premier League or EFL club. It does not apply to Chelsea’s current players, international players, players who are registering on professional terms, or players who are applying for their first registration at Under-9 level.

Speaking of Under 9s, Confidential was told a story this week when we called a former coach of Gabriel’s for the lowdown on him and his father, Joe O’Cearuill, who has found himself being crucified by United supporters on social media.

We were told Chelsea were among those interested in securing Gabriel, who was clearly on a pathway towards potential stardom even from such a young age.

O’Cearuill insisted on having a meeting with Neil Bath, formerly the senior figure within the Blues’ famous academy. It was arranged. Then, for whatever reason, Gabriel’s old man did not make the meeting. He missed it, and it is said Bath did not take kindly to that. Chelsea did not then bring Gabriel in, and, according to sources, they will not be doing so now if and when he departs United.

Chelsea say they are not in for 15-year-old sensation JJ Gabriel, who has been nicknamed 'Kid Messi’ and has officially told Manchester United he wants to leave them

HOW HENDERSON HAS IMPRESSED WHILE SIDELINED

Jordan Henderson is finally closing in on making a Chelsea matchday squad, having joined the main sessions under Xabi Alonso after a month of modified training.

Henderson, who still has protective strapping on his left arm, which he broke after a freak accident at the World Cup, has been considered in the final stages of his recovery since last week.

With Chelsea facing a Friday night trip to Brentford – the club that honoured a gentlemen’s agreement to let him leave on a free in the summer – Confidential spoke to several Cobham sources to better understand Henderson and his behind-the-scenes behaviour while sidelined.

They were highly complimentary, describing him as ‘a standards driver’, ‘the last to leave’, and ‘obsessed’ (in a good way).

Their stories included how, upon signing from Brentford while his Chelsea team-mates were still on their pre-season tour of Australia and Asia, Henderson immediately began using the gym at the training ground as he awaited the squad’s return.

His arm injury has held him back, but the 36-year-old midfielder knew he was brought in to assist off the pitch as well as on it. That is why, while restricted from playing, he has insisted on attending every game, home and away, to remain tied to the team.

Henderson knew he was walking into a young changing room, and younger players can be reluctant to take any issues they may have upstairs. That is seen as one of his responsibilities. He can relate to Chelsea's younger charges, having been where they are once upon a time, and it is said he strives to get the best out of and for them.

Jordan Henderson is finally closing in on making a Chelsea matchday squad, having joined the main sessions under Xabi Alonso after a month of modified training

Henderson has been described by sources as ‘a standards driver’, ‘the last to leave’, and ‘obsessed’ (in a good way)

Much like with Danny Welbeck, who was known personally by Paul Winstanley and Sam Jewell, Henderson had an advocate in Dave Fallows when he was signed. Formerly of Liverpool, Fallows joined Chelsea as their fifth sporting director last November, with sources saying one of his areas of responsibility is in the character checks conducted on potential signings.

They did not need to do a deep dive into Henderson’s background with Fallows knowing the discipline and experience he would add. Likewise, Bryce Cavanagh, who is in charge of Chelsea's medical department and formerly of the England national team, was able to vouch for him.

Yet all of Chelsea's sporting directors knew of Henderson and his reputation as a leader, and Alonso says he has been appreciative of that, too. Now all that is left is for him to make his debut.

DR… WHO?

Readers of this column may recall how the secret-gated entrance into Cobham is now considered off-limits after Willie Isa kicked up a fuss at some unknowns getting a glimpse of training.

Well, that made for an awkward moment last Friday when Cavanagh, whose official title with Chelsea is director of performance, tried to use it to avoid going the long way around.

Security over the tannoy would not open up for Cavanagh, who then had to try to explain that he is literally the man in charge of the medical department.

The secret-gated entrance into Cobham is now considered off-limits after Willie Isa (pictured) kicked up a fuss at some unknowns getting a glimpse of training

GARNACHO GETTING NO GAME TIME

Neither Aston Villa nor Chelsea have divulged how many appearances are required for the conditional obligation in Alejandro Garnacho’s loan deal to be triggered. There is a secrecy surrounding the particulars of that clause with sources not willing to reveal it just yet.

When Garnacho joined Villa, Chelsea insiders said they did not expect to see the winger again, claiming the obligation was easily achievable. Whatever the magic number, the start to this season will be making for some uncomfortable viewing within his parent club.

Garnacho was an unused substitute in the Carabao Cup away at Coventry last night – and that was the third game in succession that he has stayed sat on Villa’s bench.

Before that, he was brought on in the 86th, 78th and 75th minutes. He has yet to start a match.

Harvey Elliott’s loan with Villa from Liverpool last season also had what was described as an achievable conditional obligation – and that was for him to make 10 Premier League appearances. It was not triggered. Even that number seems a long way away for Garnacho presently.

Alejandro Garnacho's loan at Aston Villa has got off to a disappointing start

ALONSO TO REVEAL JOAO PEDRO NEWS

Xabi Alonso will provide an update on Joao Pedro today at his pre-Brentford press conference, though he did receive treatment for a left knee issue during last week's 2-2 draw with Hull.

Chelsea declined to comment when asked about his withdrawal from the upcoming international break for Brazil, who said it was due to him being ‘injured’.

Joao Pedro's camp likewise did not respond to requests for guidance.

If he is unable to face Brentford, Welbeck is likely to lead the line.

CITY BEMUSED BY CHELSEA CLAIMS

Manchester City won 1-0 with 10 men at Manchester United and that was largely thanks to Enzo Fernandez, who was hugely impressive in his winding-up mission at Old Trafford.

There has been amusement in City circles over the last week at the noises continuing to come out of Chelsea regarding their £125million sale of Fernandez on deadline day.

Chelsea insiders claimed last Friday: that Fernandez told them that his relationship with his team-mates was broken and beyond repair; that he revealed how he had remained in continuous contact with Enzo Maresca ever since the Italian’s acrimonious exit from Chelsea; that he submitted two written transfer requests as he pushed to leave for City.

But City are somewhat bemused as to why these revelations are coming out now, given Alonso praised Fernandez’s professionalism previously and that the Argentinian was handed the captain’s armband in Chelsea’s final friendly before the season started.

CHELSEA TOLD GABRIEL DID NOT DESERVE RED

Chelsea have been told that Arsenal centre back Gabriel did not deserve a red card for kicking Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez in the head during their 2-1 loss two weeks ago.

Arsenal defender Gabriel kicked goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez in the head in Chelsea's loss at the Emirates - but the Blues have been told he did not deserve a red card

That is via the five-man Key Match Incidents panel who are tasked with reviewing the major refereeing decisions each weekend. The report is distributed to the clubs involved weekly.

The panel concluded, by a unanimous score of 5-0, that Gabriel did nothing wrong.

A fair few within Chelsea disagree, but the KMI report states: ‘The panel unanimously supported the referee’s call of no red card. Multiple players were on the ground competing and challenging for the loose ball, and the action of Gabriel was not deemed to be an act of violent conduct or serious foul play.’

Sports.title: Aussie HYROX athlete apologises after soiling herself during competition that sparked uproar around the world - as she reveals she's forfeited her win
Sports.content:
Aussie HYROX athlete apologises after soiling herself during competition that sparked uproar around the world - as she reveals she's forfeited her win

Australian HYROX athlete Joanna Wietrzyk has issued a public apology following her win in an endurance event in Beijing – after she soiled herself during the race.

The 24-year-old, from Melbourne, refused to drop out of the event despite streams of faeces running down her legs as she powered to victory during the gruelling competition last Saturday.

Wietrzyk's decision to push on sparked ferocious criticism of the organisers for allowing her to continue competing.

The Australian athlete issued a statement today apologising to other competitors and revealing she had forfeited her win at the event.

She wrote on Instagram: 'I want to offer my sincere apology to the people of China, my fellow competitors, the spectators and the HYROX organizers for what happened during the race in Beijing.

'I felt completely fit and healthy at the start of the race, with no reason to expect any illness.

'Looking back, I regret the decision to not have stepped off the track. I recognize that I should have made a different choice.

'I take responsibility for my decision to continue and am deeply sorry for the discomfort and disruption it caused.'

Australian HYROX athlete Joanna Wietrzyk (above) issued an apology on Thursday after refusing to quit a competition despite soiling herself on Saturday

Wietrzyk (above) forfeited her win at the event and apologised to other competitors

Wietrzyk said she had thought about the incident and was 'genuinely sorry to everyone who was affected'.

'I am learning from this experience and will carry those lessons with me, including remembering that there is more to life than racing and knowing when it is right to step away,' she wrote.

'On reflection, I have decided to retroactively withdraw from the race and forfeit the points I earned.'

The Melbourne athlete then thanked those who supported her during the days of backlash following the event.

'Thank you to those standing by me, both as an athlete and as a person, during this time, and to everyone who has reached out with kindness and support,' Wietrzyk wrote.

'It means more to me than I can properly express right now. I will be taking some time to recover, reflect and look after myself and my family, away from the noise.'

Daily Mail previously revealed major sponsor Puma had distanced itself from the athlete by scrubbing references to her from its various country websites.

The incident on Saturday also prompted HYROX co-founder Moritz Fürste to issue a personal statement pledging to implement immediate rule changes.

Massive backlash from the incident (above) prompted HYROX co-founder Moritz Fürste to issue a personal statement pledging to implement immediate rule changes

Prior to the weekend's incident, official event rules punished athletes for minor infringements such as littering on the course or clearing their nose on the floor, but there were no rules relating to faecal matter.

Wietrzyk's statement drew hundreds of comments within minutes of being uploaded.

Commenters were deeply divided on whether the apology was sincere or the result of public pressure.

'This apology is just not good enough, not least because it has come far too late ... Truly terrible sportsmanship putting your fellow athletes' health at serious risk, never mind the spectators and volunteers,' one wrote.

'Hindsight is a wonderful thing but during that moment nobody knows exactly how they would have reacted,' another said.

'A real person would've apologised the same day. Not almost a week later,' another added.

'True actions of a fighter, not many people understand the mindset of the best in the world,' a fourth said.

Wietrzyk turned off comments under the statement, as well as on her other posts, within an hour of sharing it.

Wietrzyk initially made a post saying 'a win is a win' after the HYROX event

Commenters under the apology from Wietrzyk (above) were divided over whether it was delivered too late

The Melbourne athlete had initially shared a post following her accident declaring 'a win is a win' but later removed it and refused to publicly comment on the situation.

Her coach, Chris Bayens, shared a statement on Monday calling out 'hatred and personal attacks' on Wietrzyk.

'The mental health of athletes is shaped far more by the community around them, and right now that community should take a hard look at itself,' Bayens wrote.

'No one is perfect, not in sport, not on social media, not in real life. What happened was extraordinary. The hatred that has followed is ugly.'

Bayens vowed to continue supporting her and stressed that no one was prepared for what happened and that the decision to continue was made on the fly.

'Decisions were made under competition conditions by an athlete, judges and officials, all responding to a situation none of them could reasonably have prepared for,' he said.

'It is very easy to construct the perfect response once the moment has passed. Hindsight gives people time, information and distance that simply did not exist for those actually living it.

'Those decisions can be reviewed and lessons can be taken from them. But judging someone's intent, character or morality through the clarity of hindsight is neither fair nor honest.'

Her coach Chris Bayens has leapt to her defence, accusing critics of spreading negativity

Prior to Wietrzyk's accident, HYROX had no rules relating to faecal matter

Bayens followed the statement with a more comical take on the situation on Wednesday, writing: 'I had a few things on my Bingo card for the 2026-27 HYROX season.

This was absolutely not one of them. I was hoping for a slightly smoother start.'

-

Sports.title: 'Traumatised' Steve Smith moans he was 'thrown to the wolves' after sandpaper scandal
Sports.content:
'Traumatised' Steve Smith moans he was 'thrown to the wolves' after sandpaper scandal

Australia batsman Steve Smith was slapped with a 12-month ban after being found responsible for the 2018 sandpapergate scandal and has bitter memories of what followed

View 3 Images Steve Smith is gearing up for a return to South Africa (Image: Code Sports)

Steve Smith has claimed that the events of sandpapergate have left him 'traumatised' - and has hit out at Cricket Australia for being 'thrown to the wolves'. Aussie star Smith was banned from international and domestic cricket for 12 months for his role in the ball-tampering scandal which marred his side's Test series against South Africa in 2018.

‌



The batsman was stripped of the captaincy while ex-team-mates David Warner and Cameron Bancroft also received lengthy bans. Smith, now vice-captain to Pat Cummins, has been reflecting on sandpapergate ahead of Australia's first Test series back in South Africa since the incident.

‌



During an interview with News Corp, Smith confessed: "I'm not a big fan of cameras, I get anxious around cameras. That was a traumatic experience in my life and when I hear the flash of a camera it makes me revisit that, in a way."

‌



The 37-year-old went on to say: "The 24-48 hours after being told by James Sutherland (then Cricket Australia chief executive) that I was getting banned for a year, going through the airport in Johannesburg getting absolutely mobbed, and then flying back and doing that press conference...

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Kevin Pietersen handed shock England return 12 years on from brutal squad axe READ MORE :

"I still have little flashbacks here and there of it. I felt like I was kind of thrown to the wolves through [Johannesburg] airport. I didn't have any support there at all.

‌



"It was certainly a difficult period, particularly the initial few days after. "The mental state I was in was not great. That's somewhere I'd like not to get to again, but I certainly learned from that and have been able to move forward with my life.

Was Steve Smith's punishment the right one? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Steve Smith was mobbed by cameras in the Johannesburg airport (Image: GULSHAN KHAN/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



"I've tried to kind of erase a lot of 2018 and what happened. I can't remember a lot about the series. I've tried to block most of it out of my memory bank."

Smith is no stranger to hostile receptions from crowds, having returned to South Africa for a white-ball series in 2020. "It's something I'm kind of used to," he explained.

"I've copped a lot at times away from home, at different venues across my career, and it's something that I take in my own stride. I use it as motivation to try and go out and do well, and try and take a positive from it."

Article continues below

View 3 Images Steve Smith held a teary press conference once he arrived in Sydney (Image: PETER PARKS/AFP via Getty Images)

Smith's comments came shortly after he revealed that he isn't sure whether he'll feature in next summer's Ashes in England. He'll be 38 when the five-match series rolls around and recently told the Telegraph: "I don't even know if I'll be there yet.

"I'm kind of a series-by-series proposition, as I've been for a while. That's still a fair way away for me right now. I'd love to win [an Ashes in England] but you wait and see if that comes to fruition."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel dealt fresh England injury blow ahead of naming squad on Friday
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel dealt fresh England injury blow ahead of naming squad on Friday

Thomas Tuchel will announce his squad for England's Nations League games against Spain, Czechia and Croatia on Friday, but John Stones is a major doubt due to injury

View 2 Images John Stones joined Inter Milan this summer (Image: Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

England are likely to be without John Stones for their upcoming Nations League matches. Stones, 32, suffered a thigh injury while in action for new club Inter Milan earlier this week.

‌



The centre-back is unlikely to be named in Thomas Tuchel's squad which will be announced at 10am on Friday. Stones started three of England's eight games at the World Cup, including their quarter-final win against Norway and semi-final defeat to Argentina before sitting out the third-place play-off victory over France.

‌



Having been released by Manchester City in June, the ex-Everton star moved abroad for the first time in his career. But Stones had to be substituted an hour into his first start for the Italian giants, who beat Udinese 5-3 at San Siro on Monday.

‌



The 32-year-old is now set for a period on the sidelines which will see him miss England's four Nations League fixtures over the two-week international break. Inter confirmed: "John Stones underwent clinical and diagnostic tests this morning at the Istituto Humanitas in Rozzano.

"The tests revealed a muscle strain to the flexor muscles in his left thigh. His condition will be reassessed over the coming days."

According to reports, Inter hope to have Stones available when they host Parma in Serie A on October 10. Their next fixture is away to Roma this Saturday, with both sides having taken maximum points from their opening four games.

Tuchel, meanwhile, will be forced to call up and alternative in Stones' absence. Marc Guehi, Ezri Konsa, Jarell Quansah, Trevoh Chalobah and Dan Burn were England's other centre-back options at the World cup.

‌



Which defender needs to be called up instead of John Stones? Have your say in the comments section.

The Three Lions only kept two clean sheets in North America, although they managed to achieve their best finish at a World Cup since 1966. Tuchel's focus has switched to the Nations League, with England drawn in Group 3 alongside Spain, Czechia and Croatia.

Article continues below

England start their campaign at home to world champions Spain before trips to Czechia and Croatia. They'll then play Czechia again at Wembley to round out the extended international window.

For their final two group games in November, they'll welcome Croatia before travelling to Spain. A top-two finish would see them advance to the knockout stage in March, while finishing third would see them at risk of being relegated to League B via the play-offs. Should England finish fourth, relegation will be automatic.

Sports.title: Todd Boehly's colourful legacy will raise a laugh - but not from Chelsea supporters
Sports.content:
Todd Boehly's colourful legacy will raise a laugh - but not from Chelsea supporters

The American has sold his stake in the Premier League club after four years in the boardroom and leaves behind a history of big spending and long contracts

View 3 Images Todd Boehly has ended his association with Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Todd Boehly, it seems, will enjoy a ‘small profit’ from the sale of his stake in Chelsea Football Club. It is hard not to laugh.

‌



To be fair, Boehly has provided amusement during his four years at Stamford Bridge. His answer to the complex issue of financial arrangements with the English Football League and the tiers below?

‌



“You could have a North versus South all-star game for the Premier League. That would fund whatever the pyramid needed very easily.”

‌



Brilliant. And then there was the time Ruud Gullit introduced himself to the Chelsea chairman.

“What do you do?” asked Boehly. With such an in-depth knowledge of the game, it was no wonder Boehly liked to visit the dressing-room in the immediate aftermath of a fixture.

Chelsea make huge announcement as Todd Boehly steps down as chairman READ MORE :

“Todd comes to the changing room every game,” former Chelsea keeper Kepa Arrizabalaga said. “He had different chats with us after different games.”

‌



Goodness knows what those chats were about. He might have tried to explain Chelsea’s transfer policy but that would have taken more than a few minutes after a match.

Where do you start with Chelsea’s recruitment under Boehly? When Boehly installed himself as interim sporting director in 2022, one of the first things he did was sign Raheem Sterling for a fee of £50million on a five-year deal which paid the player £325,000 a week.

And in the context of Boehly’s contractual dealings, that five-year deal was a short-term agreement. In January 2023, Chelsea paid £70million for Mykhailo Mudryk. They gave the Ukrainian an eight-and-a-half year deal.

‌



And we know how it has gone for those two players. In just over four years of Boehly’s involvement, the club has signed 65 players with an outlay of around £2billion.

View 3 Images Raheem Sterling was signed by Chelsea when Todd Boehly was the interim sporting director (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Billionaire bottle-jobs, as Gary Neville once said. At least Boehly was refreshingly honest about his shortcomings.

‌



At a conference earlier this year, he reflected: “I was stuck being interim sporting director for the summer having no idea what made a good football player. But knowing that Marc Cucurella, if Manchester City want him, I want him. It was really simple that way.”

Really simple. After finishing tenth last season, Chelsea do not have European football on their current agenda. They have won two of their four Premier League games this season.

“I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success,” said Boehly in a statement about his departure. Well positioned? If you include interim managers Frank Lampard and Calum McFarlane, Chelsea are playing under their EIGHTH manager in four years.

‌



Goodness knows what the compensation payments come to. Enough to pay up Mudryk’s contract, possibly.

View 3 Images Behdad Eghbali became the most influential co-owner but Todd Boehly had an input into managerial appointments at Chelsea (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

After eight months in his post, Graham Potter received a pay-off of £13million. And what was the Liam Rosenior appointment all about?

‌



To be fair, after his initial six months as a sort of sporting director, Boehly’s influence in Chelsea’s strategy might not have been as strong as some people imagined. But he was still a key figure in a period of time when Chelsea lost any sense of identity.

They were pilloried by Neville, but he was far from alone. Boehly has always seemed to be quite an affable character.

He clearly loved being involved in Chelsea. And he brought new owners to the club when the future was uncertain.

Article continues below

So, good on him and good luck to him. But on a list of chairmen who don’t really understand the game, he was right up there.

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho's telling post about JJ Gabriel suggests Man Utd have dodged a bullet
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho's telling post about JJ Gabriel suggests Man Utd have dodged a bullet

OPINION: Alejandro Garnacho may have just proven why Manchester United shouldn't worry about losing wantaway wonderkid JJ Gabriel

View 5 Images JJ Gabriel wants out of Manchester United (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Fifteen is an age usually reserved for stressing over GCSE mocks and applying acne cream. JJ Gabriel, however, operates on a somewhat loftier plane of self-importance.

‌



Manchester United's latest academy messiah has formally requested to leave the club. Gabriel is, by all accounts, a generational talent, but would losing him for nothing really be as catastrophic as it sounds?

‌



On the face of it, the answer is a shuddering yes. Gabriel is an absurdly gifted footballer, a boy who glides through midfield with the kind of precocious, disrespectful ease that makes defenders contemplate early retirement. But behind the highlight reels lies a grimly familiar theatre: whispers of a gargantuan ego and a kid convinced the world owes him a throne before he's even old enough to drive.

‌



Enter Alejandro Garnacho. Never a man to let a piece of self-involved drama pass him by, the former United starlet waded directly into the fray.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Roy Keane tells Man Utd exactly what to do after JJ Gabriel exit threat READ MORE :

Taking to TikTok - the modern footballer's equivalent of a press conference - Garnacho reposted a video appearing to defend the wantaway United youngster.

‌



It featured screenshots of the reports surrounding Gabriel's exit, adorned with the caption: "JJ Gabriel wanting to leave Man Utd after being called one of the greatest talents itw [in the world]... and he's rumoured to join other big clubs... where have we seen this before?" This was, of course, followed by a montage of some of Garnacho's goals in red.

It was a fascinating, if entirely oblivious, piece of digital solidarity. It's just a re-post, but Garnacho is clearly drawing parallels between himself and Gabriel. Both highly-rated Carrington graduates. Both apparently misunderstood by the rigid, joyless adults in the room. Both destined for bigger and better things, apparently.

View 5 Images Alejandro Garnacho reposted the clip on TikTok (Image: TikTok)

‌



But if the Argentinian genuinely sees himself in JJ Gabriel, then Manchester United shouldn't just open the door for the 15-year-old, they should order him an Uber, pack his sandwiches, and wave him off with a big smile.

Let's answer Garnacho's rhetorical question. Where have we seen this before? We saw it last year, when his relationship with Ruben Amorim deteriorated over disciplinary concerns and a failure to meet the manager's tactical demands. Garnacho did little to repair the damage, and United eventually sold him to Chelsea for well below his market value at the time.

And how has that grand pursuit of greener pastures worked out? Not especially well. Garnacho arrived at Chelsea with plenty to prove but made next to no impact - wandering through matches with the gloomy detachment of a teenager dragged along to a garden party. For all the talk of his enormous self-belief, there was precious little evidence of it, with Garnacho producing nothing but a series of low-wattage, utterly forgettable cameos.

‌



View 5 Images Alejandro Garnacho's TikTok re-post speaks volumes (Image: Getty)

Twelve months after taking him off United's hands for a cut-price fee, Chelsea threw up their hands and offloaded the winger at the first whiff of buyer's remorse. Now parked on loan at Aston Villa, Garnacho is discovering that changing his postcode has done little to change his fortunes. The same sense of inertia that dogged him at Old Trafford and at Stamford Bridge has simply packed its bags and followed him up the M6.

On Wednesday night, Garnacho was once again an unused substitute as Villa faced Coventry in the League Cup. He sat on the bench, presumably pondering his own greatness, while a team of, let's be honest, Championship players ran around in front of him - an image that sums it up perfectly.

‌



If Gabriel is cut from the same cloth as Garnacho - disruptive, arrogant and entitled - then United aren't suffering a tragedy so much as dodging a bullet. Talent can only take you so far. Being a technical wizard with a stratospheric ceiling is one thing; having the application, humility and hunger to learn is quite another. Plenty of prodigies have dazzled at 15 only to discover that potential means very little if the attitude doesn't match it.

View 5 Images Garnacho struggled to make an impact at Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

By kicking up such an entitled fuss before he's even legally allowed to buy a Red Bull, Gabriel is teetering dangerously close to the Ravel Morrison precipice. Morrison was another United prodigy blessed with extraordinary ability, only for off-field chaos and a troublesome entourage to help smother his potential. He became a tragic monument to one of the most frustrating questions in football: just how good could he have been?

‌



Gabriel urgently needs a dose of reality. He needs to shut out the noise, pull up his socks, and concentrate on playing football. That means dropping the off-field posturing and forgetting about which European giant might offer him and his father the most lucrative signing-on fee.

Manchester United clearly rate him. The pathway to the first team is right there in front of him. If Gabriel really is as special as those around him insist, his football will do the talking soon enough. Keep working, keep learning and, before long, he could be knocking on the door of the senior squad.

View 5 Images JJ Gabriel is one of the most highly-rated youngsters in Europe (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



But kicking up a storm like this at 15 is a grim omen. Whether this attitude is coming from the boy himself or the people whispering in his ear, it's a glaring red flag, one that raises questions about whether his temperament will match his jaw-dropping talent.

Having your bridge-burning rebellion rubber-stamped by Alejandro Garnacho - one of the most exhaustingly self-involved figures in United's recent history - is not a flex, nor a seal of quality. It's a high-decibel warning siren. When a walking cautionary tale becomes your spiritual cheerleader, you haven't arrived - you've lost the plot.

United shouldn't spend another second wringing their hands over Gabriel's grand exit. They should simply open the door, wave him off, and quietly count their blessings. Because if this is how the story starts, perhaps the best thing United can do is make sure they aren't around for the ending.
