MEXICO · LIFE & CULTURE, 17 SEPTEMBER 2026

Key Facts —The season — Día de Muertos runs 1–2 November, but Mexico City’s events fill the last two weeks of October. —Grand Parade — The 10th Desfile de Día de Muertos is confirmed for Saturday 31 October, free, expected to run from Chapultepec down Paseo de la Reforma to the Zócalo. —Catrinas — The Mega Procesión de Catrinas takes over Reforma on Sunday 25 October at 18:00, from the Ángel de la Independencia to the Zócalo. —Alebrijes — The Monumental Alebrijes Parade opens the season on Saturday 17 October at noon, Zócalo to the Ángel; the figures stay on Reforma until 8 November. —2026 theme — The Grand Parade honors Mexican icons Juan Gabriel, Lola Beltrán and José Alfredo Jiménez, alongside pre-Hispanic roots and folk art. —Heritage — Día de Muertos has been UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage since 2008.

Day of the Dead in Mexico City 2026 is three weekends of parades, ofrendas and marigolds — from the Alebrijes on 17 October to the Grand Parade on 31 October and the cemetery vigils of 1–2 November. This is the expat guide to doing it right.

The Confirmed Calendar, Weekend by Weekend

Saturday 17 October — Monumental Alebrijes Parade. The season opens at 12:00 in the Zócalo, as the giant fantastical creatures of Mexican folk art march to the Ángel de la Independencia. The alebrijes then stay on display along Paseo de la Reforma until 8 November — a free open-air gallery for three weeks.

Sunday 25 October — Mega Procesión de Catrinas. From 18:00, hundreds of elegantly dressed skeletons — pre-Hispanic, classic, circus and illuminated catrinas — walk from the Ángel de la Independencia to the Zócalo. It is the most photogenic night of the season; arrive early and dress warm.

Saturday 31 October — Gran Desfile de Día de Muertos. The tenth edition of the big one: floats, comparsas and giant figures honoring Juan Gabriel, Lola Beltrán, José Alfredo Jiménez and Blanca Estela Pavón, with sections on pre-Hispanic death mythology and popular folk art. The parade is free; the traditional route runs from Puerta de los Leones in Chapultepec Park along Reforma to the Zócalo, with exact times confirmed by the city closer to the date.

1–2 November — The days themselves. Ofrendas fill homes, markets and public squares; the most moving experience is Mixquic in the city’s southeast, where the cemetery glows with candles through the night of 1 November.

Why 2026 Is a Special Year

Mexico City has been living with Día de Muertos all year: a special World Cup edition of the parade ran down Reforma in June, when the capital welcomed football fans with catrinas and marigolds. The October season is the real thing — and after the World Cup spotlight, the city expects record visitor numbers.

The parade itself is young: Mexico City invented it in 2016, inspired by the fictional sequence in the James Bond film Spectre. A decade on, it draws millions and has become the country’s biggest single public spectacle.

How to Do It as an Expat: Practical Notes

Where to stand. For the Grand Parade, the stretch of Reforma between the Diana Cazadora and the Ángel offers the best sightlines; opposite Bellas Artes works for the final approach. Arrive at least an hour early — the city closes the route to traffic and the metro gets packed.

Getting around. Use the metro and Metrobús, not cars: Reforma and the Centro Histórico close for hours on parade days. Rideshare surge pricing after the events is extreme.

What to bring. Comfortable shoes, water, a light jacket for the evening events, and patience — crowds at the Zócalo can exceed a million on parade day.

Respect the tradition. Ofrendas and cemetery vigils are family rituals, not performances. In Mixquic and San Andrés, ask before photographing people at gravesides.

Beyond the Parades

The season stacks with the city’s biggest autumn weekends: the Formula 1 Mexico City Grand Prix runs 30 October–1 November at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, and Corona Capital follows on 20–22 November — three consecutive reasons to be in the capital this fall.

FAQ

When is the Day of the Dead parade in Mexico City 2026?

The Gran Desfile de Día de Muertos is confirmed for Saturday 31 October 2026, free to attend, expected to run from Chapultepec Park along Paseo de la Reforma to the Zócalo.

What dates are Day of the Dead in Mexico?

Día de Muertos is celebrated on 1–2 November, but Mexico City’s parades and events run from 17 October through early November.

Is the Mexico City Day of the Dead parade free?

Yes. The Grand Parade, the Mega Procesión de Catrinas and the Alebrijes Parade are all free, and the alebrijes remain on display along Reforma until 8 November.

What is the Mega Procesión de Catrinas 2026?

A night procession of hundreds of costumed catrinas on Sunday 25 October 2026, from the Ángel de la Independencia to the Zócalo, starting at 18:00.

Where is the best place to experience Day of the Dead in Mexico City?

For the parades, along Paseo de la Reforma; for the traditional vigils, the cemetery of Mixquic on the night of 1 November.

The Bottom Line Three parades, two sacred nights and one unforgettable city: Mexico City’s Day of the Dead 2026 runs 17 October to 2 November — book your stay now, because the whole world is coming.

MUSIC · AWARDS, 17 SEPTEMBER 2026

Key Facts —The show — The 27th Annual Latin Grammy Awards take place Thursday 12 November 2026 at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, live on Univision. —The nominations — Announced 16 September: Anitta’s Equilibrivm is up for Album of the Year, against Karol G, CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso and more. —Record of the Year — Rosalía’s La Perla, Karol G & Marco Antonio Solís, CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, Jorge Drexler and Carín León lead the field. —Brazil’s angle — A new category, Best Portuguese Language Urban Album, debuts this year — a structural win for Brazilian music. —Calendar — Final voting runs 1–12 October; the Person of the Year gala is 11 November, the eve of the main show.

The Latin Grammy Awards 2026 nominations are out — and Anitta is in the biggest race of the night. Brazil’s biggest pop export competes for Album of the Year when the 27th edition of the awards airs from Las Vegas on 12 November.

Anitta’s Album of the Year Run

Equilibrivm, Anitta’s most ambitious record to date, is one of nine nominees for Album of the Year — the category that defines the night. It is the Rio-born singer’s highest-stakes nomination yet at the Latin Grammys, and it lands in a field that reads like a map of where Latin music went in 2026.

Her competition: Karol G’s Tropicoqueta, CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso’s Free Spirits, Jorge Drexler’s Taracá, Mon Laferte’s Femme Fatale, Carín León’s Muda, Silvana Estrada’s Vendrán Suaves Lluvias, Milo J’s La Vida Era Más Corta and Rawayana’s ¿Dónde Es El After?.

Anitta has carried Brazilian funk onto the world’s biggest stages for a decade — but a top-prize Latin Grammy has so far eluded her. Her 2023 Grammy breakthrough nomination proved the global academy was watching; 12 November decides whether the Latin one crowns her.

The Big Categories at a Glance

Record of the Year pits Rosalía’s La Perla against Karol G and Marco Antonio Solís’s Coleccionando Heridas, CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso’s Ha Ha, Jorge Drexler’s ¿Cómo Se Ama?, Carín León’s Desde Que Te Tengo, Mon Laferte’s Femme Fatale, Silvana Estrada’s Dime, Milo J’s Niño and Loulu Gilberto’s O Amor Nos Encontrou.

Argentina’s CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso are the night’s crossover story, appearing in both general-field categories — a year after their breakout swept the region’s conversation.

Brazil’s Structural Win: A New Portuguese-Language Category

Beyond Anitta, the 2026 awards bring a change that matters more for Brazilian music in the long run: the old Best Portuguese Language Urban Performance category becomes a full album category — Best Portuguese Language Urban Album.

It is the academy’s acknowledgment that Brazilian urban music — funk, trap, hip-hop — now competes at album depth, not just single level. After Caetano Veloso and Maria Bethânia’s Grammy win earlier this year, Brazil’s institutional momentum in the US academies is real.

Key Dates and How to Watch

Final-round voting runs from 1 to 12 October among the academy’s voting members. The special-awards ceremony and Person of the Year gala take place during Latin Grammy Week in Las Vegas, with the Person of the Year gala on 11 November.

The main show airs live on Univision on Thursday 12 November from the MGM Grand Garden Arena — the same venue that hosted the 2025 edition. Additional broadcast partners for Brazil will be announced closer to the date.

FAQ

When are the Latin Grammy Awards 2026?

The 27th Annual Latin Grammy Awards take place on Thursday 12 November 2026 at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, airing live on Univision.

Is Anitta nominated for a Latin Grammy in 2026?

Yes. Anitta’s album Equilibrivm is nominated for Album of the Year, the night’s top prize, against Karol G, CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, Jorge Drexler and others.

Who is nominated for Record of the Year at the 2026 Latin Grammys?

Nominees include Rosalía (La Perla), Karol G & Marco Antonio Solís (Coleccionando Heridas), CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso (Ha Ha), Jorge Drexler, Carín León and Mon Laferte.

What is new at the Latin Grammys 2026?

The awards introduce Best Portuguese Language Urban Album, upgrading the former performance category to full album level — a structural boost for Brazilian urban music.

Where can I watch the Latin Grammys 2026?

The show airs live on Univision in the US; Brazilian broadcast partners are announced closer to 12 November.

The Bottom Line Anitta goes for Album of the Year on 12 November — and win or lose, Brazil already scored the bigger prize: a permanent album category for Portuguese-language urban music.

BRAZIL · FESTIVALS, 17 SEPTEMBER 2026

Key Facts —Dates and venue — Primavera Sound São Paulo 2026 runs Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 December at the Interlagos racetrack, the Autódromo José Carlos Pace. —Headliners — Gorillaz and The Strokes top the bill, with FKA twigs and Lily Allen performing her album West End Girl in full. —The bill — Also Yung Lean, CMAT, Courtney Barnett, Cara Delevingne, Nation of Language, Mannequin Pussy, Black Pantera, Gaby Amarantos and more. —Tickets — Sold via the Ingresse platform in day and two-day formats; the festival is strictly 16+. —The comeback — Third São Paulo edition after 2022 and 2023, returning after a two-year pause. —Sister festival — The same lineup plays Primavera Sound Buenos Aires on 28–29 November, one week earlier.

Primavera Sound São Paulo 2026 closes the Southern Hemisphere festival season on 5–6 December: Gorillaz, The Strokes, FKA twigs and Lily Allen lead the Barcelona-born festival’s return to Interlagos — and for expats in Brazil, it is the last great weekend of the year.

Primavera Sound São Paulo 2026: The Lineup

The 2026 bill is the strongest the festival has brought to Brazil. Gorillaz and The Strokes headline both days, closing a South American run that also takes in Primavera Sound Buenos Aires on 28–29 November.

FKA twigs makes her long-awaited Latin American debut, and Lily Allen performs her breakup album West End Girl in its entirety — her first shows in Brazil in more than fifteen years.

The depth is vintage Primavera: Yung Lean, CMAT and Courtney Barnett in their first Latin American appearances, plus underscores, Danny L Harle, Nation of Language, This Is Lorelei, Mannequin Pussy, Model/Actriz, Smerz, Machine Girl and John Talabot. Cara Delevingne appears with a music set.

Brazil is not a footnote: Black Pantera, Gaby Amarantos, Gab Ferreira and Duquesa carry the national flag across the weekend’s stages.

Tickets and What to Expect

Tickets for Primavera Sound São Paulo 2026 are sold through Ingresse, the festival’s official platform, in single-day and two-day formats. Demand has been strong since the lineup dropped in May — the festival’s first edition after the 2024 cancellation sold its early tiers within weeks.

The event is strictly 16+. Inside the racetrack infield, expect multiple stages, food halls and the long walks between sets that define the Interlagos experience — the same grounds that host the Formula 1 São Paulo Grand Prix four weeks earlier.

December evenings in São Paulo are warm but prone to summer storms: a light rain jacket is the veteran move, and comfortable shoes are not optional.

Getting There and Where to Stay

Interlagos sits about 25 kilometers south of central São Paulo. The CPTM Line 9-Esmeralda to Autódromo station is the classic route; rideshare surge after the headliners is extreme, so the train is the smarter exit.

Stay near Pinheiros, Vila Madalena or along the Line 9 corridor for the easiest logistics. Early December is peak season — the same weekend as CCXP at São Paulo Expo — so book accommodation well ahead.

Why This Edition Matters

Primavera Sound’s return after two years away restores the anchor of São Paulo’s December calendar. Between this, CCXP and the Grand Prix, the city now owns the Southern Hemisphere’s strongest six-week run of international events — and the Gorillaz–Strokes double bill, weeks after their Corona Capital headline sets in Mexico City, confirms South America as a first-class stop on the global festival circuit.

When is Primavera Sound São Paulo 2026?

Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 December 2026, at the Interlagos racetrack (Autódromo José Carlos Pace) in São Paulo.

Who headlines Primavera Sound São Paulo 2026?

Gorillaz and The Strokes headline, with FKA twigs and Lily Allen — who performs her album West End Girl in full — plus Yung Lean, CMAT, Courtney Barnett and more.

Where can I buy Primavera Sound São Paulo 2026 tickets?

Tickets are sold via Ingresse, the festival’s official ticketing platform, in single-day and two-day formats.

Is there an age limit for Primavera Sound São Paulo?

Yes, the festival is strictly 16+.

How do I get to Interlagos for the festival?

The CPTM Line 9-Esmeralda train to Autódromo station is the fastest route; rideshare prices surge heavily after the headliners finish.

The Bottom Line Gorillaz, The Strokes and FKA twigs at Interlagos on 5–6 December — the strongest festival bill Brazil has seen in years, and the perfect close to the 2026 season.

World.title: Nicaragua Power Concentration Draws Sharp UN Criticism
World.content:
Nicaragua · Analysis

Key Facts — What happened Nicaragua faced sharp criticism at the United Nations Human Rights Council in Geneva on 16 September 2026.

— What the report covers The period from 15 June 2025 to 15 June 2026, in a study mandated by the Council itself.

— What the report counted 5,539 civil society entities dissolved in eight years, at least 56 media outlets closed, at least 46 people detained.

— The catch The latest reform still needs a second legislative reading, scheduled for January 2027, before it is ratified.

— When people next vote The reform would postpone elections to late 2028 and extend mandates from six years to seven.

— Who runs the country Daniel Ortega, 80, and Rosario Murillo, 75, hold a co-presidency created by the 2025 constitutional reform.

Volker Turk told the Human Rights Council in Geneva that the situation is utterly indefensible. A September reform extends mandates and delays the vote.

Managua. The United Nations human rights chief called the situation utterly indefensible.

Nicaragua power concentration drew unusually blunt language from the United Nations this week, in a report to the Human Rights Council. “The situation is utterly indefensible,” said Volker Turk, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.

He was presenting a report on Nicaragua to the Human Rights Council in Geneva on 16 September 2026. The Council itself had mandated the report.

What the report found

The document is titled “Human Rights Situation in Nicaragua”. It covers the period from 15 June 2025 to 15 June 2026.

Over the last eight years, 5,539 civil society entities have been arbitrarily dissolved. At least 56 media outlets have been closed.

At least 46 people were in arbitrary detention at the end of the period. There were at least eight ongoing cases of enforced disappearance and four deaths in State custody.

“There is almost no space for independent civic or political participation,” the report says. It adds that the State has extended repression against dissenting voices beyond the country’s borders.

Turk summarised the document in a single phrase. It traces “the near-total capture of State institutions by the ruling party”, he said.

He described a systematic abuse of power that has weakened institutional checks and balances. Most Nicaraguans, he said, are left without recourse in the face of human rights violations.

A further line from the report is equally direct. “Power is increasingly concentrated in the executive branch and the ruling party,” it states.

The Sandinista National Liberation Front, the governing party, holds all 153 municipalities. It also holds both Caribbean coast regional councils and the legislative majority.

“There is almost nothing left to shut down,” Turk said.

Managua. More than five thousand civil society organisations have been dissolved in eight years.

The 2025 reform that built Nicaragua power concentration

Nicaragua’s constitutional reform entered into force on Wednesday 19 February 2025, on publication in the official gazette La Gaceta. It created the office of co-president alongside the president.

Rosario Murillo, President Daniel Ortega’s wife and until then vice-president, took the new office. The presidential term went from five years to six.

The text states that the presidency directs the Government and coordinates the legislative, judicial, electoral, fiscal and autonomous bodies. It no longer shares power with them.

The presidency was also made Supreme Command of the Army, the National Police and the Ministry of Interior. The reform provided for state monitoring that media do not serve foreign interests or divulge false news.

In all, 148 of 198 constitutional articles were reformed and 37 were repealed. Among the repealed provisions was the prohibition against torture.

The September 2026 reform and the 2028 elections

On 1 and 2 September 2026 the National Assembly approved a further reform in first reading. It passed by unanimous show of hands at a special session in León.

It amends Article 47 to bar people designated “traidores a la patria” from standing for or holding public office. The phrase means traitors to the homeland.

At least 452 opponents have been stripped of citizenship under that designation. They include the writers Sergio Ramírez and Gioconda Belli.

The bar also covers those involved in coup attempts and those deemed to undermine independence, sovereignty or security. That includes seeking foreign intervention, organising with foreign financing, or supporting economic or financial sanctions.

Electoral authorities would also gain new powers to dissolve parties and sanction candidates. Mandates would go from six years to seven.

The extension applies to the co-presidents, deputies, mayors, and judicial and electoral magistrates. It also covers the attorney general, the banking superintendent and the military and police chiefs.

Ratification requires a second legislative reading, scheduled for January 2027. The reform would postpone elections to late 2028.

If re-elected then, Ortega and Murillo could remain in power until 2036. Ortega is 80 and has governed continuously since 2007, and Murillo is 75.

Ballot boxes in Nicaragua. Elections have been postponed to 2028. Photo credit should read INTI OCON/AFP/Getty Images

The succession argument, and who is making it

Cetcam, the Centro de Estudios Transdisciplinarios de Centroamérica, is quoted collectively in an EFE wire of 16 September 2026. Its reading is that the handover is being rushed.

“La dictadura avanza con prisas en la sucesión dinástica”, it said, specifically moving power from Daniel Ortega to Rosario Murillo. It calls the September reform an attempt to close any remaining legal gap.

The changes, Cetcam adds, began in 2025 with the imposition of what was practically a new constitution. Two named researchers make a sharper argument.

Luis Rivas and Manuel Orozco of the Inter-American Dialogue published it on 24 August 2026. “Nicaragua is today the most authoritarian regime in the Western Hemisphere and a family dynasty,” they wrote.

Their point is that the constitutional designation of Murillo as successor may not hold. In highly personalised autocracies, they argue, power transfer depends on those who control the coercive forces.

Rebecca Bill Chavez, president and chief executive of the Inter-American Dialogue, reads the September reform as insurance. “The objective is to ensure there is as little uncertainty as possible about what happens after Ortega,” she said.

Most of Ortega and Murillo’s children hold key government positions. Nicaragua power concentration is, on this reading, a family matter as much as a party one.

What it means for people with a business or a family there

Nicaragua power concentration removes the ordinary places to appeal a decision. With 5,539 civil society entities dissolved, little now sits between a citizen and the State.

A 2025 change also eliminated dual citizenship, so acquiring another nationality means losing the Nicaraguan one. That matters directly to anyone holding property or a company in the country.

Neither date is settled. The reform has passed only its first reading, with a second scheduled for January 2027.

More: Nicaragua coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who governs Nicaragua?

Daniel Ortega, a former Sandinista guerrilla leader, has governed continuously since 2007 and is 80 years old. His wife, Rosario Murillo, is 75 and was vice-president until a constitutional reform created the post of co-president in February 2025. She now holds that office alongside him. Their party, the Sandinista National Liberation Front, holds all 153 municipalities and the majority in the legislature.

What did the United Nations actually say?

Volker Turk is the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights. He presented a report on Nicaragua to the Human Rights Council in Geneva on 16 September 2026. He called the situation “utterly indefensible” and said the report traces “the near-total capture of State institutions by the ruling party”. Speaking of the space left for civil society, he added that “there is almost nothing left to shut down”. The report covers the year from 15 June 2025 to 15 June 2026.

What does the September 2026 reform change?

It bars anyone designated a traitor to the homeland from standing for or holding public office. At least 452 opponents have already been stripped of citizenship under that label, including the writers Sergio Ramírez and Gioconda Belli. It also extends mandates from six years to seven, across the co-presidency, the legislature, the courts and the security chiefs. Elections move to late 2028, and the text still needs a second reading in January 2027.

Why do analysts talk about a succession?

Because the reforms of 2025 and 2026 together move authority towards Rosario Murillo and remove legal obstacles to her rise. Cetcam, a Central American research centre, says the dynastic succession is advancing in haste. Luis Rivas and Manuel Orozco of the Inter-American Dialogue argue that the constitutional designation may not be decisive. In highly personalised systems, they write, a transfer of power depends on those who command the coercive forces.

Sources: Arab News and AFP on the High Commissioner’s remarks, Mirage News reproducing the OHCHR statement, Scoop on the report presented in Geneva, OHCHR on the earlier July warning, Infobae and AFP on the 2025 constitutional reform, Infobae and EFE on the September 2026 reform, Tico Times on extended mandates and the 2028 vote, Infobae and EFE on the Cetcam succession analysis, Inter-American Dialogue on the perils of a planned succession, Artículo 66 on the end of dual citizenship

World.title: Heliostar Ana Paula Gold Project Costed at US$300 Million
World.content:
Mexico · Mining

Key Facts — What happened Heliostar Metals restated a US$300 million capital cost for its Ana Paula gold project in Guerrero, Mexico.

— What the money is Initial capital expenditure of US$300.1 million in the November 2025 economic assessment, not a fresh commitment.

— When it gets built Construction is scheduled to begin in 2027, with production targeted for the second half of 2028.

— What the study projects Net present value of US$426.0 million and a 28.1% return, calculated at US$2,400 an ounce gold.

— The catch Mexico is issuing no new mining concessions, so growth must come from ground the company already holds.

— Where gold trades now About US$4,357 an ounce on 17 September 2026, roughly 80% above the study base case.

A headline number from a Durango mining congress appears to be a restatement of a study figure from November 2025. The gold price has moved a long way since.

A Mexican gold and silver mine. Ana Paula is a different project, in Guerrero, and is not yet built.

One-stop reference Company Intelligence Every listed company in Latin America — financials, ownership and structure for 1,450+ companies across 26 exchanges, in one place. Browse the directory →

The US$300 million figure attached to Heliostar Ana Paula is not a new cheque. It is the initial capital cost of an underground gold project, as set out in the company’s own economic study.

Heliostar Metals, a Canadian-listed gold miner, published that study on 6 November 2025. The Preliminary Economic Assessment puts initial capital expenditure at US$300.1 million.

Life-of-mine capital comes to US$376.3 million. The number resurfaced this month because a company manager restated it at a mining congress in Mexico.

Where the number came from

Manuel Tovar Jacquez, described as general manager, presented it at the Ninth Durango Mining Congress 2026. The congress was held in Durango on 28 August 2026.

He also marked the formal start of open-pit work at the La Colorada mine. “Hemos convertido de nuevo las actividades de minado a cielo abierto en una realidad”, he said.

That line means open-pit mining has been made a reality again. He added a second thought about the company’s purpose.

“Nuestro propósito en Heliostar Metals es sencillo”, he told delegates. He went on: “construir una empresa minera de la que todos y todas podamos sentirnos orgullosos”.

The purpose, in other words, is a mining company everyone can be proud of. The trade service BNamericas headlined the same figure as an investment of US$300 million in the flagship Mexican gold project.

The evidence points to a restatement of the study capital cost rather than a fresh announcement.

Where the project is and when it would be built

Ana Paula sits in the state of Guerrero, in southern Mexico. It is Heliostar’s flagship development project and stands at the development and pre-feasibility stage.

A Feasibility Study is scheduled for completion in the first half of 2027. The company is meanwhile extending an existing 412-metre production-scale decline, the tunnel that carries equipment underground.

Construction is scheduled to begin in 2027. Production is targeted for the second half of 2028, so the capital is spent across roughly 2027 and 2028.

Gold. The economics published for Ana Paula assumed a price far below today’s.

The economics behind Heliostar Ana Paula

The Heliostar Ana Paula assessment was run at a base case gold price of US$2,400 an ounce. On that assumption it shows a net present value of US$426.0 million at a 5% discount rate.

The internal rate of return is 28.1% and payback takes 2.9 years. The mine life is nine years, at 101.1 thousand ounces a year after ramp-up.

Life-of-mine production is put at 874,700 ounces. Measured and indicated resources are 742,000 ounces at 5.40 grams a tonne, with 514,000 inferred ounces at 3.96 grams.

Here is the point that matters most for anyone reading the numbers. Gold traded around US$4,357 an ounce on Thursday 17 September 2026, according to Trading Economics.

That is a live quote taken during the session, intraday, not settlement prices. A second price service put gold at US$4,311 the same day.

That is roughly 80% above the base case used in the study. It is also well above the US$3,800 an ounce upside case the company modelled.

Charles Funk, Heliostar’s president and chief executive, called it a low-capital, high-margin mine. “Today’s PEA demonstrates Ana Paula can be a low CAPEX, high margin gold mine,” he said on 6 November 2025.

What the company produces today

Heliostar guided in January 2026 to 50,000 to 55,000 ounces of gold for the year. Consolidated all-in sustaining costs were guided at US$2,025 to US$2,125 an ounce.

La Colorada, in the state of Sonora, accounts for 20,000 to 22,300 ounces. San Agustín, in Durango, accounts for 30,000 to 32,700 ounces.

The 2026 capital plan allots US$6.6 million to Ana Paula exploration and development. A further US$15.0 million goes to the decline extension.

La Colorada takes up to US$5.8 million and San Agustín up to US$9.7 million, with US$4.9 million for other properties. A US$27 million exploration programme is funded from operating cash flow.

The shares trade on the TSX Venture Exchange as HSTR, on the OTCQX as HSTXF and in Frankfurt as RGG1. The company enters the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF effective 18 September 2026.

Gold ingots. Mexico’s president said in June 2025 that there would be no new mining concessions. Photo: Szaaman, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

Funk has put the trajectory plainly. The company went from one asset and a US$50 million market value to several producing assets in just over six years.

It now targets 500,000 gold ounces a year by the end of the decade. That target was reported by the outlet Minart on 16 September 2026.

The Mexican rules that shape the plan

Mexico rewrote its mining law in 2023. The reform was published on 8 May 2023 and took effect the following day.

It cut the initial concession term from 50 years to 30, with a single renewal of 25 years. All concessions are now awarded by public bidding.

Holders must recycle at least 60% of the water they use, with human consumption taking priority. They must also pay at least 5% of net profits to adjacent or affected indigenous communities.

Consultation with indigenous and local communities was widened. President Claudia Sheinbaum went further on 23 June 2025.

“There is not going to be another new concession — no, there are no new mining concessions,” she said. She added that existing concessions would be reviewed for environmental impact.

What it means in practice

Growth at Heliostar Ana Paula has to come from ground the company already holds. No new Mexican concession is available to it under current policy.

The company said it was preparing a permit amendment to convert granted open-pit permits to a lower-impact underground plan. Submission was expected in the first quarter of 2026, and no current status has been published.

For investors, the gap between a US$2,400 study and a US$4,357 gold price is the whole argument. For Guerrero, the test is whether construction actually starts in 2027.

More: Mexico coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Heliostar Metals?

Heliostar Metals is a gold miner with its main operations in Mexico and a listing in Canada. Its shares trade on the TSX Venture Exchange under HSTR, on the OTCQX market as HSTXF and in Frankfurt as RGG1. It runs the La Colorada mine in Sonora and the San Agustín mine in Durango. Its guidance for 2026 is 50,000 to 55,000 ounces of gold.

Is the US$300 million a new investment announcement?

Not in the sense of new money being committed this month. The figure is the initial capital cost calculated in the Preliminary Economic Assessment published on 6 November 2025. A company manager restated it at a mining congress in Durango on 28 August 2026, and trade coverage followed. The underlying project timetable, with construction from 2027, has not changed.

What is a Preliminary Economic Assessment?

It is an early-stage study that tests whether a mineral deposit could be mined at a profit. It models capital cost, operating cost, production and the price of the metal, then produces a value and a rate of return. It is less certain than a feasibility study, which for Ana Paula is due in the first half of 2027. Its conclusions move sharply when the assumed metal price changes.

Can mining companies still get new ground in Mexico?

Not through new concessions. The 2023 reform requires all concessions to be awarded by public bidding and shortens their initial term to 30 years. On 23 June 2025 President Claudia Sheinbaum said there would be no new mining concessions at all. Companies must therefore work the ground they already hold, and amend the permits attached to it.

World.title: BCP Helm Bank USA Deal Clears Florida, Fed Still Pending
World.content:
Peru · Banking

Key Facts — What happened Peru’s largest bank, BCP, announced Florida clearance on 16 September 2026 to buy Miami lender Helm Bank USA.

— What it costs US$180 million for 100% of the shares, subject to a customary price adjustment at closing.

— The catch The Federal Reserve has not yet approved the deal, and no completion date has been published.

— The bank being bought A Florida state-chartered community bank founded in 1989, holding US$1.1 billion in assets at 30 September 2025.

— Who its customers are Roughly 75% of Helm Bank USA borrowers have their primary home outside the United States.

— Who the buyer is Credicorp, listed in New York as BAP, is Peru’s largest financial group and the owner of BCP.

Peru’s largest bank has won state approval to buy a Miami lender whose borrowers mostly live abroad. The Federal Reserve has not yet acted.

Brickell in Miami. Helm Bank USA is a Miami bank with branches there and in Orlando. Photo: Phillip Pessar / CC BY 2.0

The BCP Helm Bank USA deal has cleared its first American hurdle. Banco de Crédito del Perú, Peru’s largest bank, said on Wednesday 16 September 2026 that Florida’s banking regulator had approved the purchase.

The approval came from the Florida Office of Financial Regulation, the state agency that charters and supervises Florida banks. It was reported by the Peruvian trade outlet Peru Retail, which carried the bank’s announcement.

That is not the end of the process. One more approval is outstanding.

The Federal Reserve has not signed off

Credicorp is the Lima-based holding company that owns BCP. Its filing with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission says completion depends on two American regulators.

The filing names the Florida Office of Financial Regulation and the Federal Reserve System. Only the first of those has now acted.

The Federal Reserve, the central bank that supervises bank holding companies, has not publicly cleared the transaction. No completion date has been published.

Nor has the status of the Federal Reserve application been disclosed. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency is not involved, because Helm Bank USA holds a state charter.

The price and the structure

BCP agreed to pay US$180 million for 100% of the shares of Helm Bank USA. The price is subject to a customary adjustment at closing, according to the announcement of 29 December 2025.

The BCP Helm Bank USA transaction runs through two newly created companies. They are Orange Peru Holding S.A. and Orange Financial Holding Inc., both named in the Credicorp filing dated 5 May 2026.

The seller is the Colombian Helm group, the existing shareholder base of the Miami bank. The group had earlier sold its Colombian banking operations.

Cross-border banking. Three quarters of Helm’s borrowers have their main home outside the United States.

What Helm Bank USA actually does

Helm Bank USA is a Florida state-chartered community bank founded in 1989, during the American savings and loan crisis. It is a member of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, which insures deposits at American banks.

It is headquartered in Miami, with branches in Miami and Orlando. The Orlando full-service branch, on South Orange Avenue, opened in 2025.

The bank also keeps a representative office in Bogotá and a presence in Medellín, Cali and Barranquilla. That Colombian reach is central to the franchise.

Its core business is cross-border residential real-estate lending to internationally active clients. Roughly 75% of its borrowers have their primary home outside the United States, according to Banking Dive.

It also takes personal and business deposits and offers auto loans, credit cards and foreign exchange. At 30 September 2025 it held total assets of US$1.1 billion.

Its loan portfolio stood at US$648.2 million and shareholders’ equity at US$106.8 million on that date. Those figures come from the December 2025 announcement.

The timeline, from December to September

Credicorp and BCP announced the agreement on 29 December 2025. Peru’s own supervisor moved next.

The Superintendencia de Banca, Seguros y AFP, which regulates Peruvian banks, insurers and pension funds, authorised BCP to acquire the whole bank. Credicorp disclosed that clearance in a filing dated 5 May 2026.

Peruvian outlets including Forbes Peru carried the news on 6 May 2026. One outlet dates the Peruvian approval to 8 May 2026.

BCP announced the Florida clearance on 16 September 2026. The sequence is therefore Lima first, Florida second, the Federal Reserve still to come.

Miami. The Florida regulator has cleared the deal; the Federal Reserve has not yet.

Why a Peruvian group wants a Florida platform

Credicorp Ltd. is the largest financial holding company in Peru. It is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker BAP and is based in Lima.

It runs four business lines: universal banking, microfinance, insurance and pensions, and investment banking and wealth management. Its subsidiaries include BCP, Mibanco, Grupo Pacífico, Prima AFP, Credicorp Capital and Atlantic Security Bank.

BCP is described by the group as Peru’s leading financial institution, with more than 18 million clients. Credicorp already operates in Chile, Colombia, Bolivia, Panama and the United States.

Gianfranco Ferrari, chief executive of Credicorp, set out the logic in December 2025. The aim is to serve “Latin Americans whose financial lives span both their home countries and the United States”.

Mark Crisp, president and chief executive of Helm Bank, called the deal a natural evolution. “Credicorp’s financial strength, trusted reputation, and client-centric philosophy provide a solid foundation for our next chapter,” he said.

The prize is a regulated onshore platform. Latin American clients who want dollars, mortgages and cards in the United States can then use a bank the group owns.

What it means in practice

For customers of the Miami bank, nothing changes until the Federal Reserve acts and the deal closes. Neither the deposit insurance nor the state charter is part of what the regulators are being asked to change.

For investors in Credicorp, the value of the BCP Helm Bank USA deal sits in the licence and the client base. Credicorp has published no figure setting the price against its own balance sheet.

For Latin Americans with property or family in Florida, the practical change is an owner with deep regional reach. No change to the terms of existing loans has been announced.

More: Peru coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is BCP?

Banco de Crédito del Perú, usually shortened to BCP, is the largest bank in Peru. Its parent is Credicorp Ltd., a Lima-based holding company listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker BAP. The group describes BCP as Peru’s leading financial institution, with more than 18 million clients. Credicorp also owns the microfinance lender Mibanco, the insurer Grupo Pacífico and the pension manager Prima AFP.

Does the Florida approval mean the deal is done?

No. Credicorp’s filing with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission says completion needs two American approvals. One is the Florida Office of Financial Regulation, which BCP said on 16 September 2026 had granted its approval. The other is the Federal Reserve System, which has not publicly acted, and no closing date has been published.

What is Helm Bank USA?

It is a community bank founded in 1989, headquartered in Miami and chartered by the state of Florida. It has branches in Miami and Orlando, a representative office in Bogotá and a presence in three other Colombian cities. Its main business is cross-border residential real-estate lending to internationally active clients. At 30 September 2025 it held US$1.1 billion in total assets.

Why would a Peruvian bank want a small bank in Miami?

Wealthy and internationally mobile Latin Americans often hold savings, mortgages and cards in the United States. Serving them from Lima means relying on someone else’s American licence. Buying a chartered Florida bank gives Credicorp a regulated onshore platform of its own. Its chief executive framed the purchase as a way to serve clients whose financial lives span two countries.

Sources: Peru Retail on the Florida approval, Credicorp’s Form 6-K on the outstanding Federal Reserve approval, GlobeNewswire on the US$180 million agreement, Helm Bank USA on its charter and branches, Banking Dive on cross-border mortgage lending, La República on the Colombian footprint, Forbes Peru on the Peruvian regulator’s clearance, Credicorp investor relations on the group’s businesses

World.title: Vaca Muerta Blocks Draw Bids From PCR, GeoPark and Central Puerto
World.content:
Argentina · Energy

Key Facts — Argentina Neuquén province opened economic bids in September 2026 for new exploration areas in the Vaca Muerta shale formation.

— Who is in front PCR, GeoPark, Central Puerto’s Patagonia Energy and a Continental Resources venture with Phoenix Global Resources.

— What is on the table Over US$230 million in exploration commitments and over US$180 million in bonuses to the provincial treasury.

— The silver exit Central Puerto sold its AbraSilver stake, reported at US$163.1 million, and will pay shareholders about US$164 million.

— The catch No award date has been announced, and no per-block resource estimates have been published.

— Next round A second tender focused on gas is due to be published in November 2026.

Neuquén has opened the money envelopes on eight exploration areas, and the provisional leaders are now visible. One bidder is an electricity company that has just cashed out of a silver mine.

Vaca Muerta in Neuquén. Ten or eleven companies bid, and eight of the fifteen blocks drew offers.

Vaca Muerta blocks in Argentina’s Neuquén province drew sealed bids this month from ten or eleven companies. The provincial oil company opened those envelopes in September 2026.

Vaca Muerta is an unconventional shale oil and gas formation in the Neuquén Basin, in Argentine Patagonia. Unconventional crude reached 70% of Argentina’s total oil output by the middle of 2026.

Who is running the tender

The seller is Gas y Petróleo del Neuquén, or GyP, the province’s state oil company. The round is designated Ronda 1/2026.

Fifteen areas were offered. Eight drew bids and seven were left vacant, with ten to eleven companies taking part.

Technical envelopes were opened first, and the economic offers, known as Sobres B, followed in September 2026. GyP is now checking technical consistency and financial solvency.

It will then send a pre-award report to its board, which resolves the award.

No award date has been announced. A second round focused on gas, Ronda 2, is due to be published in November 2026.

That round is aligned with the province’s plan to feed liquefied natural gas projects on the Río Negro coast. Bids in the current round are scored on four weighted variables.

Those are the exploratory investment commitment, a bonus paid to the provincial treasury, the royalty rate, and GyP’s carried stake. The royalty starts at 15% and can move between 12% and 18%.

GyP’s carried participation in each area has a floor of 10%. Across the eight Vaca Muerta blocks, the best proposals commit over US$230 million in exploration and over US$180 million in bonuses.

Añelo in Neuquén, the arid country that sits above the shale. Photo: Gervacio Rosales, CC BY 3.0, Wikimedia Commons.

Who is ahead, and what they already own

The provisional ranking published by vacamuerta.ar puts PCR top on three areas: Águila Mora Noreste, La Tropilla I and Santo Domingo II.

PCR is Petroquímica Comodoro Rivadavia, a long-standing conventional producer with no prior shale operations. This tender would be its entry into unconventional acreage in the formation.

It raised a US$400 million bond in July 2026, eight-year paper with an 8.5% coupon. GeoPark leads on Corralera Noreste with the highest score in the round, 12,241.

GeoPark recently bought Loma Jarillosa Este and Puesto Silva Oeste, holding 36.7 million barrels of oil equivalent in 2P reserves. It projects 5,000 to 6,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day by the end of 2026.

Central Puerto’s vehicle Patagonia Energy leads on Corralera Noroeste with 4,878, narrowly ahead of GeoPark according to Forbes Argentina. Central Puerto is an Argentine electricity generator.

It already operates Aguada del Chivato and Aguada Bocarey in the basin, both conventional fields. That is what makes these Vaca Muerta blocks a change of direction for a power company.

Continental Resources bid with Phoenix Global Resources on six areas and leads on Corralera Sur. Continental bought 90% of Los Toldos II Oeste from Pluspetrol and is securing 13% of Loma Guadalosa.

Phoenix produces 25,000 to 26,000 barrels a day and operates Mata Mora with a second rig. The venture announced a US$6 billion investment programme aimed at Argentina’s RIGI incentive framework.

Doug Lawler, chief executive of Continental Resources, told Forbes Argentina that Argentina is the company’s first priority. He added that Venezuela had come up repeatedly in its meetings.

Two smaller names lead elsewhere. JPM Energía tops Pampa de las Yeguas II NE, and Selva María Oil was the sole bidder on Chasquivil Sur.

This round is predominantly shale oil, and the November round targets gas. No per-area resource or reserve estimates have been published.

A provincial source told Runrún Energético the aim is a long-term partner, not the best sale price.

Neuquén city. The province writes the terms and collects the royalties.

Why a power company is selling silver

On 16 September 2026 Central Puerto announced the sale of its entire holding in AbraSilver Resource Corp., a Canadian miner. iProfesional put the proceeds at US$163.1 million.

Infobae reported the price as CAD 228.4 million, against iProfesional’s US$163.1 million. Neither outlet published the exchange rate linking the two figures.

The sources also word the stake differently. Infobae says Central Puerto sold 100% of its shareholding; iProfesional puts that holding at 9.9% of AbraSilver.

Central Puerto bought in during April 2024 for CAD 35.7 million, about US$25.3 million, becoming AbraSilver’s largest shareholder. The buyer this time has not been disclosed.

The board said the shareholding had ceased to be strategic in character. Proceeds fund an extraordinary cash dividend of about US$164 million, payable 25 September 2026.

Central Puerto has published nothing further about the use of the money. No closing date for the transaction was given.

AbraSilver’s asset is Diablillos, a silver and gold project in the Puna region of northwestern Argentina.

The gas that has not left yet

YPF, Argentina’s state-controlled oil company, is close to signing two or three offtake contracts for gas from the formation. The buyers have not been named.

Each prospective contract covers between 0.5 and 1.5 million tonnes a year. The constraint is not a conventional export pipeline to a neighbouring country.

It is the Argentina LNG project: a dedicated 527-kilometre pipeline from Neuquén to the coast, plus two floating liquefaction vessels. They will sit off the Golfo San Matías coast in Río Negro.

Minimum liquefaction capacity is 12 million tonnes a year, scalable to 18 million. The capacity of the pipeline itself has not been published.

A final investment decision is scheduled for November 2026, the same month as the second tender round. Negotiations were being held at the Gastech 2026 conference in Bangkok.

Horacio Marín, YPF’s president and chief executive, said the most intense part now begins: four years of work.

What it means in practice

The areas on offer are exploration acreage, not producing assets. The Vaca Muerta blocks therefore absorb money years before any barrel is sold.

Argentine energy exports reached US$6.594 billion in the first half of 2026, up 42.5% on the year. Crude accounted for US$4.693 billion of that, or 71.2%.

Marín expects Argentina to export one million barrels a day around 2033 or 2034. Between that and today sit a tender with no award date and a decision due in November.

More: Argentina coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Vaca Muerta?

It is an unconventional shale oil and gas formation in the Neuquén Basin, in Argentine Patagonia. Oil is produced there by hydraulic fracturing rather than from conventional reservoirs. In June 2026 the Neuquén Basin pumped 715,105 barrels a day, 79% of Argentina’s national output. The formation itself accounts for roughly 70% of that basin total, and production has grown about 36% a year.

What is GyP?

Gas y Petróleo del Neuquén, known as GyP, is the oil company owned by Neuquén province. It runs the tender rounds that allocate exploration areas to private operators. It also takes a carried participation in each area awarded, with a floor of 10%, so it keeps a stake in whatever is found. Its board resolves the final award after a pre-award report.

What is Central Puerto?

Central Puerto is an Argentine electricity generator that has been extending into upstream energy. It already operates two conventional oil and gas fields in the Neuquén Basin, Aguada del Chivato and Aguada Bocarey. Through a vehicle called Patagonia Energy it is now bidding for shale acreage. In April 2024 it had also bought into a Canadian silver and gold developer, a stake it has now sold.

What is the Argentina LNG project?

It is the export route for gas that currently has nowhere to go. The plan combines a dedicated 527-kilometre pipeline from Neuquén to the Atlantic coast with two floating liquefaction vessels. Those vessels would sit off the Golfo San Matías coast in Río Negro province. Minimum capacity is 12 million tonnes a year, scalable to 18 million, with a final investment decision due in November 2026.

Sources: Runrún Energético on the opening of the economic offers, vacamuerta.ar on the provisional ranking by area, Forbes Argentina on the four leading candidates, Mejor Energía on what each bidder already holds, Estaciones on the eight areas bid for and seven left vacant, iProfesional on the AbraSilver sale and the dividend, Infobae on the board’s rationale for the disposal, El Cronista on the 2024 entry price, LCR Diario Digital on YPF’s gas offtake talks, Infobae on Argentine shale production and energy exports

World.title: Costa Rica’s CCSS Prioritizes Emergency Care on Strike Day
World.content:
Costa Rica’s public health system has put backup plans in place for a nationwide strike called for today over problems with workers’ pay. Emergency care and other essential treatments are being prioritized, but patients could face delays in other services. The strike was scheduled to run from 6 a.m. today until 6 a.m. tomorrow. The call covers workers at public hospitals, clinics and Ebais, the neighborhood health centers that provide basic medical care.

As of this morning, the number of workers taking part and the extent of any cancellations had not been independently confirmed. A nationwide strike call does not mean every hospital or clinic has stopped providing services. The Costa Rican Social Security Fund, better known here as the CCSS or Caja, has plans to keep emergency rooms operating and protect care for patients who cannot safely wait. That includes people in intensive care, women giving birth, patients receiving cancer treatment and those needing urgent surgery.

The backup measures include moving staff where they are needed most and adjusting how facilities provide care. Staffing levels and the ability of hospitals and clinics to treat patients are also being monitored. Those measures do not guarantee that every regular appointment, medical test or planned procedure will go ahead as usual. The effect on patients will depend on staffing at each facility.

The dispute centers on complaints that some employees have received incomplete salary payments or have gone without pay. Five labor organizations called the strike to demand full, timely payments. The complaints followed the introduction in July of a new system for managing employee information and payroll. Resolving those payment problems is the central demand behind the planned 24-hour walkout.

For patients, the main unresolved question this morning was how much routine care would be affected. The emergency plans focus on keeping essential services available while protecting people whose health could worsen if treatment is delayed.

World.title: CDC Flags Costa Rica for Higher-Than-Expected Dengue Risk
World.content:
If you’re in Costa Rica or heading here soon, mosquitoes deserve more of your attention than usual. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has added Costa Rica to its list of countries with a higher-than-expected dengue risk. The update came on Sept. 3, and the U.S. Embassy in San José passed it on to U.S. citizens in a health alert on Sept. 11.

Costa Rica joins Colombia, Vietnam, the Maldives, Bolivia, Cambodia, Kenya, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, the Marshall Islands and Vanuatu on the list. This is not a travel warning. Costa Rica stays at Level 1, the lowest step on the CDC’s travel health scale, which means “practice usual precautions.” Nothing about the CDC’s travel recommendations has changed.

What the listing does mean is that dengue is more active than normal. Countries land on the list when they report more cases than usual, or when more U.S. travelers than expected come home sick with dengue after a visit. Either way, your odds of being bitten by an infected mosquito are higher right now.

The numbers here back that up as Costa Rica’s Ministry of Health has recorded 4,172 dengue cases through the 34th epidemiological week of 2026, compared with 2,751 at the same point in 2025. Earlier in the year, the ministry reported the Central Pacific region had the highest infection rate in the country, while the North Central region had the most cases overall.

The timing is not by coincidence as dengue spreads most during the rainy season, when puddles, gutters and discarded containers fill with water. The Aedes mosquito that carries the virus breeds in very small amounts of standing water and bites mostly during the day. Protecting yourself comes down to not getting bitten. Use an EPA-registered repellent with DEET, picaridin or IR3535, and reapply it as the label directs. Wear long sleeves and long pants outdoors, especially around dawn and late afternoon.

Where you sleep matters too. Choose rooms with air conditioning, window screens or mosquito nets. If you’re staying in a rental home, walk the property and empty anything holding water, from plant saucers and buckets to old tires and bottle caps. A single forgotten container can produce a steady supply of mosquitoes.

Know the symptoms, because the illness can show up as long as two weeks after the bite. That means you may feel fine the whole trip and get sick after you’re home. Watch for fever, headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle or joint pain and rash. See a doctor if you develop those symptoms during or after your time in Costa Rica. Get help quickly if you have severe stomach pain, repeated vomiting or bleeding from the nose or gums, since these can signal severe dengue. In an emergency in Costa Rica, call 911.

Don’t treat yourself before a diagnosis. Health authorities warn against self-medicating, and the CDC advises against aspirin and ibuprofen for suspected dengue because they can raise the risk of bleeding. Acetaminophen is the usual option for fever and pain, but check with a doctor first.

Most people recover within a week. The illness can still knock you flat, and a second infection with a different strain of the virus carries a higher risk of severe disease, so prevention pays off even if you’ve had dengue before. Dengue is not the only mosquito-borne illness on health officials’ radar this year. The CDC also has an active notice for a chikungunya outbreak in northwest Costa Rica, and the same precautions protect against both.

For anyone living in or visiting Costa Rica during the rainy season, the steps are easy to follow and the payoff is obvious. Clear standing water, cover up, use repellent and see a doctor early if a fever appears.

World.title: Belize Chamber of Commerce and Industry honors legacy partners for 3 decades of Expo Belize Market Place
World.content:
Belize Chamber of Commerce and Industry honors legacy partners for 3 decades of Expo Belize Market Place

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCI) has recognized 13 Legacy Partners for their longstanding support and commitment to the Expo Belize Market Place®, which recently celebrated its 30th anniversary.

The annual event has brought together businesses, consumers and communities for three decades, creating opportunities for businesses to showcase their products and services.

The BCCI honored partners whose support dates back to the inception of Expo Belize Market Place in 1996.

The 13 Legacy Partners recognized were Bowen & Bowen, GraceKennedy (Belize) Ltd., Belize Telemedia Limited (Digi Belize), Love FM/TV, KREM FM 96.5, 91.1, 101.1/XTV, Marie Sharp’s Fine Foods Ltd., Quality Poultry Products, Western Dairies Ltd., Wood Stop, Western Union, the Belize City Council, Santiago Castillo Ltd., and the Belize Tourism Board.

The BCCI says that the collective three-decade commitment of these partners represents more than a milestone, highlighting the importance of partnership and consistency in creating opportunities for Belizean businesses and the communities they serve. Their continued involvement has helped support Expo’s growth and sustainability throughout the years.

The BCCI expressed gratitude to the Legacy Partners for being part of Expo’s history and for growing alongside the annual marketplace.

World.content:

During the two day promotion, chicken legs in bags will be available for $2.90 per pound, while chicken cuts in trays will sell for $3.18 per pound.

The special prices are available for two days only on September 18 and 19.

World.content:
Newly appointed Ambassadors present Letters of Credence

By Zoila Palma: Today, Governor-General Froyla Tzalam received Letters of Credence from four newly appointed ambassadors to Belize.

André Driessen, Ambassador of the Kingdom of the Netherlands; Abedelazím Elsayed Rifai, Ambassador of the Arab Republic of Egypt; Dag Halvor Nylander, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Norway; and Samy Tatiana Araya Rojas, Ambassador of the Republic of Costa Rica; presented their credentials at the Belize House in Belmopan.

Julia Hyatt, High Commissioner of Jamaica, also made a courtesy call on the Governor-General.

The ambassadors shared their visions of fostering stronger international ties with Belize during their tenure. The Governor-General extended a warm welcome and best wishes on behalf of the nation.

World.title: Belize, Mexico Business round explores Trade and Investment Opportunities
World.content:
Belize, Mexico Business round explores Trade and Investment Opportunities

By Zoila Palma: Belize and Mexico are strengthening economic ties through a business round aimed at identifying new opportunities for trade and investment between the two countries.

On Tuesday, September 15, 2026, the Belize Trade and Investment Development Service (BELTRAIDE) participated in the Mexico–Belize Business Round as part of the Belize 2026 Trade Mission.

The event brought together a distinguished business delegation from Quintana Roo, Mexico, along with key Belizean representatives, including Mexico’s Ambassador to Belize, Ana Luisa Vallejo Barba; Belize Chamber of Commerce & Industry CEO Kim Aikman; Director of the Investment Policy and Compliance Unit Lincoln Blake; and Lianne Torres, Manager of BelizeINVEST, a unit of BELTRAIDE.

More than 28 Belizean enterprises participated in discussions across several key sectors, including agribusiness, manufacturing, logistics, energy, hospitality and financial services. The engagement provided an opportunity for businesses to explore potential partnerships while highlighting Belize’s market potential and opportunities for cross-border investment.

BELTRAIDE said the mission reflects Belize’s commitment to strengthening sustainable economic integration across the region and building lasting partnerships with Mexican counterparts.

World.content:
Las Terrazas Resort hiring General Manager or Management Couple in Belize

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Las Terrazas Resort on Ambergris Caye is seeking an experienced General Manager or Management Couple to lead its luxury island resort operation.

The boutique beachfront property, which is a member of the Preferred Hotels & Resorts LVX Collection, is looking for candidates with extensive experience in resort management and luxury hospitality.

Applicants should have a minimum of 10 years of experience as a General Manager in an island or condominium resort setting.

The position provides an opportunity to lead a beachfront property within the Preferred Hotels & Resorts LVX Collection.

World.content:
Belize welcomes High Commissioner of Jamaica to Belize
