World.title: Alexander Ovechkin backs Putin party in campaign video
World.content:
Ice hockey legend Alexander Ovechkin has lent Vladimir Putin's party a helping hand in its parliamentary election campaign. That's in keeping with a pattern of support by an athlete who claims not to be political.

When Russia's parliamentary elections are held from September 18 to 20, Alexander Ovechkin won't be there to cast his ballot in person. On Monday he took his first few strides back on the ice in the United States as he starts gearing up for a new National Hockey League (NHL) season with the Washington Capitals, his 22nd in the world's best league.

Before leaving his homeland, where he spent his summer break, he did make his contribution to the election campaign, however, appearing in a video promoting the ruling United Russia party, which steadfastly supports President Vladimir Putin.

In the video, which has been widely shared on social media, Ovechkin doesn't speak but can be clearly seen in the third row of a group of supporters behind Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, who is heading the United Russia list for the parliamentary vote.

Ovechkin's appearance has faced criticism, including from Ukrainian skeleton pilot Vladyslav Heraskevych, who was disqualified from the 2026 Olympic Games for insisting on wearing a helmet depicting athletes killed in Russia's war in Ukraine.

Ovechkin a long-standing Putin supporter

This is certainly not the first time that Ovechkin has expressed his support for Putin, with whom he shares his profile photo on his Instagram account.

Ovechkin's Instagram account features a profile photo of him with Putin Image: @aleksandrovechkinofficial/instagram

And, at times, Ovechkin's public support has appeared even more active than in the current United Russia video. Back in 2017, Ovechkin used his Instagram account to announce the creation of "PutinTeam" a group to help support Putin in the 2018 presidential campaign.

"I have never hidden my feelings about our president; I have always openly supported him. I am certain there are many of us who support Vladimir Putin! So let's unite and show the world a strong, united Russia!" he wrote.

"Being part of such a team is a source of pride for me; it feels just like pulling on the Russian national team jersey, knowing the whole country is rooting for you."

The creation of PutinTeam came three years after Russia had invaded and seized the Ukrainian territory Crimea in 2014, a move that was met with widespread condemnation in the international community. Later that year, Ovechkin appeared to express support for the operation, posting a photo of himself on Instagram holding up a sign with the message: "#savechildrenfromfascism."

"Our grandfathers and grandmothers witnessed all the horrors of fascism! We will not let it happen in our time," he wrote.

Putin has painted the Ukrainian authorities as "neo-Nazi" or fascist, in particular when justifying Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, launched in February 2022. What Putin calls a "special military operation" raised questions in the minds of many about how this might affect Ovechkin's view of the man he had always so publicly supported.

On February 25, 2022, a day after Russia launched the invasion, a reporter covering the Washington Capitals asked Ovechkin if he still supported Putin.

"Well, he's my president," Ovechkin replied. "But how I said, I'm not in politics, I'm an athlete."

He did issue a vague appeal for peace but declined to criticize Moscow's military action.

"Please, no more war. It doesn't matter who's in the war — Russia, Ukraine, different countries," he said.

Capitals: 'Ovechkin asked by his country'

Approached for comment on Tuesday, the NHL referred reporters to the Washington Capitals.

"Alex Ovechkin is a Russian citizen who ‌lives in Moscow with his family during the offseason and will ‌live ​there following his retirement," team spokesperson Sergey Kocharov said in the statement.

"This summer, while in Russia, he was asked by his country to participate in a video campaign. As the longest-tenured athlete in Washington, D.C., and a pillar of the community, his focus and ours is on the season ahead and the ⁠continued impact ​he makes on the ice and in our ​city."

'They asked me, I said yes, simple as that'

When Ovechkin was made available to reporters two days later, his message was essentially the same.

"About the video; I'm Russian. Once I finish playing hockey I am probably going to live there, my kids going to live there, my family. So I'm for peace and love and I hope everthing is going to be okay. My home is Russia," he said.

Asked by a reporter how he came to be involved in the campaign video, Ovechkin replied: "They asked me to do this and I said yes. Simple as that."

Back on the ice

Whatever you may think of his political views, Ovechkin is without a doubt one of the best players to ever lace on a pair of skates.

Now, back on the ice in Arlington, Virginia, ahead of the Washington Capitals' training camp, "Great8" is focused on getting his aging body (he turned 41 on Thursday) ready to compete for what would be a second Stanley Cup for both him and the Caps.

For much of the offseason, Ovechkin had left open whether he would return for another year. After all, he has achieved just about everything you can in the NHL, having broken Wayne Gretzky's career goal-scoring record two seasons ago. Going into the 2025-26 campaign he has 929 goals in 1,573 regular season games. In July though, after a conversation with his wife, he decided to come back for one more year in Washington – and he hasn't ruled out extending his career beyond that.

Over 40 and still going strong

"I'm going to be 41. I've had a lot of pressure on my shoulders over the years," he said. "I'm going to focus on the game and helping my team to win," he told reporters after his first skate. "I'm still a good player and can still help the team to win."

His numbers support that last assertion, having scored 32 goals in 2025-26. Only two other players have ever scored more over the age of 40.

"I can't wait for the season," he said. "On paper, you can see our team is one of the best teams but now we have to work for the Stanley Cup."

The bookies disagree, however, with some putting the Capitals way down at 18 (of 32) on their list of Stanley Cup candidates for 2027.

On the other hand, the prospect of United Russia's winning this weekend's parliamentary elections, the first since the launch of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, appears a safe bet.

This article was originally published on September 15, 2026. It was updated on September 16 with the comment of the Capitals spokesmand and on September 17 with the comment of Ovechkin himself.

Edited by: Jonathan Harding

World.title: Saudi Arabia, Houthis exchange blows as conflict escalates
World.content:
Five people were reportedly killed as the escalation between the two sides continues to spiral. The Houthis denied attacking Mecca, with Saudi Arabia saying one person was killed by drone shrapnel.

At least five people were killed in the escalation between the Iran-backed Houthirebel group and the internationally recognized Yemeni government, supported by Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Arabia accused the Houthis of a "cowardly" strike on Mecca, the holiest city in Islam and the site of the hajj and umrah pilgrimages, this week.

The rebel group denied the accusations.

Meanwhile, the Houthis claimed Saudi warplanes targeted three telecommunication towers in Taiz in southwestern Yemen.

According to the Almisrah TV channel, backed by the Houthis, one civilian was killed in the town of Abs in the northwest, with the channel later reporting that three children were killed by strikes carried out by Yemen's internationally recognized government.

In Saudi Arabia, one person was killed by shrapnel from a downed drone in the Mecca area, the country's civil defense agency said. Damage was also caused to buildings and vehicles.

This was the first reported death in Saudi Arabia in the current escalation between the two sides.

Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces are fighting against the Houthis Image: AFP

Houthis advance along coast after collapse of truce

A 2022 truce between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia collapsed in July after the rebels allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen's capital Sanaa, which defied the Saudis' control over Yemeni airspace. As a result of the escalation, the Houthis announced a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia.

The Houthis have controlled Sanaa and much of Yemen's more populous western areas since the start of Yemen's civil war in 2014.

The rebel group has reported dozens of Saudi strikes since its recent offensive to secure control over the coastal areas near the Red Sea's Bab al-Mandab Strait, one of the world's most important shipping routes, from government hands.

The strait's importance has increased since Iran put restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz over the US and Israel's war with Tehran.

The conflict in Yemen has forced more than 100,000 people to flee their homes, according to UN figures.

World.title: Judges: As AfD ascends, Germany must bolster justice system
World.content:
German judges and prosecutors warn that the government needs to reform the laws covering state prosecutors to prevent "extremists in government" from abusing the legal system.

The official association of German judges, the Deutscher Richterbund (DRB) , has called on the federal government to tighten up the law to stop state governments from abusing prosecution powers to potentially influence criminal cases.

The prospect that the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) could take over the government in Saxony-Anhalt, which appears highly likely after the party's resounding election win in early September, has raised fears that "extremists in government" could steer "criminal investigations in one direction or another through directives," according to the DRB.

The AfD, sections of which are considered a threat to the German constitutional democratic order by domestic intelligence agencies, is set to take control of a state government for the first time ever in Saxony-Anhalt. This has sparked concern in the judicial system that the party could, for instance, push prosecutors away from pursuing cases against right-wing extremists.

"The top priority now is to prevent the misuse of public prosecutors' offices in Germany for partisan political purposes," DRB executive director Sven Rebehn said in a statement emailed to DW. "Currently, the law allows state justice ministries to interfere even in individual criminal proceedings. While there is a political tradition of self-restraint when issuing directives to prosecutors, this tradition can be abandoned at any time and offers no effective protection."

New report backs ban of German far-right party To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

State prosecutors — not independent

In Germany, unlike in many other countries, state prosecutors, along with the police, are part of the executive branch of government. This puts them under the authority of the state or federal Interior Ministries, and subject to parliamentary oversight. This dependence is seen by many constitutional lawyers as a democratic principle, as it means that prosecutors' actions can be checked by a democratically elected body. But others see it as a problem, as it opens the possibility of political influence.

German Interior Ministries, both at the federal level and in the 16 states, have the power to issue directives to prosecutors in individual cases. For instance, if some evidence has been supplied by an intelligence agency, the Interior Ministry can issue a directive to the prosecutor to keep that fact out of a court case, as disclosing it could compromise the work of the agency.

The German domestic intelligence agency, the Verfassungsschutz, which reports to the Interior Ministry, has long been a focus of the AfD's ire, as members of the party consider it politicized. The agency is charged with keeping tabs on extremist tendencies in the country. By the same token, German Justice Ministries can make a ruling over how prosecutors interpret a certain law, or how investigations are to be pursued.

One such directive was made in 2015, when the then federal justice minister, Heiko Maas, told the federal prosecutor to withdraw a report that found that state secrets had been compromised in a particular case. Maas denied that this had been the directive, and federal prosecutor Harald Range was dismissed in the ensuing power struggle.

As things stand, there is still no way to check the ministry's directives, which some see as a problem. Berlin's state prosecutor, Margarete Koppers, also has strong opinions on this point, and sees the danger as acute: "The rule of law is at risk when its rules are politically abused," a spokesperson for Koppers told DW by email. "A look at European countries that have, at various times, been under authoritarian-populist leadership — and where the structures of the rule of law were subsequently eroded — shows that this is not an unrealistic scenario." When the far-right Law and Justice (PiS) party took over in Poland, it triggered a constitutional crisis by trying to appoint judges to the constitutional court. The government of Viktor Orban in Hungary also tried to intervene in the judicial system.

EU, Poland row over judicial committee To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Another option: Make directives transparent

Both the DRB and Koppers believe that removing the ministries' right to take directives is long overdue, but others in the judicial field are not so sure.

"I can understand the fear that a sword like this in the hands of the wrong people makes the executive branch a danger," said Gül Pinar, a criminal lawyer based in Hamburg who in 2020 offered expert testimony in the Bundestag on the issue.

Pinar said reform was necessary, but mainly because ministries' directives are not documented. "The people who are affected by the criminal procedures don't know that certain actions taken by the prosecutors stem from a directive, from the government, or the federal prosecutors, or the Interior Ministry," she told DW.

If the directives were documented, Pinar said, it would be possible for lawyers to examine whether they were legally sound, or whether they overstepped their authority. "We have to insert new mechanisms to check what is happening," she said.

"But the solution is not to make the state prosecutors independent," Pinar said. Hardly anyone in the judiciary, she said, doubts that the right to issue instructions stems from the principle of democracy. But she added that there were many voices, particularly amongst judges and public prosecutors, who advocate for an independent public prosecution service.

The current federal government has not shown any inclination to change the law. In a statement to the Legal Tribune Online, the Federal Justice Ministry said that the current laws provided plenty of safeguards: Ministries are prohibited from issuing "unlawful" directives, and prosecutors from following them.

In fact, according to the ministry, keeping prosecutors in the executive branch is important, because it means that they are more accountable and subject to parliamentary oversight.

Inside the AfD To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The European arrest warrant problem

The relatively unique position of Germany's state prosecutors has come up at the European level before: In 2019, the European Court of Justice warned that European arrest warrants could be compromised by political influence because German state prosecutors were not independent enough: European arrest warrants are supposed to be issued by state prosecutors, but, in Germany, only judges are allowed issue them.

Pinar said allowing state prosecutors to issue arrest warrants was "not compatible with our legal system." In fact, she said, the German system safeguards more civil freedoms. "In Germany, withdrawing someone's freedom is always under the authority of the judge," she said. "I think it would better if other countries adapted their systems to ours, so that the executive branch can decide on the freedom, but was under a judge's authority."

Edited by Rina Goldenberg

World.title: As global crises grow, Germany cuts development aid
World.content:
The budget of Germany's Economic Cooperation and Development Ministry is set to shrink for the fifth consecutive year. Aid organizations warn that the cuts will have severe consequences for millions of people.

German Development Minister Reem Alabali Radovan opened her speech in the lower house of parliament, the Bundestag, with a litany of catastrophes and suffering: floods in Nepal, heat waves, forests engulfed in flames, rivers running dry, and crop failures caused by drought.

"Millions of people are facing hunger," said Radovan, of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD). "And one thing is clear: The climate crisis is threatening the entire world. No country can tackle it alone."

Radovan opened the debate on the federal government's proposed 2027 budget for her ministry with a stark assessment. The budget is set to shrink for the fifth consecutive year, falling from just over €10 billion to just under €9.5 billion ($10.9 billion). In 2022, it stood at nearly €14 billion, meaning that the ministry's budget has been reduced by roughly one-third over the past half decade.

Fighting to end suffering in Africa's conflict zones To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

How does this sharp decline square with the dramatic picture painted by Germany's development minister? She pointed to a strategy she unveiled in January, when she declared that "development policy will become an even more important pillar of German security, alongside diplomacy and defense."

Funding for humanitarian aid stagnates

Aid organizations reacted skeptically to this policy shift when it was first announced, and their concerns have deepened in light of the latest funding cuts. "The renewed reductions in funding for international cooperation are further exacerbating an already critical situation," said Michael Herbst of VENRO , the umbrella organization representing around 150 development and humanitarian NGOs.

Herbst criticized the stagnant budget for humanitarian aid administered by the German Foreign Office. While it exceeded €3 billion in 2022, it has remained at just €1 billion since 2025. In light of worsening global crises, VENRO is calling for a change of course. "Next year, we will need to invest more in combating hunger because the conflict involving Iran and the dry summer are expected to trigger a sharp decline in agricultural yields," Herbst said, explaining the organization's demand for substantially higher funding.

Ten million people left without assistance

The impact of the cuts is already clearly visible, according to VENRO. A survey of its member organizations found that the number of funded projects is declining significantly. "Our sample of 34 organizations shows that, among these organizations alone, more than ten million fewer people are being reached with assistance."

"And many local partner organizations, which are indispensable to effective development cooperation and humanitarian assistance, are no longer able to operate," Herbst said. He added that the full impact of these far-reaching cuts is unlikely to become apparent for another three to four years.

A 'debt brake' exemption for development?

The federal government's belt-tightening across virtually all ministries is a consequence of the Zeitenwende announced by 2022 Chancellor Olaf Scholz(SPD) in response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Since then, Germany has embarked on a major military buildup, increasing its defense budget year after year, while nearly all other ministries have had to make do with significantly less funding.

Herbst, a member of VENRO's executive board, is calling on the Bundestag to exempt both development cooperation and humanitarian assistance from Germany's "debt brake." "After all, exceptions have already been made for the modernization of the Bundeswehr and for military aid to Ukraine," he said. Herbst said an exemption would enable Germany to once again assume greater responsibility on the international stage.

Germany's Radovan warns SDGs unlikely to be met by 2030 To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Less money, less impact?

Jamila Schäfer, a member of parliament from the opposition Green Party, made a similar argument during the Bundestag debate on the Development Ministry's budget. Climate action and development cooperation, she argued, are not acts of charity but are firmly in Germany's own interest.

"Germany must invest in its defense capabilities, but security is not created through investments in the defense budget alone," Schäfer said. "Those who strengthen military security while cutting support for international stability have a blind spot in their security policy."

Nicolas Zippelius, a lawmaker from the governing center-right conservative alliance, the Christian Democratic Union and Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU), sees the ongoing cuts to development spending differently. In his view, every ministry must contribute to consolidating the federal budget. "Less money does not necessarily mean a smaller impact. Instead, it should encourage us to focus more clearly on priorities and critically review existing structures."

Zippelius dismisses demands to exempt the Development Ministry from Germany's debt brake. "The key question is whether every euro spent is directed to where it can make the greatest difference." The Christian Democrat argues that success in development cooperation, as in other areas of policy, should be judged not by the size of the budget but by the impact it achieves.

German Development Minister Reem Alabali Radovan in Kenya To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The case for more prevention

Jan Sebastian Friedrich-Rust, who heads the humanitarian and development aid organizationAction Against Hunger , has a very different view. "The cuts planned for the 2027 budget are short-sighted and dangerous. As a result, up to 22.6 million people worldwide could die by 2030," he said in a written statement to DW.

Cuts to development cooperation and humanitarian aid are also fiscally short-sighted, Friedrich-Rust said. "Hunger, crises and instability generate long-term costs that far exceed the cost of prevention. Those who cut spending today are merely postponing the bill and ultimately making it much more expensive," he warned.

To underscore its concerns, the Action Against Hunger alliance delivered a petition to the leaders of the governing coalition of SPD and CDU/CSU parliamentary groups on the eve of the Bundestag's budget debate. About 100,000 people added their names to the appeal, titled "Don't Balance the Budget at the Expense of Solidarity: Strengthen International Aid!"

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: Baby orangutans are adorable, but five in a forest in India is a telltale sign of animal trafficking
World.content:
Orangutans, rare reptiles and other exotic animals are popping up in India, suggesting the country is becoming a major destination for trafficked wildlife.

Five infant orangutans, a species found only on the Indonesian island of Sumatra and on Borneo, were found in a forest by rangers patrolling in the Balasore district of India's eastern Odisha state last week.

Indonesia's Forestry Ministry has asked India to establish the origin of the abandoned orangutans, known for their shaggy red fur, and return them if they are found to have come from their usual habitat abroad.

The rescue of the rare apes has raised fresh questions about how exotic animals enter India and how the country is used in the illegal wildlife trade.

How did five baby orangutans end up in India?

"The discovery on the eastern coast of India is a bit mind-boggling. It's like that time a few years ago when live kangaroos were found wandering along the highways of West Bengal," Kanitha Krishnasamy, Southeast Asia director at wildlife trade monitoring network TRAFFIC, told DW.

"What are orangutans doing in India? Were they smuggled from their native Malaysia or Indonesia or did they come from a facility?" she asked.

The youngsters appeared to be healthy and were being cared for at a zoo after their rescue Image: ANI/IMAGO

The Odisha government has asked the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau to investigate how the critically endangered animals reached the state.

"These animals are not found in India and are mostly seen in the rainforests of Malaysia, Indonesia, Borneo and Sumatra in Southeast Asia," said Odisha's Forest and Environment Minister Ganesh Ram Singh Khuntia.

"We suspect that they might have been released in the Balasore district forest… by an international wildlife smuggling racket."

Indian officials seize pythons, parrots, giant tortoises

The orangutans are the latest in a series of exotic wildlife being seized in India.

In November 2024, authorities in the Indian city of Bengaluru seized 40 rare animals arriving from the Malaysian capital, Kuala Lumpur, including Aldabra giant tortoises, gibbons, American alligators and iguanas.

In June 2025, Mumbai Customs seized 284 exotic animals arriving in four consignments from the Thai capital, Bangkok, including snakes and tortoises.

In July 2025, customs officials in the Indian city of Pune intercepted 20 exotic animals from passengers arriving from Bangkok. They included 14 green tree pythons, four double-eyed fig parrots and two Sumatran striped rabbits.

'Shocking' volume of trafficked wildlife found in India

According to figures from TRAFFIC, 7,272 individual animals, alive and dead, were seized from passenger baggage in smuggling attempts between Thailand and India between January 2022 and May 2025, with more than 80% of interceptions taking place in India.

The animals included reptiles, birds and mammals — many apparently destined for the exotic pet trade.

"We have found hundreds of species and thousands of individuals being trafficked into India through air and land routes. This changed drastically from around 2020," conservation researcher and practitioner Uttara Mendiratta told DW.

"Both the volume of this trafficking, and the number of species involved, many of which are endangered, have been shocking."

Law enforcement lagging behind smugglers

TRAFFIC says India and Malaysia were the countries most implicated in an illegal gibbon trade chain identified in 2025, with gibbons being moved from Malaysia to India.

Trishala Ashok, a conservation filmmaker and science communicator, says the scale of the trade remains difficult to establish.

"Our enforcement systems haven't evolved at the same speed as the trade," Ashok told DW. "We are still reacting to individual seizures rather than mapping the networks, financiers, suppliers and buyers behind them."

Tito Joseph of the Wildlife Protection Society of India says the situation is escalating.

"Smuggling of exotic species was always there in India," Joseph told DW.

At the same time, he noted that it has increased significantly since 2018.

He identifies routes running from Myanmar through northeast India into other parts of the country, as well as movement from Bangladesh into India. By air, Thailand and Malaysia are important sources of trafficked wildlife.

The routes into India also extend beyond airports. Exotic animals are also reaching India through its northeastern land borders.

"What is new is the large volume of incoming live wildlife. There are indications that some of the traders who were involved in smuggling live animals like star tortoises out are now also involved in sourcing [other] exotic wildlife," said Mendiratta, the conservation researcher.

Social media fans illegal animal trade

Demand is being fueled by growing ownership of exotic pets and unregulated digital marketplaces, according to a June 2026 analysis of India's exotic pet trade by Humane World for Animals India, an NGO that works to tackle the root causes of animal cruelty.

"Internationally, social media platforms have aided and abetted the growth of illegal trade in wild animals by providing a platform for people to display and boast about the animals they collect," wildlife biologist and conservation scientist Ravi Chellam told DW. "These platforms are also serving as an online marketplace for the illegal trade to flourish."

"The problem is exacerbated by the senseless and obscenely huge personal collections of animals from around the world by the rich and the famous," Chellam noted.

Establishing where an animal came from can become particularly difficult once it has crossed several borders.

"A seizure cannot be the end of the investigation. It should be the beginning," said Ashok, the conservation filmmaker.

"Who supplied the animals? Who arranged the movement? Who paid? Who was waiting for them?" she asks. "Until we start following those links, we will keep catching consignments without dismantling the networks behind them."

World.title: El Gobierno de Ayuso reconoce ahora que el ático de 6,3 millones iba a usarse para “alojamiento ocasional de autoridades de la Comunidad”
World.content:
El Gobierno de la Comunidad de Madrid, que preside Isabel Díaz Ayuso, ha reconocido este jueves por primera vez que el ático de 6,3 millones que adquirió Planifica Madrid iba a usarse como “alojamiento ocasional para autoridades de visita o las propias autoridades de la Comunidad”. Así lo ha confirmado el consejero de Presidencia, Miguel Ángel García Martín, durante una comparecencia en la Asamblea de Madrid. Su explicación supone un nuevo giro argumental en el intento de la Administración por explicar esta polémica operación, desvelada por EL PAÍS en julio. La primera explicación sobre la compra fue que serviría como oficina de la presidenta durante unas obras en la Real Casa de Correos. Luego se especificó que no se usaría como residencia oficial. Y ahora se abre la puerta a que tuviera un uso intermedio, precisamente como alojamiento temporal de autoridades del Gobierno regional. Un anuncio que ha coincidido con otra novedad: Madrid no ha logrado vender el ático en la subasta que había convocado para ello, por lo que volverá a sacarlo al mercado a partir de este viernes.

Ahora, la administración madrileña intentará encontrar un comprador a través de un nuevo mecanismo. “El inmueble de la calle Martínez Campos se mantendrá a la venta a través de un procedimiento abierto de adjudicación. Hoy mismo se han celebrado las mesas técnicas y mañana celebraremos un consejo de Administración para mantener a la venta el inmueble”, ha anunciado el consejero de Presidencia, Miguel Ángel García Martín, que ha comparecido en la Asamblea por este caso a petición propia.

La Comunidad de Madrid compró el ático el 14 de abril y lo mantuvo en secreto hasta que EL PAÍS reveló su existencia el 29 de julio. A esas alturas, Planifica Madrid se lo había alquilado a la Administración madrileña. Ese mismo día, Ayuso dijo que el piso se había adquirido para que fuese su oficina temporal mientras se realizaban obras en la sede de Sol, la sede del Gobierno. Sin embargo, debido a toda la polémica que generó el caso, el Gobierno madrileño anunció que lo sacaba a subasta y que el dinero recaudado se destinaría a la reconstrucción de las zonas de la región afectadas por los incendios de este verano.

La oposición denunció que la presidenta había comprado una finca de lujo millonaria para convertirla en su residencia presidencial. El informe demuestra que, al menos, Ayuso podía usar esa vivienda “de forma ocasional”. Los motivos que llevaron a Planifica Madrid a comprar este inmueble en concreto han sido motivo de especulación y disputa política estos casi 50 días desde que este periódico publicó la exclusiva. El Gobierno de Ayuso ha tratado de zanjar hoy cualquier polémica con la publicación de partes del informe y la declaración del consejero.

Además de ser destinado a vivienda ocasional para la presidenta “o autoridades de visita en la región”, la memoria explica que el ático servía también para situaciones de emergencia: “Disponer de espacios accesorios o complementarios a las sedes institucionales en contextos de gestión de crisis que puedan prolongarse en el tiempo y que puedan requerir de un inmueble de estas características. Recordemos en este punto la pandemia del covid-19”.

La Comunidad de Madrid justifica la adquisición con varios informes más incluidos en ese mismo expediente de Planifica Madrid. Uno incluye el contrato de alquiler suscrito entre Planifica Madrid y el propio Gobierno regional. Otro, de Economía y Hacienda, autoriza ese alquiler y el pago plurianual correspondiente. Ese alquiler, de acuerdo con más información incluida en la memoria, estaba avalado por la Abogacía General, que reconoce “expresamente” la condición de arrendamiento para “uso distinto del de vivienda”. Un cuarto documento, también de Hacienda, insiste en que usarlo también como despacho “es plenamente compatible con la normativa urbanística”.

El consejero García Martín ha aparecido en el pleno de la Asamblea apenas minutos después de que este periódico adelantara que la subasta ha quedado desierta. Según él, las críticas al ático han pretendido “ocultar” la crisis migratoria de Ceuta y los “gravísimos” casos de corrupción del sanchismo. “España le queda muy grande”, ha dicho en referencia a Pedro Sánchez, el presidente del Gobierno central. García Martín ha asegurado que “nunca” se compró para convertirlo en la vivienda de Ayuso, que permanecía sentada en el lugar preferencial que ocupa en la Asamblea.

Sin embargo, la presidenta parecía distraída. Sus consejeros han intentado levantar una burbuja a su alrededor, conocedores de la profunda crisis interna que han vivido a cuenta de este thriller inmobiliario. Ayuso tenía un Airpods puesto en una oreja y a ratos anotaba en un papel. No miraba de frente a sus interlocutores. Uno de sus consejeros, incluso, la llevó a una esquina del recinto para contarle algo, lo que parecía una táctica de distracción. Los diputados populares aplaudieron con más énfasis que nunca y celebraron todos y cada uno de los anuncios del consejero. Tocaba defender el fuerte.

García Martín ha explicado cómo se eligió el ático de Chamberí: “Planifica Madrid, en el marco de sus competencias y su normal actividad de gestión patrimonial (art. 2 de sus Estatutos), y a petición de la Consejería de Presidencia, Justicia y Administración Local, adquirió un inmueble en el Paseo del General Martínez Campos tras un proceso de búsqueda e identificación de posibles alternativas y con el objetivo de ponerlo a disposición de la Comunidad de Madrid”. Y ha añadido: “Y aquí viene la gran mentira de la izquierda: este inmueble nunca se adquiere para que sea una residencia oficial para la presidenta, como sí tienen la mitad de los ministros y muchos presidentes autonómicos”.

A continuación, ha leído párrafos incluidos en los informes de la memoria, que ya aparecen al comienzo de este artículo. Según él, esta documentación demuestra que no existen pruebas de que se buscara “ninguna residencia oficial”. Las palabras de García Martín han estado todo el tiempo acompañadas de los gritos de la oposición. El presidente de la Asamblea ha tenido que pedir silencio en varias ocasiones. En un momento dado le ha tenido que pedir al consejero que pare un momento y ha reprendido a los diputados de PSOE y Más Madrid.

El momento más abucheado ha sido cuando García Martín ha asegurado que el inmueble no se puso a la venta por la revelación de EL PAÍS, sino por “los incendios en la sierra oeste”. Ambos eventos coincidieron en el tiempo. El consejero ha dicho que Ayuso “no ha tenido, tiene ni tendrá una residencia oficial”. Y ha enumerado los ministros que cuentan con una que, según sus cálculos, suman 4.600 metros cuadrados y más de 75 millones de euros de valor (algo que ha sido así con gobiernos del PSOE o del PP).

A esas alturas, García Martín había elevado el tono al máximo y parecía ir en volandas. “Señorías, la presidenta les retó la semana pasada a demostrar que la Comunidad de Madrid le había comprado una residencia oficial para vivir y, en caso de no poder hacerlo, presentaran su dimisión. Pues bien, están tardando en hacerlo”, dijo emocionado. Sus compañeros de bancada lo ovacionaron.

El consejero presumió de transparencia, pero los diputados de la oposición no han podido llegar a su comparecencia con el expediente, que la Comunidad de Madrid ha evitado dar a conocer hasta el último momento. La portavoz socialista, Mar Espinar, ha acusado a García Martín de ocultar la operación y ha sostenido que el ático se compró para Ayuso. “Todos estamos obligados hoy a estar aquí por su ocultismo, por su censura y por la opacidad de este Gobierno. La que debería comparecer hoy en esta Cámara es su jefa, la señora Ayuso, que por lo menos ha tenido la decencia de volver a aparecer en este pleno y mirarle mientras pasa usted este trago”, ha reprochado. Ayuso, a mitad de la comparecencia, ha abandonado el hemiciclo.

El expediente completo de Planifica Madrid no ha visto la luz, por ahora. Los informes dados a conocer no detallan que se tratase de una “residencia presidencial”, pero sí le daba la posibilidad a la presidenta de dormir y trabajar en él de forma ocasional. Hugo Martínez Abarca, diputado de Más Madrid, ha dicho no creer las explicaciones del Gobierno porque enseñan “un taco de folios que no podemos ver”. “¿Saben quién enseñó un taco de folios y dijo que había hecho un máster? Efectivamente, la señora Cristina Cifuentes. Pues en este caso igual. El expediente deberíamos tenerlo nosotros en nuestra mesa hace tres semanas", insistió Martínez Abarca.

La polémica no queda zanjada. Parecía que la comparecencia del consejero revelaría toda la información del ático, pero por ahora la Comunidad de Madrid la está proporcionando a cuentagotas. El expediente completo sigue guardado en un cajón. Mientras tanto, nadie quiere hacerse con el polémico ático.

World.title: Un informe interno del Gobierno de Ayuso afirma que la apuesta por el ático no estaba “suficientemente” explicada
World.content:
Un informe interno de la Comunidad de Madrid recogió el 27 de julio que la apuesta por el ático del paseo del General Martínez Campos no estaba “suficientemente” explicada. La interventora delegada jefa de Economía y Hacienda informó favorablemente sobre la operación, aunque también recogió unas observaciones taxativas: el alquiler que iba a permitir al Gobierno usar el ático se había realizado “sin profundizar en el estudio de necesidad, idoneidad, aspectos económicos tales como renta, gastos, comparativa de edificios similares, etc.”. Así consta en el dosier documental sobre la operación distribuido este jueves por la Administración regional, tras la comparecencia del consejero de Presidencia, Miguel Ángel García Martín, para explicar el proyecto. Son más de 200 páginas que también recogen que la Comunidad estaba dispuesta a pagarle 3.000 euros al mes a Planifica Madrid para utilizar el inmueble.

Al analizar el informe sobre el contrato de alquiler que pretendía suscribir la Administración regional con Planifica Madrid, la interventora no solo señala que no se le ha transmitido un informe que explicara la idoneidad de la compra a través de la comparación del precio y las características del inmueble con otros similares. También destaca que no se le haya hecho llegar el informe de conformidad del uso con la normativa aplicable, emitido por el director técnico de Planifica el 7 de julio de 2026. Esa observación pone bajo los focos uno de los aspectos más polémicos del proyecto: si el ático, como explicó inicialmente el Gobierno, podía usarse como oficina o si se puede utilizar como residencia temporal, como ha explicado García Martín, en un nuevo giro de guion.

Además, el informe interno afea la poca precisión de los datos aportados: señala, por ejemplo, que deberían haberse recogido en todo el expediente “datos homogéneos de su superficie”. En todo caso, la interventora concluyó que sus observaciones no producían “efectos suspensivos”, por lo que podía “continuar la tramitación del expediente”.

Este jueves, el consejero de Presidencia ha aclarado que la Comunidad de Madrid pretendía alquilar el ático a Planifica Madrid, la empresa pública que lo había adquirido por 6,3 millones, para ponerlo a disposición de la Administración regional. Desde que EL PAÍS desveló la operación en julio, el Gobierno ha ofrecido distintas explicaciones sobre su finalidad. Primero afirmó que serviría como oficina temporal de Ayuso durante las obras en la Real Casa de Correos; después precisó que no se utilizaría como residencia oficial; y este jueves ha reconocido por primera vez que iba a destinarse a “alojamiento ocasional para autoridades de visita o las propias autoridades de la Comunidad”.

World.title: La estafa del falso empleado de banca
World.content:
Recibir un SMS que alerta sobre un movimiento sospechoso en nuestra cuenta bancaria puede evitar que seamos víctima de un robo, excepto si no ha sido el banco quien realmente lo ha emitido

En la estafa del falso empleado de banca el delincuente primero envía un mensaje con una alerta sobre un movimiento sospechoso en la cuenta y facilita un enlace o un número de teléfono al que llamar. Ya en la conversación, intenta convencer a la víctima de que su dinero está en peligro para que autorice operaciones que resultarán fraudulentas

En 2025, Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (INCIBE) registró 25.133 casos de phishing. Durante los dos últimos años, tanto la Policía Nacional como la Guardia Civil y el Banco de España han emitido alertas sobre el aumento de las llamadas de falsos empleados bancarios.

TÉCNICAS DE MANIPULACIÓN

Autoridad Suplantan a profesionales pertenecientes a bancos a los que la víctima concede poder y confianza Urgencia Crean la sensación de que hay poco tiempo para actuar, lo que evita que la víctima reflexione o consulte con alguien Sobrecarga de información técnica Emplean jerga bancaria para intimidar y hacer creer que dominan una situación compleja Aumento gradual de las peticiones Incluye a la víctima en grupos de aplicaciones de mensajería para hacerle creer que mucha gente ya está ganando dinero

CIBEREXPERTO NOMBRE Jordi Sánchez CARGO Experto en fraude de CaixaBank “Durante la llamada, el estafador te hace creer que te está guiando para solucionar tu problema, pero en realidad, está intentando que tu hagas exactamente lo que necesita, emitir operaciones bancarias, descargar aplicaciones o facilitar información, como códigos o datos de tarjetas” Play / Pause CÓMO EVITAR LA ESTAFA DEL FALSO EMPLEADO DE BANCA 1 Sospechar de mensajes inesperados. No clicar en ningún enlace que aparezca en el mensaje ni llamar al número que ofrecen. Ante la duda, siempre se debe llamar a los números oficiales del banco 2 Desconfiar de la urgencia y de las amenazas.Mensajes como “Su cuenta será bloqueada” buscan que se actúe sin pensar 3 No compartir claves ni códigos de verificación. El banco nunca solicitará contraseñas u otros códigos de seguridad 4 No descargar archivos ni instalar aplicaciones. Los estafadores pueden pedir que se descarguen programas que en realidad les están dando acceso al teléfono de la víctima

Una estafa que ha evolucionado. Este fraude comenzó como un SMS y una llamada, pero hoy se dan variantes como la que busca robar información de las tarjetas bancarias mediante el uso de la tecnología NFC del teléfono móvil. Este sistema de comunicación inalámbrica permite compartir información entre otros, tarjetas y móviles, y realizar pagos sin contacto. Los estafadores solicitan a la víctima que se descargue una aplicación maliciosa y que acerque la tarjeta al smartphone. Así, sus datos son enviados a otro teléfono de los atacantes, donde crearán una tarjeta de forma virtual con la que intentar sacar dinero o comprar en comercios.

El teléfono puede parecer auténtico. Los estafadores pueden hacer que en la pantalla del móvil de la víctima figure el mismo número que utiliza el banco para atender a sus clientes o que el SMS aparezca en el mismo hilo que las comunicaciones legítimas mediante una técnica que se conoce como spoofing (que significa suplantación).

Conocen datos personales de su víctima. En muchos casos, disponen de información de su objetivo, como el banco del que es cliente, parte del DNI o la dirección de correo electrónico.

Si ya se ha caído en la estafa. Se debe poner en conocimiento del banco de inmediato para que se puedan adoptar las medidas operativas oportunas. También es muy importante guardar las evidencias, como capturas de pantalla, SMS, correos y registro de llamadas. Presentar una denuncia ante la Policía Nacional o la Guardia Civil.

OTROS CASOS DEL FALSO EMPLEADO DE BANCA

World.title: La Bolsa celebra la firmeza de la Fed: el Ibex avanza un 1% y recupera los 19.800 puntos
World.content:
La subida de tipos de la Reserva Federal y la moderación de los precios de la energía han devuelto el apetito por el riesgo a los mercados. Aunque el endurecimiento monetario suele ser un obstáculo para la renta variable al encarecer el coste de financiación de empresas y hogares y enfriar el crecimiento económico, en esta ocasión los inversores han interpretado la decisión de la Fed como una reafirmación de su compromiso con la lucha contra la inflación. La actuación del banco central estadounidense ha contribuido a reforzar la confianza en que las autoridades monetarias mantendrán el control sobre los precios, mientras que el retroceso de las cotizaciones energéticas ha ayudado a aliviar los temores sobre un nuevo repunte inflacionista. La combinación de ambos factores ha favorecido la vuelta de las compras a unos mercados que llegaban especialmente castigados por las correcciones de los últimos días.

La mejora del sentimiento inversor ha sido generalizada. El Ibex 35 se ha anotado un 1%, en la que es su mejor sesión de la semana. Aunque permanece lejos de los 20.213,6 puntos marcados en agosto, su récord histórico, el selectivo español ha recuperado cerca de 200 puntos en las últimas horas y vuelve a moverse en el entorno de los 19.800.

El comportamiento de la Bolsa española se mantiene en línea con el del resto de mercados europeos. El Dax alemán rebota un 0,8%; el Cac francés, un 0,6%; el Euro Stoxx 50, un 1%, y el FTSE británico, un 1,2%. Los inversores han optado por centrarse en las señales de moderación de la inflación y en la determinación de la Reserva Federal para preservar su credibilidad, relegando a un segundo plano las nuevas amenazas arancelarias lanzadas por la Casa Blanca en respuesta al acercamiento entre Canadá y la Unión Europea.

Wall Street también se ha sumado al rebote. Después de que la sesión anterior estuviera marcada por fuertes ventas en la renta variable mientras la rentabilidad del bono estadounidense se afianzaba por encima del 5%, los inversores han recuperado el apetito por el riesgo y, al cierre de los mercados europeos, el S&P 500 avanza un 1%. Bob Edwards, director de inversiones de Edwards Asset Management, considera que las caídas registradas el miércoles fueron una sobrerreacción. Aunque el futuro de los tipos de interés sigue siendo incierto y los gestores no terminan de ponerse de acuerdo sobre si la Fed volverá a mover las tasas, el experto cree que la mayor claridad mostrada por el banco central está ayudando a reducir uno de los factores que más castigan a los mercados: la incertidumbre. La combinación de una Reserva Federal decidida a contener la inflación y unos precios energéticos menos tensionados está despejando el camino para la recuperación del ánimo inversor.

Las ganancias se extienden al mercado de deuda. Después de semanas de subida incesante de los rendimientos en referencias como la estadounidense marcando niveles no vistos en dos décadas, las subidas se han detenido este jueves. La deuda estadounidense a 10 años baja seis puntos básicos y se apea del 5%. Por su parte, el bono español al mismo plazo baja tres puntos básicos y cae por debajo del 4%. A pesar de esta moderación, los analistas aconsejan prudencia y creen que de momento ha salvado el golpe, pero las amenazas no han desaparecido. Los analistas de ING defienden una “postura bajista sobre los tipos de interés a largo plazo a pesar de la calma posterior a la decisión, ya que un aumento de 25 puntos básicos no modifica sustancialmente la dinámica que los ha perjudicado en los últimos meses. La inflación sigue siendo alta, al igual que el déficit fiscal y la emisión de deuda. Es probable que el rendimiento a 10 años supere el 5% en los próximos días y semanas”, añaden.

La recuperación de los mercados también encuentra apoyo en la relajación de los precios energéticos. El brent, el petróleo de referencia en Europa, prolonga los descensos y cae hasta los 103 dólares por barril después de que mejoraran las perspectivas de suministro en Oriente Próximo. Arabia Saudí trabaja para recuperar aproximadamente la mitad de la capacidad de su estratégico oleoducto Este-Oeste, mientras que las últimas informaciones apuntan a que Riad ha incrementado las ventas de crudo a las refinerías asiáticas para su recogida en puntos situados fuera del estrecho de Ormuz, una de las principales arterias del comercio mundial de energía. La mayor visibilidad sobre los flujos de petróleo ha ayudado a rebajar la tensión en el mercado, aunque los riesgos geopolíticos continúan siendo elevados. “Vemos esta corrección como una oportunidad para comprar en las caídas tanto en crudo como en productos refinados. Los precios han bajado, pero los riesgos subyacentes para la oferta siguen intactos”, señala a Bloomberg Arne Lohmann Rasmussen, analista jefe de Global Risk Management en Copenhague.

La incertidumbre no ha desaparecido, pero la combinación de una Fed creíble y un petróleo menos tensionado vuelve a dar oxígeno a los mercados.

World.title: Jetten refuses to pick a side as opposition warns of drama
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten has declined to say whether his minority coalition will seek support from the left or right to pass its first budget, telling MPs on the second day of debates that making that choice now would be “short-changing the country”.

Instead of committing one way or the other, Jetten said the cabinet would send invitations on Thursday evening to seven opposition parties – Pro, JA21, ChristenUnie, SGP, BBB, Volt and 50PLUS – for a new round of talks on support for the current budget and tax plan.

But the two parties whose votes matter most, which are pulling left and right, have said they see little point in such talks. Opposition party Pro leader Jesse Klaver said more discussions would be a repeat of the ones that collapsed in the summer.

Far-right JA21 leader Joost Eerdmans said the cabinet had to choose. “Broad isn’t going to work,” he told Jetten. “Which way are you going?”

Jetten admitted the cabinet had underestimated how much time it needed in August to work opposition demands into the budget, and said it wanted to keep talking in the coming weeks. He again said a broad agreement was his preference, but did not rule out seeking support for individual budgets if needed.

“A drama for the Netherlands”

Klaver said the coalition is “divided to the bone”, and told Jetten “lock yourself in a room,” because “if you don’t make the choice, it will grind to a halt and this autumn will be a drama for the Netherlands.”

ChristenUnie leader Mirjam Bikker said it was “hard for us to talk” to a cabinet that could not agree with itself.

On the first day of the debates yesterday, Eerdmans said a total deal with the cabinet was no longer realistic and JA21 would judge each departmental budget separately, ruling out support for the climate budget and probably the asylum budget so long as the spreading law for asylum seekers remains in force.

Klaver responded that Pro would withhold support from every budget if the cabinet struck separate deals with JA21. The coalition of D66, VVD and CDA has 66 of the 150 seats in parliament and needs 16 extra votes in the senate.

Siding with Pro would give it the easiest chance of a majority, but the right-wing VVD does not want to concede to them on many issues.

Stabs in the back

PVV leader Geert Wilders opened the day by confronting Jetten with an article in the newspaper AD, in which unnamed ministers criticised the prime minister for failing to take charge, one saying the only direction he took was the visual direction””, managing the image.

Wilders said Jetten’s colleagues had “stuck three daggers in your back” and asked what he thought of not being trusted by his own party.

Jetten said he was proud of his team and “we are making the best of it”.

Tax plans

In mid-November parliament will vote on the tax plan. Pro and ChristenUnie have both said they will not back it as it stands, because the burden falls largely on people in work, and Eerdmans said there is no way the plan can satisfy both JA21 and Pro at the same time.

The Council of State, the government’s main advisory body, said this week that €5.8 billion of the €6 billion in tax rises planned for 2027 would be paid by workers, while the burden on companies and wealth falls slightly. A decision on the tax on savings and investments, known as Box 3, has been postponed until next year.

Jetten said the cabinet would spend an extra €10 billion on infrastructure in the coming years and told Pro that the nitrogen plans would not be watered down, though “improvements” were possible provided they delivered the same reduction in emissions.

MPs will vote on motions, including a motion of no confidence tabled by Wilders, at the end of the debate on Thursday night.

The Dutch public health institute RIVM has announced a fourth death from West Nile virus in the country, after a patient contracted the disease from a blood transfusion.

The authorities do not yet know whether the person, who was already ill, died directly from the virus.

The total number of West Nile cases is now at 28, with ten new patients reported to RIVM in the last week.

Most were infected by mosquitoes. West Nile virus is harmless to the majority of people. Around 20% of those infected develop mild flu-like symptoms.

The elderly and people with health vulnerabilities have the highest risk of death.

The RIVM also reported that since September 10, there have been 30 reports of horses infected with West Nile virus, bringing the total so far this year to 88.

Around 100 cases have also been found in birds.

World.title: FvD refuses to remove racist podcast episode amid outcry
World.content:
An English language podcast broadcast aired by the far-right FvD party’s international arm, Forum & Friends, has sparked an outcry after guests described African people as “pack animals”, discussed racial IQ theories and described Black people as genetically inferior.

The podcast is a weekly show which, like other party operations, is funded through the interior ministry’s subsidy for political parties.

The August 26 episode was hosted by John Laughland, a British party staffer who has run FvD International since 2022 and is a mentor to party founder Thierry Baudet.

Laughland’s guest was British author Simon Elmer, who had posted a series of messages on X about Jason Arday, a Black Cambridge professor who took his own life earlier this year following plagiarism accusations.

Elmer went on to describe the “genetically determined culture and mentality of African people” and said their only use was “to destroy us and breed us out of existence”. He called people from 10 African countries “feeble-minded”. Laughland nodded along and said at the end that it was “hard to disagree” with the analysis.

“Outlandish”

FvD parliamentary leader Ralf Dekker told Volkskrant he had not heard the episode. The podcast gives a platform to voices that “provoke thought”, he said, “and then it can sometimes be outlandish. But if this was said literally, I do not agree with it.” He said there was no reason to remove it: “You should never take anything offline.”

Laughland and the FvD press office have not responded to questions from Volkskrant since Friday.

Léonie de Jonge, a political scientist who researches the far right, told the paper the English-language format was no accident: the podcast is aimed at international far-right networks, not Dutch voters. Anthropologist Amade M’charek said “feeble-minded” is a eugenics term used to justify mass sterilisation in the 20th century.

Earlier episodes have featured guests defending the “great replacement” conspiracy theory, and Laughland himself has spoken of a “horrible cabal” transferring wealth to a small elite, a phrase closely tied to antisemitic conspiracy theories, Volkskrant said.

Laughland, who taught Baudet at Oxford, worked from 2008 to 2015 for a Russian-funded think tank in Paris. Investigative platform Follow the Money reported last year that he spoke at four Russian government-linked conferences between June 2024 and May 2025, with his travel and accommodation paid by his Russian hosts, which the FvD confirmed. He has described Ukraine as “a fiction”.

World.title: Dutch asylum numbers a third lower than a year ago
World.content:
The number of people registering for asylum in the Netherlands has fallen below 600 a week for the first time this year, according to weekly figures from the asylum ministry.

The drop is heavy compared to last year, when for most of autumn 2025 the weekly total was around 1,000, Volkskrant reported on Thursday.

The drop in numbers is mostly down to a reduction in family reunification requests. The number of relatives arriving to join people who already have refugee status has dropped from around 300 a week before the summer to between 110 and 120 a week over the past fortnight.

Syrians

The Netherlands has recorded more than 40,000 asylum-related arrivals every year since 2022. New applications fell sharply after the collapse of the Assad regime in Syria in December 2024, but the total stayed roughly level because Syrians who already had refugee status were still bringing over their families.

A record 16,500 family members arrived in 2025, up 39% on the year before, and three-quarters of them were Syrian, according to statistics agency CBS.

Tighter EU rules on family reunification came into force in June under the European migration pact. The ministry has not yet said what is behind the drop.

Senate

The ministry has only published a breakdown of the weekly figures since late June. Until then its weekly press release was a single line giving one total for new applications, repeat applications, resettlement and family members combined.

Applications are reportedly falling across Europe. The EU asylum agency EUAA said last week that the 27 member states plus Norway and Switzerland received 332,000 applications in the first half of 2026, 17% fewer than a year earlier and the lowest first-half total since 2021.

The agency attributed much of the drop to fewer applications from Venezuelans and Syrians.

World.title: Nearly a quarter of children in NL have divorced parents
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

New research shows that 24% of 15-year-olds have parents who are no longer together, just a slight increase from a decade ago, according to statistics bureau CBS.

In 2025, 3.3 million children were living in the Netherlands. Around 782,000 had parents who are separated.

Twenty years ago, around 13% of 15-year-olds had divorced parents. That number increased steadily, reaching 23% in 2016, when it plateaued.

Most children of separated parents lived with their mother, particularly the youngest: 93% of 4-year-olds, falling to 83% by the age of 17.

Since 1995, the number of children with same-sex parents has also increased. In 1995, around 1,000 children had two legal mothers. By 2025, that number was more than 12,000. There are far fewer children with two legal fathers, just 500 in 2025.

The number of parents who never marry has increased sharply in the last 30 years. In 1995, of 15-year-olds with two legal parents, 80% lived with their married legal parents. Only 1,500 children of that age lived with unmarried parents.

By 2025, that share had fallen to 54.7%.

World.title: Unemployment virtually unchanged in August
World.content:
The unemployment rate remained at 4% in August, the same as July, with around 408,000 people out of work, according to new figures from Dutch statistics bureau CBS.

While the total number of unemployed people in the Netherlands has risen, on average, by around 3,000 per month since June, the number of people leaving the labour force has also increased.

During the same time period, the number of people outside the labour force decreased by an average of 4,000 per month. Retirees and those who are unable to work due to disability or illness make up the majority of the non-labour force.

Since 2023, the number of unemployed people in the Netherlands has been slowly rising. In April, 343,000 were unemployed.

The Dutch unemployment agency UWV registered around 195,000 people on unemployment benefits. That was slightly higher, around 1.4%, than it was in July.

World.title: Netherlands slips again in global gender equality ranking
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Netherlands has fallen three places to 46th out of 145 countries in the World Economic Forum’s Global Gender Gap Index, a year after dropping 15 places to 43rd.

The annual index measures the gap between men and women on economic participation, education, health and political influence.

The Netherlands has closed 75% of its gap, down 0.6 percentage points on last year, according to the University of Amsterdam team that compiled the Dutch data.

There is no longer a gap in education or health and the economic score has risen slightly, but neighbouring countries are moving faster, Henk Volberda, the UvA professor who led the research, told broadcaster NOS.

The main drag is politics: the share of women in parliament rose slightly but the number of women ministers fell, and the country has never had a female prime minister.

“I thought we had hit rock bottom last year,” Volberda said. He argued that nobody in government feels responsible for the issue, which sits with the education ministry, and wants quotas for senior public and corporate posts along with Scandinavian-style free childcare and longer maternity leave.

Iceland tops the ranking, followed by Finland, Norway, Namibia and the UK. Germany is ninth. The Netherlands was in the top 15 almost every year between 2006 and 2016.

World.title: Opposition urge cabinet to pick a route as budget debate begins
World.content:
The left-wing opposition party Pro is willing to talk to the coalition parties about reducing healthcare costs, but only if the cabinet abandons its €6.5 billion cuts to welfare spending, party leader Jesse Klaver said on the first day of the Dutch budget debate.

Klaver said it would be a “scandal” if the government fell over its first budget, but he also pressed Rob Jetten’s administration to make up its mind whether to seek support from left or right.

As the first speaker in the two-day debate on finance minister Eelco Heinen’s budget, Klaver said his party wanted to break the deadlock that led to pre-budget talks breaking down.

“After so much political unrest in recent years, I think it is in all our interests that this cabinet succeeds,” he said. “Sometimes I think the opposition is keener to make it a success than the coalition parties themselves.”

Jan Paternotte, leader of the largest coalition party D66, called on parties on all sides to work on a budget with broad appeal and look beyond “the left-right discussion in The Hague”.

But his words found little support from the opposition, which accused the coalition of D66, CDA and VVD of lacking leadership. “What kind of road map does the cabinet see before it?” Mirjam Bikker, leader of the ChristenUnie, asked.

The three parties have 66 seats in the lower house, 10 short of a majority, while in the Senate they need to find 16 extra votes to pass their legislation.

No perfect match

Pro, with 20 seats in the lower house and 14 senators, provides the most straightforward route, but the right-wing VVD is reluctant to make too many concessions to the left and favours a deal with parties such as JA21 and the orthodox Protestant SGP.

Paternotte said the coalition wanted to continue talking to parties on all sides in the coming weeks. “The perfect political match doesn’t exist, only the will to come to an agreement. My invitation stands.”

Klaver himself came in for criticism from other opposition leaders who said the proposed budget deal had already made too many concessions to the left.

Joost Eerdmans, leader of the hardline conservative JA21, said the cabinet needed to “make the choice” between his party and Pro rather than trying to reach out to both.

In contrast to Pro, JA21 argues the cabinet should cut even more from the welfare bill to create room in the budget for tax cuts and measures to ease the cost of living.

Eerdmans also said plans to invest billions in climate change measures should be redirected to help working families. “The idea that we can change the world’s climate is unrealistic,” he said.

Two budgets

Eerdmans suggested to Paternotte that the cabinet should write two budgets, one for the left-wing parties and one for the right, and let MPs debate them both.

But Paternotte urged Eerdmans to “take off the rose-tinted glasses”. “How does that get you to a majority in the Senate?” he said. “Pro or JA21 on their own aren’t enough.”

Klaver’s pitch to the cabinet also prompted Socialist Party leader Jimmy Dijk to ask how far Pro was willing to compromise on healthcare spending.

Pro would not “work to break things down”, Klaver replied, but he saw potential to make savings by tackling “all kinds of treatments that aren’t necessary” and “taking the market out of youth care”.

Draft published

Paternotte also said D66 was willing to discuss surrogate parenthood with the SGP, which wants the cabinet to block any moves to legalise the practice as a condition for its support.

MPs also voted to ask the cabinet to publish the original draft budget by finance minister Eelco Heinen which was rejected by his coalition partners, prompting an extra weekend of negotiations.

NRC reported that the original version preserved most of the plans to cut welfare spending, despite Pro pressing for them to be taken off the table. In both the draft and the final version Heinen proposed delaying around half the cuts by a year.

Warsaw has launched special joint patrols by its municipal police and roads authority to check whether electric scooters are being parked legally and in keeping with rules introduced under a recent agreement with rental firms. According to the city’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, more than 140 improperly parked scooters have been towed away within just a few days. Under the agreement, their operators now face potential fines. Nie ma miejsca dla hulajnóg tam, gdzie nie ich miejsce. Zdecydowałem o uruchomieniu specjalnych patroli Straży Miejskiej i ZDM. W ciągu ostatnich kliku dni dzięki ich pracy odholowanych zostało ponad 140 nieprawidłowo zaparkowanych hulajnóg elektrycznych. Taką możliwość daje… pic.twitter.com/U5fd7YDN8U — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) September 16, 2026 “There’s no place for scooters where they don’t belong,” Trzaskowski said in a social media post announcing the patrols. “There are specific provisions, agreements and legal regulations – and action is being taken. No leniency.” An agreement reached between the city and three scooter operators – Bolt, Dott and Lime – in May expanded the number of streets where the vehicles are subject to a maximum speed of 12 km/h (7.5 mph) and increased the areas where their use is entirely prohibited. It also introduced measures to prevent scooters from being left in places where parking is illegal. Riding and parking electric scooters was banned in several areas of Warsaw, including popular tourist attractions such as the Old Town, Krasiński Garden and Łazienki Park. Trzaskowski added that the city has now expanded the list of areas covered by the ban, as permitted under the agreement. He did not, however, provide the new list. The agreement requires operators to programme their scooters so they cannot enter areas where riding is prohibited or be parked in places where parking is illegal, including on bridges, in tunnels, in residential areas and on streets where the pavement is too narrow to allow legal parking. Operators can be fined when scooters are left in violation of the rules. The city says that, despite electric scooters accounting for just under 8% of all traffic on cycle lanes, their riders were found to be responsible for 39 of the 66 accidents recorded on cycle lanes last year. Those accidents resulted in 73 injuries. Concerns over the safety of electric scooters have also prompted the national government to introduce stricter rules, including a nationwide requirement for children under 16 to wear a bicycle helmet when riding bicycles and electric scooters, which took effect in early June. Poland first introduced regulations governing electric scooters in 2021, formally setting out rules for their use. Under those rules, scooters are generally required to use cycle lanes where available, with their maximum speed capped at 20 km/h. The Polish government has moved to introduce new rules on the use of electric scooters. E-scooters, which are currently unregulated in Poland, have been blamed for hundreds of accidents annually, with half of victims being pedestrians hit by riders https://t.co/TcrfPQocfr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 3, 2021 Under the nationwide legislation, electric scooters must be parked parallel to the outer edge of the pavement, and municipal authorities have the power to penalise those responsible for improper parking – a provision that primarily affects rental companies. A year after the legislation was introduced, after the first report on e-scooter-related accidents showed that they had caused hundreds of injuries and three deaths in 2021, Poland’s police launched a campaign publicising the new rules. At national level, infrastructure minister Dariusz Klimczak has announced further restrictions the government is working on, including a new law requiring scooters to be collected and left only in specially designated zones. A group of MPs from Poland’s main right-wing and far-right opposition parties have jointly called on the government to organise a march on Polish Independence Day in the Ukrainian city of Lviv, which was historically part of Poland. The idea has been firmly rejected by figures from the ruling coalition, who have called it “gross stupidity” and “madness”. It is also unclear to what extent the leadership of the opposition parties support the proposal. Pomysł zorganizowania "polskiego Marszu Niepodległości ulicami Lwowa" połączył polityków całej prawicy: PiS, Konfederacji, Rozwoju Plus i Konfederacji Korony Polskiej. Odsłaniamy kulisy. Pisze @patrykmichalski, autor programu #NewsMichalskiego ⤵️ 🔵 https://t.co/9L0M5lN0zY pic.twitter.com/1W3YxHdXHT — TVN24+ (@tvn24plus) September 15, 2026 The suggestion was made in a so-called parliamentary interpellation – through which MPs can ask questions and make suggestions to the government – submitted this month and signed by a group of 21 opposition MPs. They called on the government to do more to support the ethnic Polish community that still lives in Lviv, arguing that neither the Polish nor the Ukrainian state does enough to help them preserve and celebrate their identity. By contrast, argued the signatories, Polish state entities provide funding for Ukrainian organisations and events in Poland, including celebrations of Ukrainian Independence Day on 24 August. As such, they called upon the government to “organise official celebrations of [Polish] Independence Day in Lviv, including a Polish Independence March through the streets of the city” on 11 November. This would be “a concrete sign of remembrance and solidarity with Poles living in Ukraine”. Among the 21 signatories, 14 are from the caucus of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s ruling party between 2015 and 2023 and now the largest opposition group. A further three are from Confederation (Konfederacja), a far-right opposition group. One is from Development Plus (Rozwój Plus), a group that broke away from PiS earlier this year; another is from Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), a radical-right, pro-Russian party led by Grzegorz Braun. The final two are an independent, Janusz Kowalski, who recently quit PiS; and Jarosław Sachajko, who was elected in 2023 on the PiS party list but is part of the small Direct Democracy (Demokracja Bezpośrednia) group associated with Paweł Kukiz, a right-wing, anti-establishment figure. Interpelacja do Prezesa Rady Ministrów w sprawie zorganizowania 11 listopada polskiego Marszu Niepodległości ulicami Lwowa 11 listopada Rzeczpospolita Polska obchodzi Narodowe Święto Niepodległości. Jest to święto wszystkich Polaków, również tych, którzy mieszkają poza granicami… pic.twitter.com/7m6yUg1iKZ — Dariusz Matecki (@DariuszMatecki) August 25, 2026 It remains unclear to what extent the MPs have the backing of their parties in calling for the government to organise an Independence Day march in Lviv. Indeed, when Krzysztof Bosak, one of the leaders of Confederation, was asked about the idea on Wednesday, he appeared to know very little about it. Speaking to broadcaster RMF, Bosak said that he had first heard about the proposal on Tuesday and that, after looking into it, he said it appeared to be a “stunt”, and one that he felt was “unnecessary”. “I think the point is to draw attention to the fact that Polish institutions are participating in the celebration of Ukraine’s Independence Day in Warsaw, and that there should be some symmetry,” said Bosak. However, he added that he felt many people would not understand this intention. “The appeal should be directed at Ukrainian institutions, not the Polish foreign ministry,” he said, adding that the MPs who came up with the idea should better explain it. “Frankly, I have more serious matters to attend to.” Czy przemarsz Polaków ulicami Lwowa z okazji Dnia Niepodległości to dobry pomysł? Zdaniem @krzysztofbosak niepotrzebny, a traktować go należy w kategorii happeningu. Ale jeśli się trzymać zasady wzajemności, to już lepiej organizować coś podobnego… w Kijowie. pic.twitter.com/PxdqNKBlCC — Ekonomat (@ekonomat_pl) September 16, 2026 Throughout much of history, Lviv (known in Polish as Lwów) was part of the Polish state, most recently during the period between the First and Second World Wars. However, amid postwar border movements, it became part of Ukraine along with some other former Polish territories. Many in Poland still feel a sense of attachment to the former Polish “borderlands” (kresy) that are now located in Ukraine, Lithuania and Belarus, and which are still home to at least hundreds of thousands of ethnic Poles (though the exact number is a matter of dispute). In Lviv itself, the most recent Ukrainian national census, taken in 2001, showed just under 10,000 people declaring Polish ethnicity in the city (around 1% of the population), though some estimates put the figure higher. Poland's culture minister has condemned Russia's attacks on the historic centre of Lviv in Ukraine, a UNESCO World Heritage site. She noted that Lviv, which was once part of Poland, represents the "shared history of Ukraine, Poland and all of Europe" https://t.co/qPhqXMAZ9r — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 25, 2026 Last year, Confederation’s other main leader, Sławomir Mentzen, clashed with the mayor of Lviv, Andriy Sadovyi, after visiting the city and criticising a monument commemorating nationalist leader Stepan Bandera, a figure seen as a hero by many in Ukraine but regarded as a war criminal in Poland. Followers of Bandera were responsible for the so-called Volhynia massacres during World War Two, in which Ukrainian nationalists massacred around 100,000 ethnic Polish civilians. Poland regards the killings as a genocide but Ukraine rejects that label. The issue has caused renewed tension this year after President Volodymyr Zelensky named a Ukrainian military unit after the “heroes of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army”, which led the massacres. Any Polish attempt at a state-backed Independence Day march in Ukraine would likely stir further controversy. A leading candidate in Poland’s presidential election has clashed with a Ukrainian mayor after visiting his city and criticising the presence of a monument to Stepan Bandera, who is seen as a hero by many in Ukraine but regarded as a war criminal in Poland https://t.co/nA9JzMmBcg — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 26, 2025 Although the Polish government has not yet officially responded to the opposition MPs’ interpellation, a number of figures from the ruling coalition – which ranges from left to centre right – criticised the idea on Wednesday. Deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk called it “gross stupidity” to think of organising such a march in Ukraine, especially at a time of war. He asked how Poles would feel if Germany tried to organise a similar march in Poland (some of whose current territory was part of Germany before World War Two). Both Dariusz Wieczorek, an MP from The Left (Lewica), and Marek Biernacki from the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL) told broadcaster TVN that the idea was “madness”. Próba zorganizowania we Lwowie prawicowej prowokacji z udziałem PiS-u, Rozwój Plus i Brauna to jednoznaczne działanie na rzecz Rosji i przeciwko polskiej racji stanu. — Witold Zembaczyński🇵🇱 (@WZembaczynski) September 16, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers.
